Topic 127608

DC Scale AVI64 card
The AVI64 is a general purpose V/I card that features analog and high-voltage digital
capabilities and is optimized for providing a true universal analog pin, covering a wide
range of test application needs. The card belongs to the DC Scale family and can reside
in any channel card slot.
The card features 64 general purpose channels; each of them capable to force or sink
-40 V to +80 V at ±50 mA and up to ±200 mA at ±10 V. Ganging for higher currents is
supported. AWG, digitizer, digital I/O capabilities, and a time measurement unit (TMU)
are available per channel.
One floating high-current unit with a current of up to ±4 A, one high-resolution voltage
AWG, and one floating differential voltmeter are available per group of 8 channels.

AVI64 safety
WARNING Voltages greater than 60 V DC may be present on this card. Only
trained users are allowed to operate test equipment containing this card. The card
contains a high voltage safety circuit. This must be used in combination with the
DUT board / DUT interface safety circuitry specified below to protect users from
exposure to high voltages.
General safety precautions
The following safety precautions must be observed during all phases of operation,
service and repair of a high voltage power supply card. Failure to comply with these
precautions, or with specific warnings in this manual, violates safety standards and the
intended use of the system. Advantest assumes no liability for the customer's failure to
comply with these requirements.
All safety advice and requirements on the safe handling of DUT boards are applicable to
the Twinning DUT board and the Twinning family board as well.
This is a Safety Class 1 instrument (provided with terminals for protective grounding)
and has been manufactured and tested to international safety standards.
Topic 148737

Operation
WARNING Do not remove isolating covers from the DUT board or the DUT
interface during operation.
High-voltage protection system
A combination of electrical and mechanical protection devices shall be used to protect
users from exposure to high voltages. High voltage power supply cards comprise a
safety circuit. This has to be regarded as part of the entire high-voltage protection
system.
The following devices must be used to fulfill the safety requirements:
All parts of the DUT board must be equipped with isolating covers.
All parts of the DUT interface must be equipped with isolating covers.
Isolating covers that can be removed or opened without the use of tools must be
fitted with a safety interlock.
This safety interlock must be used to control the safety circuit on all high voltage
power supply cards installed in the test system.
WARNING A faulty DUT or DUT board may cause high voltages to be applied
to various parts of the DUT board or DUT interface. To protect users from exposure
to high voltages, all parts of the DUT board and DUT interface shall be equipped
with isolating covers.

in any channel card slot.

Operating modes
DPS operating mode: The channel is typically used for DPS applications to supply
the DUT. The channel is basically programmed using DPS primary sets. The
connection modes NORM, UNGANG, and HIMP are supported. For more information,
refer to AVI64 in DPS operating mode.
To find a summary of all supported resource parameters in the level file, refer to
DPSPINS resources.
PMU operating mode: The channel is typically used for VI applications and is
basically programmed using test methods and APIs. The connection modes for
normal operation and for high impedance voltage measurements are supported.
For more information, refer to AVI64 in PMU operating mode.
Digital I/O operating mode: The channel is typically used for applications that
require a seamless integration of the high voltage, medium power of the AVI64
PMU into digital pattern. The channel is basically programmed using levels, timings,
and digital pattern. For more information, refer to AVI64 in Digital I/O mode.
An AVI64 channel can be configured either for the DPS operating mode or for the other
two operating modes.
Since both the PMU operating mode and Digital I/O operating mode are configured in
the same way, an AVI64 channel can be configured for both modes with different Mode
contexts selected. The two operating modes can be changed on the fly using the AVI64
operating mode crossover.

Additional features
PMU pins P#, PS# and GS# are protected against overload and short circuits
between -44 V and +84 V for an unlimited time and any operating condition.
A Kelvin test unit is available for each channel. The unit can be used to verify that
the force lines and the sense lines are properly connected at the DUT.
The on-board safety circuit, in combination with related hardware and cover of the
DUT board, prevents the users from being exposed to hazardous voltages.
Each of the pins P#, PS# and GS# features a circuit that pulls the pins of a
disconnected channel with a low current to ground.
Profiling with Hardware view is supported for voltage and current measurements
The gain/offset arithmetic processing unit allows you modifying already loaded
force values and waveforms in pattern‑based mode by applying a freely
programmable gain and offset in real‑time.
Smart Ranging minimizes glitches when the force range of an already connected
and active channel is changed.
Smart Mode Switch avoids glitches when the measurement mode of an already
connected and active channel is changed (for example, from force voltage to force
current).
Smart Connect avoids glitches caused by hot switching when connecting a channel
to an already powered-up DUT pin.
Test processor, memory, and data analysis features
Setup and measurement sequences are controlled by test processors. A test
processor features eight cores, each controlling one channel.
The test processor memory is shared between setups, testpoints, waveforms, digital
patterns, and sample data or measurement results.
The memory available per channel for the test program is approximately 107 MB for
a typical setup.
Several alarm flags are available to indicate irregular operating conditions.
Hardware based averaging is available for better accuracy and throughput.
A built-in result analysis is available that checks the measurement data against user
specified test limits.

PMU power budget
The AVI64 card comprises limited power budgets. To prevent any likelihood of an
overpower shutdown, SmarTest limits the overall power usage of an AVI64 card. Warning
flags are set (SmarTest 7) or alarms are generated (SmarTest 8) in case the utilization of a
power budget reaches a critical level. An error message is issued and the involved
channel or channels are disconnected if a power budget is exceeded. The programmed
force or clamp current and the programmed voltage range are used to calculate the
utilization of the available power budgets.
For more information refer to AVI64 power budget.
HV (High-Voltage) protection
The AVI64 card may be connected to low-voltage cards via defective DUTs or
unintentionally closed connections. The card provides enough energy to damage the
low-voltage cards in this case. Therefore, we recommend that you implement a HV
(High-Voltage) protection circuitry on your DUT boards to protect the low-voltage cards.
This will improve the uptime of the test system and the throughput of high-voltage
applications.

AVI64 arbitrary waveform generator (AWG)
An AVI64 pin can be used as an arbitrary waveform generator (AWG), supporting both
voltage and current waveforms.
Topic 148763

An AVI64 channel used in AWG mode is set to the PMU operating mode or to the DPS
operating mode and programmed like a standard PMU or DPS. The usual commands,
APIs or level setups are used to set the initial values for the forced or clamped voltage
or current. The arbitrary waves are defined by DC events and test points, stored into the
pattern memory and applied to the selected front end of the AVI64 channel by the test
processor.
Both, the voltage force or clamp values and the current force or clamp values can be
defined as waveform and therefore may be controlled by the AWG functionality.
Refer to AVI64 AWG specifications for specification data of an AVI64 channel in AWG
mode.
PMU in PMU- and DPS-operating mode
An AVI64 channel in the PMU operating mode or in the DPS operating mode features
the AWG functionality for all force voltage and all force current ranges.
The PMU operating mode supports the AWG for all measurement modes like CFVM and
VFIM.
The measurement mode in the DPS operating mode is limited to the forcing voltage
and clamping current mode.

High‑speed voltage AWG
An AVI64 channel in the PMU operating mode features a high-speed voltage AWG
mode that is programmed in the same way as the normal AWG mode of the PMU but
does not use closed loop control. Unlike the normal AWG mode, that is synchronized to
the 1 MHz clock of the digital closed loop control, the high-speed voltage AWG runs
always synchronous to the pattern sequencer.
The high-speed voltage AWG mode is intended for applications that require high speed,
pattern‑synchronized waveform generation with limited accuracy.
Refer to High-speed voltage AWG in AVI64 AWG specifications for specification data of
an AVI64 PMU in high-speed voltage AWG mode.
The high‑speed voltage AWG is not supported in the DPS operating mode.
Note that when using the high‑speed voltage AWG in combination with the AVI64
gain/offset arithmetic processing unit, you must take into account that the unit adds a
delay of 80 ns, which is required for data processing.
Connections
The output of the high-speed voltage AWG is connected only via the force pin P# or
via the sense pin PS#. The supported connection schemes are
the AVI64 Kelvin connection scheme and
the AVI64 Sense only connection scheme.
Voltage ranges of the high-speed voltage AWG
The high-speed voltage AWG mode features three programmable force voltage
ranges:
±8 V
±30 V
-40 ... +80 V
The voltage drive range can be programmed manually or the best fit range can
automatically be selected based on the set voltage. The ±30 V drive range and the
-40 ... +80 V drive range feature the same resolution of the voltage. For an optimized
utilization of the AVI64 power budget we recommend using the lower drive range if
possible.

The maximum output current of the high-speed voltage AWG is defined as follows:

Measurements
Measurements are also supported in the high-speed voltage AWG mode:
The analog-to-digital converters (ADC) are operating still at a 1 MHz clock that
is not synchronous to the clock of the pattern.
The measure voltage range can be selected independently of the active force
voltage range.
High-resolution voltage AWG
Each group of eight channels features an additional shared high-resolution voltage AWG
for forcing voltages at the DUT. The high-resolution voltage AWG is supported in the
PMU operating mode and replaces the PMU and the floating high-current unit if
connected. The high-resolution AWG uses analog closed loop control and runs
synchronous to the pattern sequencer.

High-current AWG
Each group of eight channels features an additional shared floating high-current unit
that can be set up as high-current AWG. The high-current AWG is supported in the PMU
operating mode and replaces the PMU and the high-resolution voltage AWG if
connected.

High-impedance coherent voltage sampling mode
The PMU features an additional high-impedance voltage sampling mode that disables
the digital closed loop control and allows sampling coherent to the vectors of the digital
pattern.
The sample values of the digitizers are normally taken from the analog-to-digital
converter (ADC) values of the digital closed loop control. The ADCs are synchronized to
the timing of the loop and not with the timing of an AWG pattern. A jitter of 1 µs
between the trigger definitions in the pattern and the trigger of the ADCs must
therefore be accepted in the normal operating mode of the digital control loop.
The high-impedance coherent voltage sampling mode disables the digital closed loop
control and changes the inputs of the ADC to the pattern data that are defined by DC
events.

AVI64 floating differential voltmeter
Each group of eight channels features a floating precision differential voltmeter. The
differential voltmeter can be connected to any combination of channels within the
group. The ground sense referenced operation is also supported. The floating
differential voltmeter takes over the voltage feedback and measurement functionality of
the high-current unit.
Topic 148764

Key characteristics
One floating unit per group of eight channels
Three voltage measurement ranges: ±200 mV, ±1 V, ±8 V
Common mode range: -40 V ... +80 V
Programmable digital filter
The following measurement modes support the differential voltmeter as optional
voltage measure instrument:
"VFVM"
"CFVM"
"IFVM"
"VM_HIZ"
"VFVM_HR"
"IFVM_UNGANGED"
Connections
The differential voltmeter can be connected to any combination of two high sense pins
(PS#) within groups of eight channels. The ground referenced connection to the high
sense pin (PS#) and the ground sense pin (GS#) of a single channel is also supported.
The differential voltmeter does not replace the PMU voltage measure ADC that is
furthermore measuring the output voltage as feedback value for the digital control loop.
Note  As already mentioned, the differential voltmeter does not replace the
continuously connected PMU voltage measure ADC. In 3 V and 10 V voltage range,
the input circuit of the PMU‑ADC clamps the common‑mode voltage to about 15 V.
Therefore, if the common‑mode input voltage at any of the PMUs involved exceeds
the measurement range, the result of the differential voltmeter measurement will be
invalidated, even if the differential voltage is within the set range of the differential
voltmeter.
You must therefore ensure, that the voltage range of the PMUs involved matches or
is greater than the expected common‑mode voltage. This must be done before the
pin is changed to a differential voltmeter measurement or used as reference pin for
a differential voltmeter measurement.
This restriction applies to pins that are in high impedance mode while the
differential voltmeter is connected.

Operation in combination with the floating high-current unit

voltmeter. The floating differential voltmeter takes over the voltage feedback and
measurement functionality of the high-current unit. For more information refer to AVI64
floating high-current unit.

AVI64 channels feature programmable anti-aliasing, low-pass measurement filters for all

Voltage feedback and measurement
Operating the floating high-current unit additionally requires the floating differential

measurement functionality of the high-current unit. For more information refer to AVI64
floating differential voltmeter.

Pulsed operation
The floating high-current unit is designed for pulsed operation. The duration of the
pulse is limited to some milliseconds and a maximum duty cycle must be considered for
recharging the on-board energy storage in disconnected state.
For the relationship between the current, the voltage at the DUT, and the maximum
pulse length refer to
AVI64 HCU pulse width vs. load current - 100 mΩ DUT board resistance or
AVI64 HCU pulse width vs. load current - 1000 mΩ DUT board resistance.
Offline power analyzer for pulsed operation
Advantest provides a spreadsheet that helps you verifying that the combination of the
required DUT voltage and current, the resistance of the DUT board traces, and the
required pulse length match the capabilities of a fully charged high current unit.
To download the power analyzer, click the link below:
AVI64_HCU_PowerAnalyst.xlsx

Maximum duty cycle
A maximum value of the duty cycle must be considered to allow the unit to recharge the
on-board energy storage in disconnected state.
The duty cycle is the ratio of time when the floating high-current unit sources or sinks
the current and the time when the unit is disconnected. For example a current pulse of 1
ms followed by 19 ms in the disconnected mode results in 5.0 % duty cycle.
The following restrictions and rules are to be respected:
The maximum average duty cycle of the floating high-current unit is 10 % for a
current of 4 A.
The maximum duty cycle is higher than 10 % for currents lower than 4 A.
The continuous operation is not supported.
A maximum accumulated pulse length before the energy storage must be
recharged is to be respected. For more information refer to paragraph "Pulsed
operation" above.
The actual output current must be considered for the calculation of the duty cycle.
The duty cycle is to be considered separately for sourcing and sinking currents.
The following diagram shows an example for a single 4 A current pulse in combination
with a disconnect time of 5 ms:
The duty cycle is to be calculated from the 0.5 ms of the current pulse and the sum of
the current pulse time and the disconnected time. The duty cycle for the diagram above
is therefore 0.5 ms / (0.5 ms + 5 ms) = 9.1 %.
The next diagram shows an example for a 4 A current pulse, followed by a 1 A current
pulse and a disconnect time of 5 ms:

The combination of the two current pulses and the 5 ms disconnect time results in a
duty cycle of 13 %. The maximum duty cycle of 10 % is valid for a 4 A pulse. The 1 A
current pulse must therefore be normalized to 4 A for the calculation: ¼ of the 1 A pulse
time is to be considered for the calculation of the duty cycle.
The time where the floating high-current unit is disconnected in the example above
must be changed from 5 ms to minimum 6.75 ms to comply with the maximum duty
cycle of the unit.
Charging of the energy storage
The floating high-current unit is supplied by an also floating on-board energy storage.
This floating energy storage must be charged before the high-current unit can be used.
The unit features a flag that indicates the charging status of the energy storage. We
recommend checking the status before the floating high-current unit is connected to a
channel.
Refer to AVI64 floating high-current unit programming overview and to AVI64 status
flags for more information.
Charging of the energy storage is initiated automatically if the required power from the
combined ±10 V (±3 V) power budget is available. Charging is initiated only if the
floating high-current unit is disconnected from all eight channels of the group.
Unusual operating conditions like a damaged DUT may totally discharge the energy
storage. The required time to charge the totally discharged energy storage is in the
range from 32 ms to 130 ms.
CAUTION The floating high-current unit must be disconnected from all eight
channels to charge the energy storage.
Note  The floating high-current unit supports an unlimited idle time in connected
state. The idle time in connected state need must not be considered for the duty
cycle calculation. The "idle time in connected state" means that no output current is
flowing.
AWG and DGT
The floating high-current units feature an arbitrary waveform generator (AWG) and
digitizer (DGT) like the PMU. Both, the AWG functionality and the DGT functionality are
defined and controlled by DC events and test points that are stored in the pattern
memory and applied by the pattern sequencer.

Refer to AVI64 arbitrary waveform generator (AWG) for more information regarding the
AWG and refer to AVI64 digitizer (DGT) for more information regarding the DGT.

Application note
State of the high-current unit
The floating high-current unit is supplied by an also floating on-board energy
storage. This energy storage must be charged when the unit is disconnected from all
pins. Charging of the energy storage requires some current from the related power
budgets and needs some time. In addition, the energy storage will provide only a
limited amount of energy for the current pulse.
Therefore, we recommend checking the status of the high-current unit for each
pulse. Several solutions are available to check the state:
The flag Battery full indicates the load state of the energy storage. This flag
should be checked before the high-current is connected to a channel.
The latched Low Headroom flag is set if the stored energy is not sufficient for
the programmed pulse and the high-current unit has entered an unregulated
state.
An API based solution is to measure not only the target value for the test but
also the forced value to verify that the condition for the high-current test has
been applied correctly.
Refer to AVI64 floating high-current unit programming overview and to AVI64 status
flags for more information.

AVI64 gain/offset arithmetic processing unit
The gain/offset arithmetic processing unit (APU) allows you modifying already loaded
force values and waveforms in pattern‑based mode by applying a freely programmable
gain and offset in real‑time. Single values and waveforms can therefore be reused with a
different amplitude and offset without reloading them into the memory.
The basic idea behind the gain/offset APU is that force values for dynamic DC tests,
which are generated as DC events and stored in the memory as testpoints, are modified
by the gain/offset APU when the corresponding pattern is executed. The gain/offset
APU modifies the received force values of the testpoints with two user‑defined, freely
programmable values for gain and offset. The modified force values are then passed on
to the front‑end.
For the AWG mode use case, waves (but also individual test points) can be reused with
different amplitudes and offsets or levels, which leads to a significant reduction in the
consumed memory.
Gain/offset APU features
The gain/offset APU is available per AVI64 channel and is supported only for AVI64 pins
in PMU operating mode and the pattern‑based mode.
The following values of DC events or testpoints can be processed by the gain/offset
APU:
Voltage force values
Current force values
The following units and modes are supported:
PMU in normal mode
PMU forcing voltage in High‑speed voltage AWG mode
High-resolution voltage AWG
Floating high-current unit (HCU)
The X4 mode
Note  The gain/offset APU is designed in such a way that setting and activation of a
user‑defined gain and offset does not automatically modify the force value:
The currently set force value must be explicitly changed or reapplied in order to
apply the change in offset and gain to the output stage.

AVI64 high-resolution voltage AWG
A high-resolution voltage AWG is available per group of eight channels. The ground
referenced high-resolution voltage AWG is designed for optimized AC performance and
replaces the PMU and the AWG functionality of the PMU when connected to a channel.
Key characteristics
One floating unit per group of eight channels
Two force voltage ranges: ±4 V and ±8 V
Maximum current: 20 mA
Ground sense range: ±0.5 V
Operation principle
The AWG functionality is defined and controlled by pattern sequencer DC events. The
high-resolution voltage AWG uses the same pattern memory as the channel where it is
connected. The controller of the output buffer and the voltage feedback utilize pure
analog circuitry for optimized AC performance.
For specification data, refer to table High-resolution voltage AWG in AVI64 AWG
specifications.
Connections
The high-resolution voltage AWG features Kelvin connections. The shared output can be
connected to P# and PS# pins of any channel within the group of eight channels. The
ground reference is connected to the GS# pin of the used channel.
The return pin of the high-resolution voltage AWG is the common ground (GND) of the
card.

discrete settings:

AVI64 Kelvin test unit
The AVI64 card features a Kelvin test unit, also known as sense-connection test unit. The
Kelvin test unit is available per channel for the P# to PS# connection and for the GND to
GS# connection.
Topic 148867

Kelvin test means that the connection from the force lines to the sense lines on the DUT
board or at the DUT pins is verified with a small test current applied. A PASS/FAIL result
is returned.
The Kelvin test unit applies the small test current to the tested force to sense (FS)
connection and measures the voltage drop between the two lines. The measured
voltage is used as criterion for the pass/fail decision and should be near 0.0 V for a good
FS connection.
The Kelvin test unit is available in the PMU operating mode and in the DPS operating
mode.
Note  The purpose of the Kelvin test unit is to ensure that when the DUT is
contacted, the high-impedance sense line is connected to the force line at the DUT
with a sufficiently low contact resistance. Due to the high input impedance of the
sense lines, the fixed threshold of some kilo-Ohms will be sufficiently low.
The Kelvin test unit is the only resource that can perform a reliable sense connection
test on the ground sense line with a defined test current applied.
Since connections and hardware on the DUT board can sabotage the test of the
sense connections, we recommend that you check the functionality of the test
without DUT and with open sense connections. All tested sense connections must
fail in this verification.
CAUTION The AVI64 PMU forces the test current via one of the tested lines, the
FS connection, and via the other tested line to ground. For the sense connection
test, one of the lines may be internally connected to ground. Therefore, the DUT
must be powered down before the Kelvin test (or sense connection test) is started in
disconnected mode.
Basic data of the AVI64 Kelvin test unit:
The Kelvin test unit is available per channel.
The threshold for the pass/fail decision is about 5 kΩ.
The test current is about 100 µA.
The maximum capacitance between the force lines and the corresponding sense
lines is 5 nF.
The set up and set down of the test is performed in parallel on all selected pins.
Three measurements are serially performed for the P# pin, the PS# pin and the GS#
pin.

Testing eight AVI64 pins requires a test time of about 10 ms per site.
The test can be performed only in the disconnected state of the selected pins.

Operating principle
The test is divided into two sub-tests for the P# and PS# pin and for the GS# pin. The
measurements are performed serially on the pins.
Note that the internal connections used for the tests described below are accessible
only through the Kelvin test unit. The results of the tests are available only as PASS/FAIL
results.
Although the AVI64 supports reverse Kelvin connections or can apply a test current via
the sense line, only the Kelvin test unit can correctly apply the test current as shown
below. This is especially true for high-impedance DUT pins or the test of the DUT
ground sense connection.
As a reminder, a high-impedance voltage measurement on a sense line can return a
random value if there is only a high-impedance connection to the force line. A reliable
sense connection test is only possible if a defined test current flows through the tested
connection.
DUT force and sense test
The test is divided into two measurements:
P#: The test current is applied to the high force pin (P#). The sense pin (PS#) is
internally connected to ground. The voltage drop from the high force pin via the
FS connection at the DUT to the sense pin is measured and judged.
PS#: The test current is applied to the high sense pin (PS#). The force output
(P#) is internally connected to ground. The voltage drop from the high sense pin
via the FS connection at the DUT to the force output pin is measured and
judged.
DUT ground sense test
The test current is forced at the ground sense pin (GS#). The voltage drop from the
ground sense pin via the FS connection at the DUT to ground is measured and
judged.

AVI64 safety circuit
The card includes an on-board safety circuit to protect users from exposure to
hazardous voltages.
WARNING Voltages greater than 60 V DC may be present on this card. Refer to
AVI64 safety for more information.
On-board safety circuit
The on-board safety circuit limits the PMU peak output voltage to about ±35 V if the
circuit is not activated by an external control voltage. The AVI64 card will operate
without restrictions up to ±30 V in any force voltage range and any force current range
regardless if the safety circuit is activated or not. The card features a flag that indicates
the state of the on-board safety circuit.
Topic 148752

Behavior with disabled safety circuit
The AVI64 card behaves as follows if the safety circuit is not enabled and a force voltage
or clamp voltage outside a range from -30 V to +30 V is programmed for minimum one
channel:
All programmed force voltages or clamp voltages outside a range from -30 V to
+30 V are limited to ±30 V.
The PMU supply voltage of the related channels is reduced to about ±35 V that is
the normal supply voltage for the ±30 V force voltage range.
The force and measure voltage range of the related channels is not changed. The
resolution of the forced, clamped, or measured voltage is still the resolution of the
-40 V ... +80 V range.
The Safety line flag is set.
The flag is set only for the channels that are programmed to a voltage outside a
range from -30 V to +30 V. The flag is not set for channels that are programmed to
a voltage within the range from -30 V to +30 V.
An error message is shown in the report window and in the console window with
the next access to the card.
Therefore, the channels that have been connected and are set to a force voltage or
clamp voltage outside a range from -30 V to +30 V are still active and remain connected
but the forced or clamped voltage is limited to ±30 V.
Behavior with enabled safety circuit
The AVI64 card behaves as follows if the safety circuit is enabled and a force voltage or
clamp voltage outside a range from -30 V to +30 V is programmed for minimum one
channel:
The PMU supply voltage of the related channels is restored to the normal supply
voltage for the -40 V ... +80 V force voltage range.
All programmed force voltages that has been limited to ±30 V are restored to the
programmed value.
The software has to read and clear the safety alarm after the safety circuit has been
enabled again but no more actions are required.
CAUTION The original voltage settings of the channels are restored
automatically as soon as the safety circuit is enabled.

In addition, a disabled safety
circuit does not disconnect the related channels but limits the voltage to ±30 V. As a
result, channels that are operating in the -40 V ... +80 V force voltage range
immediately output the programmed force or clamp voltage.

On-board hardware and required DUT board circuitry
To enable the AVI64 for operation at voltages above ±30 V connect a control voltage of
+5.0 V DC from an adequate power supply to the pogo pins SAFETY_P and SAFETY_N.
The supply must be applied via a safety interlock that is open when the DUT board
cover or the DUT interface cover is open.
Status flag
The AVI64 card will operate without restrictions up to ±30 V regardless of the state of
the safety circuit.
The card does not check the state of the safety circuit if all channels are programmed to
force voltages or clamp voltages within a range from -30 V to +30 V and will therefore
not update the related flag.
The Safety line flag is set only for the channels that are programmed to a voltage
outside a range from -30 V to +30 V if the safety circuit is disabled. The flag is not set
for channels that are programmed to a voltage within the range from -30 V to +30 V.
Application note
Checking the state of the safety circuit
The APIs DPS_AUX_PIN_TASK.checkPowerFlags() and DPS_AUX_TASK.getSafetyLine()
can be used to read the state of the safety circuit. The APIs return a reasonable value
only if minimum one AVI64 channel is programmed to a force voltage or clamp
voltage outside a range from -30 V to +30 V. The state of the safety circuit is ignored
if all channels are set to voltages within this range.

AVI64 surge tracker
The AVI64 features a surge tracker per channel that monitors the voltage between the
high sense (PS#) and ground sense (GS#) pins or the output current of the PMU or the
output current of the floating high-current unit.
The surge tracker is available in the PMU operating mode and in the DPS operating
mode.
Once the surge tracker is turned on, it monitors the voltage or current unless being
turned off. In a typical use scenario the surge tracker is activated in the very beginning
of a testflow and the status is checked at the end of the testflow.
The surge tracker checks against both high (positive) and low (negative) voltage or
current thresholds, which can be set individually. Two flags indicate if thresholds have
been exceeded. These flags are latched (stored) and can be retrieved any time in the
testflow.
Refer to AVI64 other specifications for specification data of the surge tracker. The
detectable pulse width is defined by the used comparators. Refer to the Digital compare
(high-speed mode) and Digital compare (high-resolution mode) specifications in AVI64
digital driver, comparator, and TMU specifications for more information.
Voltage surge tracker
The surge tracker in voltage sensing mode uses the high-speed comparator as input for
an optimized detection speed.
Current surge tracker
The surge tracker in current sensing mode uses the current measurement values of the
digital control loop as input:
The effective maximum and minimum thresholds are limited by the actual current
measurement range.
SmarTest supports programming the thresholds to values outside of the actual
current measurement range.
Therefore, the same thresholds can be maintained over a complete test suite or testflow
but the effective thresholds are always truncated to the actual current measurement
range.
Topic 149134

Application notes
TMU and surge tracker
The TMU (Time measurement unit) and the surge tracker cannot be used in parallel.
The two functionalities use the same comparators that can be assigned to only one
of them at the same time.
Surge tracker is silently disabled in temporarily unganged mode
Note that on AVI64, DPS128/64, and FVI16 you cannot execute a current compare on
a ganged group of channels if the group is in unganged mode. Already activated
comparators are silently disabled in unganged mode. A user notification (Error or
warning) is omitted in this case, to avoid any interrupt in the testflow. The previous
state of the comparators is automatically restored after the ganged group has been
restored.

AVI64 time measurement unit (TMU)
The AVI64 card features a time measurement unit (TMU) per channel that is available in
the PMU operating mode and in the Digital I/O operating mode.
The TMU allows you to accurately measure frequency, period length, pulse width, rise
and fall times, edge times, jitter and propagation delay (skew) of periodic and non-
periodic output signals.
The TMU measures the time elapsed between the arming (activation of the TMU) and
the occurrence of a certain event. Events are defined by a slope (rising or falling edge) of
the DUT signal, and by a threshold. The event occurs at every rising or falling slope of
the DUT signal when the threshold is crossed.
An upgrade license is required both for TMU measurements in the Digital I/O operating
mode and in the PMU operating mode. For more information, refer to Licensing in
AVI64 specific setup tasks.
Topic 148837

TMU characteristics
The following items must be considered when using the TMU:
The TMU is supported in the PMU operating mode and in the Digital I/O operating
mode.
The TMU is not supported in the DPS operating mode.
For ganged pins, the time measurement unit (TMU) is supported but only the
high‑speed voltage comparator and the high‑resolution voltage comparator of the
PMU can be used. The measurement is performed on the master channel. The
high‑resolution current comparator of the PMU and the comparators of the shared
resources are not supported.
The default connection set must be used for TMU measurements.
The TMU uses features that are designed for digital pins. Therefore, the DC Scale
specific connection sets cannot be used. TMU measurements can be applied only
on pins defined in the default connection set.
For more information regarding the default connection set refer to Digital Pins
editor and DFPN, DFPN?.

TMU block diagram
The following drawing highlights the complete TMU structure in the AVI64 block
diagram.

TMU front end
The TMU input signal is derived from the voltage at the PS# pin or the output current of
the PMU or the floating high-current unit. The TMU features the high-speed voltage
comparator and high-resolution comparators. All comparators are window comparators
with two programmable thresholds.
High‑speed voltage comparator
The channel compares the DUT output voltage with high bandwidth and tracking
slew rate against VOL and VOH thresholds. The threshold voltages are referenced to
the channel specific ground sense pin GS#. The high-speed comparator features
also a differential compare and termination mode for adjacent channels.
Two voltage ranges are available for the high-speed comparator:
±8 V
-40 ... +80 V
Several termination modes are available to adapt the comparator input to the
needs of the DUT outputs:
No termination.
50 Ω single ended termination to ground.
100 Ω termination to the adjacent channel in combination with differential
compare.
Termination by the driver: VIL, VIH and VT.
The Digital I/O mode supports also active pull down circuits that pull the
output pins with a low current to ground.
The voltage in the single ended 50 Ω termination mode is limited to maximum ±3.5
V. The voltage in the differential compare and termination mode is limited to
maximum ±7 V. The termination is disconnected if these limitations are violated.
The threshold voltages are referenced to the mid voltage of the two channels if the
differential compare and termination mode is used. The differential compare and
termination mode is supported for the channel combination 1‑3, 2‑4, 5‑7, and 6‑8
within a group of eight channels. Refer to AVI64 channel group and differential
compare assignment for a complete table of the supported channel combinations.
The high-speed comparator features a switchable hysteresis of about 25 mV.
High-resolution comparators of the PMU
The channel compares the DUT voltage or current with the full PMU single shot
accuracy and limited bandwidth against the two thresholds:

Voltage compare: The threshold voltages are referenced to the voltage that is
measured differentially between the high sense pin PS# and the channel
specific ground sense pin GS#. This compare mode supports all voltage
measurement ranges of the PMU. The voltage measurement range can be set
independently of the digital drive range.
Current compare: The channel compares the DUT output current with full
PMU single shot accuracy and limited bandwidth against ICL and ICH
thresholds. The current measurement range is fixed at ±200 mA in the Digital
I/O operating mode. All current measurement ranges are supported in the
PMU operating mode.
The sample frequency of the high-resolution comparators is defined by the sample
frequency of the voltage and current measurement and is 1 MHz. Interpolation
between two samples provides an optimized resolution of 5 ns.
High-resolution comparators of the shared resources
The channel compares the DUT voltage or current with the full single shot accuracy
of the shared resource and limited bandwidth against the two thresholds:
Voltage compare: The threshold voltages are referenced to the voltage that is
measured differentially between the high sense pin PS# and the channel
specific ground sense pin GS# or between the PS# pins of two channels.
Current compare: The channel compares the DUT output current with the full
single shot accuracy of the floating high-current unit and limited bandwidth
against ICL and ICH thresholds.
The high-resolution comparators of the shared resources support all voltage or
current measurement ranges of the used ADCs.
The following high-resolution comparators are available for the shared resources:
Voltage measurement of the shared floating differential voltmeter
Current measurement of the shared floating high-current unit
The floating differential voltmeter takes also over the voltage measurement for the
floating high-current unit and can be defined as comparator input in this
functionality.
Note  The connection to the high-speed voltage comparator is not supported for
the force only connection scheme of the PMU operating mode.

Hysteresis and sample frequency of the high resolution
comparators
The high-resolution comparators feature a programmable hysteresis that is defined in
percent of the measurement range. Half of the resulting value is symmetrically applied
to the programmed thresholds:
A programmed threshold of 15 V and 1 % hysteresis in the ±30 V range results in a
difference of 0.3 V.
The effective thresholds are
15.15 V for the rising edge and
14.85 V for the falling edge.
A programmed threshold of -2.0 mA and 2 % hysteresis in the ±5 mA range results
in a difference of 0.1 mA.
The effective thresholds are
-1.95 mA for the rising edge and
-2.05 mA for the falling edge.
A programmed threshold of 50 V and 3 % hysteresis in the -40 ... +80 V range
results in a difference of 2.4 V.
The effective thresholds are
51.2 V for the rising edge and
48.8 V for the falling edge.
The hysteresis calculation for the -40 ... +80 V range uses always 80 V as range
regardless of the polarity of the threshold.
The sample frequency of the ADCs used for the high-resolution comparators is 1 MHz.
Interpolation between two samples provides an optimized resolution of 5 ns.

Measurement filters
AVI64 channels feature programmable anti-aliasing, low-pass measurement filters for all
ADCs:
Voltage measurement ADC and current measurement ADC of the PMU
Voltage measurement ADC and current measurement ADC of the floating high-
current unit
Voltage measurement ADC of the floating differential voltmeter
Measurement filter characteristics
Minimum cutoff frequency: 10 Hz
Maximum cutoff frequency: 250 kHz
Default cutoff frequency: 250 kHz
The dynamic behavior of the force output is independent of the measurement filters.
Note  The high-resolution comparators of the TMU utilize the continuous data
stream of the ADCs. The measurement filter setting has therefore also an effect on
the TMU measurements.
For high-speed TMU measurements using the high-resolution comparators, we
therefore recommend setting the measurement filter to the maximum value.
TMU in PMU operating mode
The basic set up of the TMU in the PMU operating mode of the channel is to be done by
APIs in a test method. TMU measurements are armed and controlled by DC events in a
pattern.
The TMU of an AVI64 channel in the PMU operating mode supports all ranges and
terminations modes of the high-speed comparator and the high-resolution comparators
of the PMU and the shared resources as defined above.
The TMU of an AVI64 channel in the PMU operating mode features an additional sample
number filter and a measurement mode filter. The measurement mode filters and
combines both the comparator events from the high comparator and the comparator
events from the low comparator. The TMU therefore supports single shot rise and fall
time measurements.

TMU in Digital I/O operating mode
The basic setup of a TMU in the Digital I/O operating mode of a channel is to be done in
the level setup. The TMU uses the same comparators as the digital compare
functionality. The TMU thresholds are defined by compare levels.
The TMU measurements are started by executing special arming waveforms in a pattern.
The TMU of an AVI64 channel in the Digital I/O operating mode supports all ranges and
terminations modes of the high-speed comparator and the high-resolution comparators
of the PMU. All voltage measurement ranges are supported by the high-resolution
voltage comparator but the high-resolution current comparator uses a fixed range of
200 mA. The high-resolution comparators of the shared resources are not supported in
this operating mode.
The TMU of an AVI64 channel in the Digital I/O operating mode is assigned to the
output of the high comparator. The TMU depends therefore on the VOH level. We
recommend setting both the VOH and the VOL threshold to the same value due to
compatibility with other cards.

Specific design rules must be followed when designing a new DUT board and assigning
AVI64 channels:

Introduced in SmarTest 7.4.0
AVI64 operating modes
The AVI64 channels feature the PMU operating mode, the DPS operating mode, and the
Digital I/O operating mode.
The AVI64 operating mode is defined by the pin type that has been selected in the Pin
setting editors. The operating mode can be set individually for each channel of the card.
The combination of the operating mode and the selected connection state defines the
characteristics, the dynamic behavior, and the basic programming mode of the channels.
Digital I/O operating mode
An AVI64 channel is configured for the Digital I/O operating mode if the channel is
defined as digital "i", "o", or "io" pin using the Digital Pins editor. In Digital I/O operating
mode, the AVI64 channel is used like a standard digital pin. An AVI64 channel in Digital
I/O mode is controlled using levels, timings, and digital pattern.
Topic 148766

PMU operating mode
An AVI64 channel is configured for the PMU operating mode if the channel is defined as
DC Scale pin using the Digital Pins editor. In PMU operating mode, the channel is used
like a standard PMU to temporarily supply power during the execution of a single test
suite or a group of test suites. An AVI64 channel in PMU operating mode is
programmed using test method APIs. The connection state is also set by test method
APIs.
DPS operating mode
An AVI64 channel is configured to operate in DPS mode if it is defined as a device power
supply using the DPS Pins editor. In DPS mode, the channel behaves like a DPS-slot
device power supply and is normally used to supply devices with power during the
execution of a testflow. An AVI64 channel in DPS operating mode takes part in the
standard connect and disconnect sequences and is programmed using DPS primary
sets.

provides a positive or negative voltage up to the programmed clamp current and is
programmed using DPS primary sets. Programming an AVI64 channel by DC events is
also supported.
Features:
An AVI64 channel in DPS operating mode supports the PMU functionality including
the AWG and DGT mode.
An AVI64 channel in DPS operating mode does not support
the shared resources "Floating differential voltmeter", "Floating high-current
unit", and "High-resolution voltage AWG"
"ganging on the fly" and the "Time measurement unit (TMU)".

AVI64 in PMU operating mode
In PMU operating mode, an AVI64 channel is used like a standard PMU to temporarily
supply power during the execution of a single test suite or a group of test suites.
Configuration
An AVI64 channel is configured for the PMU operating mode if the channel is defined as
a DC Scale pin using the Digital Pins editor. Both, the AVI64 channel in PMU operating
mode and in the Digital I/O operating mode are defined in the digital pins editor. The
context definition, the type, and the mode are used to differentiate between the two
operating modes.

Glitchless operating mode crossover
The AVI64 pins support the glitchless operating mode crossover from the PMU
operating mode to the Digital I/O operating mode and vice versa without disconnecting
the pins. Refer to AVI64 operating mode crossover for more information.
Characteristics
An AVI64 channel in PMU operating mode is typically used for VI applications. The
channel provides a positive or negative voltage or current up to the programmed clamp
current or voltage and is basically programmed using test methods and APIs.
The static and dynamic behavior is defined by a combination of the connection state,
the measurement mode, and the execution mode as described below. For more
information refer to the AVI64 programming - PMU operating mode.
Connection state
The connection state defines the behavior of the channel when it is configured for the
PMU operating mode. For more information, refer to SPMU_PIN_TASK.connectState().
The following forcing connection states are supported:

"NORMAL" Kelvin connection
 The force output is connected to the DUT via the P# pogo pin. The
sense input is connected to the DUT via the PS# pogo pin.
The two pogo pins P# and PS# must be connected together on the
DUT board or directly at the DUT so that the digital closed loop
control is able to compensate the voltage drop on the P# line.
This is the default state.
For more information, refer to AVI64 Kelvin connection.
"KELVIN_REVERSE" Reverse Kelvin
connection
The sense input is connected to the DUT via the P# pogo pin. The
force output is connected to the DUT via the PS# pogo pin.
The two pogo pins P# and PS# must be connected together on the
DUT board or directly at the DUT so that the digital closed loop
control is able to compensate the voltage drop on the P# line.
The maximum current is limited to 50 mA in this mode. The
connection to the shared resources (Floating high-current unit,
floating differential voltmeter, high-resolution voltage AWG) is not
supported.
For more information, refer to AVI64 reverse Kelvin connection.
"SENSE_ONLY" Sense only connection
 Both the force output and the sense input are connected to the
DUT only via the PS# pogo pin.
Only the PS# pogo pin must be connected to the DUT.
This mode minimizes the capacitive load at the DUT pin if the P#
pogo pin is not connected to the DUT. The maximum current is
limited to 50 mA in this mode.
For more information, refer to AVI64 Sense only connection.
"FORCE_ONLY" Force only connection
 Both the force output and the sense input are connected to the
DUT only via the P# pogo pin.
Only the P# pogo pin must be connected to the DUT.
The connection to the shared resources (Floating high-current unit,
floating differential voltmeter, high-resolution voltage AWG) and to
the high-speed voltage comparator is not supported.
For more information, refer to AVI64 Force only connection.

For more information, refer to AVI64 Force only connection.
"VM_HIZ"
"VM_HIZ_COH"
High impedance
connection
The sense input is connected to the DUT via the PS# pogo pin. The
force output is not connected to the DUT.
The high impedance connection is set by API
SPMU_PIN_TASK.mode().
The preferred DUT board connection scheme for the high
impedance connection is the Sense only scheme.
The high impedance connection is also supported for the Kelvin
and reverse Kelvin DUT board connection schemes. A higher input
leakage current and input capacitance is to be considered for these
schemes. For more information, refer to Interface characteristics in
AVI64 other specifications and to Combination of the Sense only
connection and the Kelvin connection.

Measurement mode
The measurement mode defines the force mode and the measurement mode of the
channel when it is configured for the PMU operating mode. For more information and a
list of all supported measurement modes, refer to AVI64 programming - PMU operating
mode.
Execution mode
The execution mode defines the measurement behavior of the channel when it is
configured for the PMU operating mode. For more information refer to
SPMU_PIN_TASK.execMode().
The following execution modes are supported:
"SER": Serial measurements are performed per device, but in multisite tests
multiple sites are tested in parallel whenever possible.
"PAR": Parallel measurements are performed per device and on all sites whenever
possible.
Connecting and disconnecting channels in PMU operating
mode
An AVI64 channel in PMU operating mode does not take part in standard connect and
disconnect sequences and cannot take part in the set activation, although the channel
can be added to user-defined connect and disconnect sequences.
Unlike other DC Scale cards in DPS operating mode, an AVI64 channel in PMU operating
mode needs not to be disconnected for changing the force voltage range or the force
current range. AVI64 supports changing the force voltage range and the force current
range in connected state both for the DPS operating mode and for the PMU operating
mode.

Timing relationship of AVI64 DC events
DC events are fully synchronized to digital pattern but processing of the event data
causes some delay times.
The following basic characteristics are to be considered for programming AVI64 DC
events:
A DC event requires always 32 vectors.
Programming of overlapping DC events is not supported.
Setup commands like the force value, the clamp value, or the forcing mode are
always sent first in the 32 vector block.
Measure commands are always sent last in the 32 vector block.
Processing of the DC events in the front-end adds an additional delay time.
The availability of the measured values depends on the sample mode (coherent or
non-coherent) and the programmed averaging. A measure event defines only the
trigger of the measurement.
Dummy vectors may be required at the end of a pattern to ensure that the
communication between the test processor and the front-end is running until
sampling, data processing, and the data transfer has been finished for the last
measure event.
The following table shows the delay time that is caused by the data transfer to the front-
end and by synchronization to the free running sample clock and the internal clock of
the digital control loop. The table shows the delay of DC events with respect to the
begin of the first event vector in the pattern. The table defines the delay time where the
receiving device like a DAC or ADC of the front-end receives the trigger for changing the
output value or starting sampling. The analog settling time is not covered.
DC event delay of AVI64
Function Delay time
Set voltage or current (Force or clamp) 8 vectors + (0.1 ... 1.11) µs
Set force mode (Voltage or current) 8 vectors + (0.1 ... 1.11) µs
Set range 8 vectors + (0.1 ... 1.11) µs
High-speed voltage AWG, set voltage 41 vectors
High-resolution voltage AWG, set voltage 9 vectors + 1.5 µs / vector period
Sampling non-coherent 32 vectors + (-0.9 ... 0.11) µs
Sampling coherent 47 vectors
Some notes on the table above:

The delay time is referenced to the begin of the first vector of the DC event (T0 in
the drawing below).
Non-coherent sampling utilizes the measured values that are already available for
the digital control loop. The effective ADC trigger may be therefore up to 0.9 µs
before the end of the last vector.
Coherent sampling requires some more vectors for setting up the ADC.

AVI64 in Digital I/O operating mode
In Digital I/O operating mode, an AVI64 behaves like a standard digital pin and features
pattern functionality within the full PMU force voltage range.
The following topics are covered:

Characteristics
Configuration and connection
Digital comparator
Drive operation
Error map size

Glitchless operating mode crossover

Maximum sequencer frequency and minimum period
Power budget and alarm
Third level VT of the AVI64 digital driver
Transition between High-Z mode and active drive mode
Configuration and connection
An AVI64 channel is configured for the Digital I/O operating mode if the channel is
defined as a digital pin using the Digital Pins editor. Both, the AVI64 channel in PMU
operating mode and in Digital I/O operating mode are defined in the digital pins editor.
The context definition, the type, and the mode are used to differentiate between the
two operating modes.
An AVI64 channel in the Digital I/O operating mode is always connected in the sense
only connection scheme. This connection mode features the required controlled
impedance environment and a low capacitance for the optimal performance.
An upgrade license is required for operating an AVI64 channel in the Digital I/O mode.
For more information, refer to Licensing in AVI64 specific setup tasks.
Topic 148853

Characteristics
The channel is typically used for applications that require a seamless integration of the
high voltage, medium power of the AVI64 PMU into digital pattern. An AVI64 channel in
Digital I/O mode is programmed using levels, timings, and digital pattern.
Block diagram - AVI64 in digital drive and compare operating
mode
The block diagram above shows an AVI64 channel in the Digital I/O operating mode
with the pin type set to io. The active components and connections are marked red. The
optional high-resolution comparators are marked blue. The shared resources are not
supported in this operating mode.

Feature comparison
The AVI64 is a V/I card that is optimized for high precision and high voltage
measurements. Some standard features and some pure digital features of other digital
pins are therefore not supported by the AVI64 or are replaced by the corresponding
functionality in the PMU operating mode:
Features replaced by the related PMU functionality Unsupported pure digital features
Pin PMU
Board ADC measurement
HPPMU measurement
Active load
Jitter injection
Pseudo random bit sequences (PRBS)
Clock forwarding
Overlay stream
SmartLoop™
Glitchless operating mode crossover
The AVI64 pins support the glitchless operating mode crossover from the PMU
operating mode to the Digital I/O operating mode and vice versa without disconnecting
the pins. Refer to AVI64 operating mode crossover for more information.
Maximum sequencer frequency and minimum period
The AVI64 supports a maximum sequencer frequency of 400 MHz that results in a
minimum vector period of 2.5 ns.
The digital driver supports a maximum data rate of up to 10 Mbps as defined in the
digital driver specifications. The pattern sequencer may apply a higher data rate but this
will result in unpredictable changes of the digital levels at the output. Therefore, we
recommend limiting the changeover between the drive levels to the maximum
supported data rate if a higher sequencer frequency is used.
Digital compare is supported with the maximum frequency but the limited maximum
data rate and the signal path bandwidth as defined in the digital compare specifications
must be considered to get meaningful and reliable results.

Drive operation
In digital drive mode, the test pattern will be used to set the AVI64 PMU to a previously
defined level or the high impedance tri-state mode. Supported levels are VIL, VIH and
VT.
The third level VT can be used instead of the high impedance tri-state mode. The VT
level is software programmable within the maximum driver level range independent of
VIL and VIH.
An AVI64 channel in digital drive mode features three programmable drive ranges:
±8 V
±30 V
-40 ... +80 V
The voltage drive range can be programmed manually in the level setup or the best fit
range can automatically be selected based on the defined drive levels. The ±30 V drive
range and the -40 ... +80 V drive range feature the same resolution of the voltage. For
an optimized utilization of the AVI64 power budget we recommend using the lower
drive range if possible.
The output voltage is referenced to the channel specific ground sense pin GS#.
The channel will be connected via the controlled impedance and low capacity path of
the sense pin (PS#). The output current of the driver supports ±50 mA in the Digital I/O
operating mode.
Drive current and current range:
Nominal maximum drive current: ±50 mA
Peak drive current: ±75 mA
Drive and compare current range: ±200 mA
The actual output current of the driver is measured continuously. A channel in Digital
I/O mode is disconnected if the current limit as defined above is exceeded for more
than 100 µs. Refer to paragraph "Digital I/O operating mode and power budget" below
for more information.
Transition between High-Z mode and active drive mode
The digital driver features a high impedance (High-Z) or Tri-state mode. Switching from
the high or low level into the High-Z mode and back requires about 10 μs.

Third level VT of the AVI64 digital driver
The AVI64 digital driver features the third level VT. The third level replaces the High-Z
mode in the pattern and is selected by the additional vt level definition in the level
setup.
The seamless transition from the third level VT to the other two levels requires that
certain drive edge actions are programmed:
Transition from the third level VT to level "0":
Use drive edge action "F0Z" to enter the VT level.
Use drive edge action "F00" or "0" for the transition to level "0".
Transition from the third level VT to level "1":
Use drive edge action "F1Z" to enter the VT level.
Use drive edge action "F10" or "1" for the transition to level "1".
For more information, refer to Timing Wavetables - Reference and Physical drive edge
action (physical_drive_edge_action).

Digital comparator
The digital comparator input signal is derived from the voltage at the PS# pin or the
output current of the PMU. An AVI64 channel features the high-speed comparator and
high-resolution comparators. All comparators are window comparators with two
programmable thresholds.
High‑speed voltage comparator
The channel compares the DUT output voltage with high bandwidth and tracking
slew rate against VOL and VOH thresholds. The threshold voltages are referenced to
the channel specific ground sense pin GS#. The high-speed comparator features
also a differential compare and termination mode for adjacent channels.
Two voltage ranges are available for the high-speed comparator:
±8 V
-40 ... +80 V
Several termination modes are available to adapt the comparator input to the
needs of the DUT outputs:
No termination.
50 Ω single ended termination to ground.
100 Ω termination to the adjacent channel in combination with differential
compare.
Termination by the driver: VIL, VIH and VT.
The Digital I/O mode supports also active pull down circuits that pull the
output pins with a low current to ground.
The voltage in the single ended 50 Ω termination mode is limited to maximum ±3.5
V. The voltage in the differential compare and termination mode is limited to
maximum ±7 V. The termination is disconnected if these limitations are violated.
The threshold voltages are referenced to the mid voltage of the two channels if the
differential compare and termination mode is used. The differential compare and
termination mode is supported for the channel combination 1‑3, 2‑4, 5‑7, and 6‑8
within a group of eight channels. Refer to AVI64 channel group and differential
compare assignment for a complete table of the supported channel combinations.
The high-speed comparator features a switchable hysteresis of about 25 mV.
High-resolution comparators of the PMU
The channel compares the DUT voltage or current with the full PMU single shot
accuracy and limited bandwidth against the two thresholds:

Voltage compare: The threshold voltages are referenced to the voltage that is
measured differentially between the high sense pin PS# and the channel
specific ground sense pin GS#. This compare mode supports all voltage
measurement ranges of the PMU. The voltage measurement range can be set
independently of the digital drive range.
Current compare: The channel compares the DUT output current with full
PMU single shot accuracy and limited bandwidth against ICL and ICH
thresholds. The current measurement range is fixed at ±200 mA in the Digital
I/O operating mode. All current measurement ranges are supported in the
PMU operating mode.
The sample frequency of the high-resolution comparators is defined by the sample
frequency of the voltage and current measurement and is 1 MHz. Interpolation
between two samples provides an optimized resolution of 5 ns.
Unlike PMU measurements in the PMU operating mode, the voltage measurement
range of the PMU "High-resolution comparators" can be selected independent of the
active range of the digital driver.

Hysteresis and sample frequency of the high resolution
comparators
The high-resolution comparators feature a programmable hysteresis that is defined in
percent of the measurement range. Half of the resulting value is symmetrically applied
to the programmed thresholds:
A programmed threshold of 15 V and 1 % hysteresis in the ±30 V range results in a
difference of 0.3 V.
The effective thresholds are
15.15 V for the rising edge and
14.85 V for the falling edge.
A programmed threshold of -2.0 mA and 2 % hysteresis in the ±5 mA range results
in a difference of 0.1 mA.
The effective thresholds are
-1.95 mA for the rising edge and
-2.05 mA for the falling edge.
A programmed threshold of 50 V and 3 % hysteresis in the -40 ... +80 V range
results in a difference of 2.4 V.
The effective thresholds are
51.2 V for the rising edge and
48.8 V for the falling edge.
The hysteresis calculation for the -40 ... +80 V range uses always 80 V as range
regardless of the polarity of the threshold.
The sample frequency of the ADCs used for the high-resolution comparators is 1 MHz.
Interpolation between two samples provides an optimized resolution of 5 ns.

Digital I/O operating mode, power budget and alarm
An AVI64 channel in the Digital I/O operating mode is also subject to be disconnected if
the 50mA limit of the channel in digital I/O operating mode or the total power budget
of the supply rail per card is exceeded. A channel in Digital I/O operating mode may
therefore be disconnected while a functional test is running. The related functional test
will fail if the channel is disconnected.
We strongly recommend checking and resetting the Power Budget exceeded flag after
every failing functional test using the APIs DPS_AUX_PIN_TASK.checkPowerFlags() and
DPS_AUX_TASK.getOvercurrent(). For more information refer to DPS power flags - get...()
functions.
We also recommend checking the flags Overtemperature and Safety Line. The
related critical conditions may also cause that a pin in digital I/O mode is disconnected
while a functional test is running. The best way checking all relevant flags are API
DPS_AUX_PIN_TASK.checkPowerFlags() followed by
DPS_AUX_TASK.getStatusWithoutConstVol().
Checking the PowerBudget 1 ... 3 warning flags at least once at the end of the
testflow is recommend for stable conditions in production environment. We recommend
checking the flags to ensure that the utilization of the power budgets leaves some
headroom for the DUT specific variance of the actual current. The warning flags are set
for all channels that caused the critical power budget utilization to be exceeded. The
flags are also set for channels that increased the power budget utilization within 10 ... 20
µs of the critical level's violation. The flags can be checked by API
DPS_AUX_PIN_TASK.checkPowerBudget() followed by the related APIs for retrieving the
read result. For more information refer to AVI64 status flags.
Error map size
For Smart Scale generation channel cards, the size of the internal error map (DCRT TP) is
65536 bits.

The number of cycles that fit into the error map (in Acquire All mode, DCGM
ALL) depends on the selected X mode and the number of bits stored per result:
numberOfCycles = errorMapSizeInBits / (xMode * bitsPerResult)
For example, in X1 PFC mode (2 bits/result), AVI64 channels can store 32768 cycles. In
X8 mode (1 bit/result), AVI64 channels can store 8192 cycles.
The size of the external error map (DCRT RAM) is not fixed and always depends on the
amount of available RAM. The number of testpoints defined in the .technology file, the
initially loaded patterns, the patterns generated by SmartRDI, and the DC result areas
limit the maximum size of the external error map. See also Result areas and vector
memory consumption.

AVI64 force, clamp, and measure voltages
The AVI64 card features a PMU per channel for forcing, clamping, and measuring
voltages. Additionally, some specialized shared resources that extend these functions
are available per group of eight channels.
Forcing or clamping voltage
The AVI64 PMUs are digitally regulated VI supplies with remote sense lines and a
common return path. The output voltage is referenced to ground sense pins GS# of the
channels. The common return path is the combination of all GND pins.
The digital controller of a PMU in force voltage mode will adjust the control value so
that the voltage between the high sense pogo pin (PS#) and the ground sense pogo pin
(GS#) is equal to the programmed voltage as long as the output current stays within the
programmed clamp current limits.
For more information refer to AVI64 force and clamp voltages.
Each group of eight channels features an additional shared floating high-current unit
and a ground referenced high-resolution voltage AWG for forcing voltages at the DUT.
Topic 148769

Measuring voltage
In Kelvin connection mode, the voltage is measured differentially between the high
sense pogo pin (PS#) and the low sense pogo pin (GS#). The digital controller measures
voltages and currents continuously, uses the measured values as feedback for the
control loop, and provides the measured values for software controlled or pattern
controlled measurements.
For more information refer to AVI64 measure voltages.
Each group of eight channels features an additional shared floating differential
voltmeter for measuring voltages differentially between two DUT pins. The floating
differential voltmeter also takes over the voltage feedback and measurement
functionality of the high-current unit. For more information refer to AVI64 floating high-
current unit.
PMU power budget
The AVI64 card comprises limited power budgets. To prevent any likelihood of an
overpower shutdown, SmarTest limits the overall power usage of an AVI64 card. Warning
flags are set (SmarTest 7) or alarms are generated (SmarTest 8) in case the utilization of a
power budget reaches a critical level. An error message is issued and the involved
channel or channels are disconnected if a power budget is exceeded. The programmed
force or clamp current and the programmed voltage range are used to calculate the
utilization of the available power budgets.
For more information, refer to AVI64 power budget.

Each AVI64 channel features a switchable clamp circuitry between the P# pogo pin and

Load step response
The load step response of an AVI64 channel depends on the selected filters, the actual
current range, the impedance of the high force and low force traces on the DUT board,
and on the capacitive load on the DUT board.
The selected voltage bandwidth and the set load capacitance value have an effect
on the load step response for an AVI64 channel that is forcing or clamping voltage.
The selected current bandwidth has an effect on the load step response for an
AVI64 channel that is forcing or clamping current.
Voltage sense lines
The forced or clamped voltage is measured differentially between the high sense pogo
pin (PS#) and the low sense pogo pin (GS#) or between the high sense pogo pins of two
channels if selected. The measured value is the voltage feedback value for the digital
controllers and is used to adjust the forced or clamped voltage. Refer to Voltage sense
lines in AVI64 measure voltages for a detailed description.

DC Scale voltage limits
The AVI64 card supports the DC Scale voltage and current limits. Both SmarTest and the
control logic of the AVI64 card ensure that the defined voltage and current limits cannot
be exceeded by programming higher or lower force or clamp values.
For accuracy specifications of the DC Scale voltage limits refer to the High-speed
(voltage) AWG specifications in AVI64 AWG specifications.
Note  The DC Scale voltage limits are independent of the voltage measured at the
PS# pogo pin. The voltage drop on the force line from the PMU buffer output to the
DUT must therefore be considered for the set voltage limits. We recommend setting
the voltage limits minimum 2.0 V above or below the highest or lowest expected
force or clamp value.
The defined DC Scale voltage limit ensures that the forced voltage cannot exceed the
DUT specific voltage limits for abnormal operating conditions. The following examples
for abnormal operating conditions are covered by the DC Scale voltage limits:
An irregular operating sequence of external switches like the PMUX01 Power MUX
or relays causes that the sense line temporarily is tied to another DUT pin than the
force pin. This will result in a high output voltage if the DC Scale voltage limits are
not set.
The maximum operating current of the FS clamp between P# and PS# is exceeded.
A user defined test method calculates a force value that exceeds the compliance
range of the DUT.

Each group of eight channels features an additional shared floating differential

Voltage sense lines
The voltage at the DUT is measured differentially between the high sense pin (PS#) and
the ground sense pin (GS#). Both pins are available per AVI64 channel.
The high sense pin (PS#) must be connected to the related high force pogo pin (P#)
directly at the DUT pins if the Kelvin connection scheme or the reverse Kelvin connection
scheme are used. The ground sense pin (GS#) must be connected to the common
ground pin (GND) or an adequate DUT pin directly at the DUT both for all connection
schemes.
The voltage difference between the force pins and sense pins is typically caused by the
voltage drop, produced by current flow over parasitic resistances on the DUT board. A
maximum voltage difference must be maintained between the high force pin (P#) and
the high sense pin (PS#) and between the ground sense pin (GS#) and the common
ground. Violating this rule will result in a wrong force voltage and wrong voltage
measurements.

Measurement filters
AVI64 channels feature programmable anti-aliasing, low-pass measurement filters for all
ADCs. For more information, refer to the Measurement filters section in AVI64
programming - Measure voltages. Note that the dynamic behavior of the force output is
independent of the measurement filters.
High-impedance voltage measurement mode (HIMP)
An AVI64 PMU features two high-impedance voltage measurement modes. The two
modes are used to measure the voltage at the DUT with no voltage or current applied.
The force output of the PMU is switched to a high-impedance mode. The voltage is
measured differentially between the high sense pogo pin (PS#) and the ground sense
pogo pin (GS#).
VM_HIZ mode: The PMU force output is set to high-impedance mode. The voltage
is measured differentially between the PS# pin and the GS# pin. The digital closed
loop control is still active in this mode and the voltage measure ADC is
synchronized to the clock of the loop. This mode supports on-board averaging of
the measured values as described above.
VM_HIZ_COH mode: This mode behaves similar to the VM_HIZ mode but the digital
closed loop control is disabled for this mode. The ADC is directly controlled by DC
events. The intended use of the VM_HIZ_COH mode are measurements that require
coherent sampling that is strictly synchronized with the controlling pattern.
The PMU output is disabled and set to high-impedance for both HIMP modes.
Previously applied PMU settings have no effect on the input bias current or the dynamic
behavior of the disabled PMU output or the sense input.

AVI64 force, clamp, and measure currents
An AVI64 card features a PMU per channel for forcing, clamping, and measuring
currents. A shared floating high-current unit features additional forcing, clamping, and
measuring current capabilities for each group of eight channels.
Forcing and clamping current
The AVI64 PMUs are digitally regulated VI supplies with remote sense lines and a
common return path. Each PMU is able to force or clamp voltages or to force or clamp
currents and features six combined force and measure current ranges.
The digital controller of a PMU in force current mode will adjust the control value so
that the output current at the high force pogo pin (P#) is equal to the programmed
current as long as the voltage between the high sense pogo pin (PS#) and the ground
sense pogo pin (GS#) stays within the programmed clamp voltage limits.
For more information, refer to AVI64 force and clamp currents.
Each group of eight channels features an additional shared floating high-current unit for
forcing and measuring currents at the DUT.
Current measurements
An AVI64 PMU measures the current at the output of the force amplifier regardless of
the PMU operating mode or the connection. The digital controller measures voltages
and currents continuously, uses the measured values as feedback for the control loop,
and provides the measured values for software controlled or pattern controlled
measurements.
Each group of eight channels features an additional shared floating high-current unit for
forcing and measuring currents at the DUT.
For more information, refer to AVI64 measure currents.
 The maximum PMU output voltage referenced to the common ground (GND) must be
maintained. For more information, refer to table "Maximum PMU output voltage
referenced to ground (GND)" in AVI64 force and clamp voltages.
 The voltage sense pins PS# and GS# are assigned to the floating differential voltmeter.
 A high voltage drop on the force lines P# or GND decreases the usable pulse width,
current, or voltage at the DUT. Refer to the diagrams in AVI64 floating high-current unit
for more information.

Topic 148772

Power budget
The AVI64 card comprises limited power budgets. To prevent any likelihood of an
overpower shutdown, SmarTest limits the overall power usage of an AVI64 card. Warning
flags are set (SmarTest 7) or alarms are generated (SmarTest 8) in case the utilization of a
power budget reaches a critical level. An error message is issued and the involved
channel or channels are disconnected if a power budget is exceeded. The programmed
force or clamp current and the programmed voltage range are used to calculate the
utilization of the available power budgets.
For more information refer to AVI64 power budget.

Averaging
