DPS128 voltage ranges
Voltage ranges are implemented to utilize the maximum specified output current per
channel as well as to effectively maximize the available current budget per board.
Topic 147812

Note  The voltage ranges are not linked to any electrical performance or accuracy
specification and are only applicable to HC type of channels.
Maximum output current
The maximum clamp current limit depends on the voltage range. For a specified
voltage range of 2.5 V, the maximum current is 1 A, while for a specified voltage
range of 7 V, the maximum current is 500 mA.
For more details, refer to DPS128 V-I curves and board power restrictions.
Power budget optimization
Using voltage ranges minimize the current dissipation, which also increases the
effectively usable current budget per power domain.
SmarTest internally calculates a certain current margin in dependency to the
programmed clamp current and programmed voltage range. By limiting the voltage
range the available current margin will increase. The amount of effective power gain
depends on multiple factors and is built up in a very complex formula that cannot
be described here.
If no voltage range is specified, the HC channels always works in the maximum voltage
range of 7 V (DPS32 compatible). This significantly limits the effective current budget of
a power domain because the SmarTest internal power budget calculations are based on
a potential force voltage of 7 V (which may never be programmed or applied).
To optimize the overall power usage of the board, it is mandatory to set up voltage
ranges for all channels, if some of them are operating in the 1 A current range.
The voltage range can be programmed to any value (no dedicated range), while all
values below 2.25 V are auto‑corrected to 2.25 V (minimum voltage range for 1 A
current range operation).
In total there are 256 internal range steps from 2.25 V up to 7 V. This gives a resolution
of ~18 mV per step. Any programmed value is therefore mapped to the next higher
range based on the resolution.

Limiting the voltage range can be done by:
DPS operation mode:
vout_frc_rng keyword in level equations, for example:
DPSPINS VDD
vout = 1.8
vout_frc_rng = 3.5 # max bump voltage
PMU operation mode:
vForceRange API of SPMU_TASK, for example:
SPMU_TASK dc;
dc.pin("VREF").vForce(1.8 V).vForceRange(3.5 V);
The voltage range should define the maximum voltage that is applied when the
DPS is in the connected state. Any dynamic actions that may "over-program" the
force voltage must be considered.
Switching the voltage force range requires a disconnect sequence. From a test time
point of view no spec should be used, but a maximum value that is valid for all
relevant specs and equations.
The HV type of channel does not implement voltage ranges. It operates solely in
the 15 V range fix.
DPS128 power budget decision model
To prevent any likelihood of an overpower shutdown of the DPS card, SmarTest limits
the overall power usage and issues an error message if it is violated. The decision is
based on the programmed current clamp limit of the channels, with the HC type also
taking care of the programmed voltage range.
Topic 147813

For the DPS operating mode, the parameters are defined in the level equations (ilimit,
vout_frc_rng). The decision is based on the level primary set and is triggered during
its activation.
For example, the following DPS128-HC setup triggers the error message during primary
set activation, as it is impossible to source / sink 1 A @ 2.5 V on all 128 channels in
parallel.
For the PMU operating mode, the current clamp limit and voltage range is typically
specified during the connect sequence of the instrument.
In the pattern‑based, dynamic mode, SmarTest also analyzes the programmed test
points for the defined current clamp limits (current force) on a per pattern basis. Based
on this, an error is triggered during pattern activation. There is no check for the voltage
range, as it cannot be changed during the pattern execution.

HC channel version
Specified voltage range with a minimum value of 2.25 V.
Current sink is the most important factor for voltage below 3.3 V.
Current source is the most important factor for voltage above 3.3 V.
No limitations when all channels operate at current below 1 A.
HV channel version
No dependency on voltage ranges - only a single range is available.
Current source is the most important factor.

DPS128 / DPS64 in DPS operating mode
For the DPS mode specify the pin type as DPS+. In DPS mode you can use the DC Scale
DPS128/DPS64 card like a DPS-slot DPS, to supply devices with power during the
execution of a test flow.
Each of the 128/64 channels can source and sink current at a programmed voltage, and
each channel can measure the voltages and currents supplied. Each high current channel
provides up to 1 Amp. Each high voltage channel can provide -6 to +15 Volt. For the
maximum source/sink current per card see the DPS128 / DPS64 specifications.
To find a summary of all supported resource parameters in the level file, refer to
DPSPINS resources.
Equations
Note  To use all features of the DC Scale DPS128/DPS64 card in DPS mode you
should use equations. For details see Level Equations.
Connecting and disconnecting in DPS operating mode
When connecting and disconnecting in DPS operating mode, the DPS128/DPS64 card
behaves like a DPS-slot device power supply.
When connected, it forces the programmed power supply voltage (vout). The current is
limited to the connect current limit (ilimit).
The DPS128/DPS64 must be disconnected before changing any of the following:
a voltage force range (vout_frc_rng)
a clamp current range (iout_clamp_rng)
If the card is still connected, you cannot activate a dps set that contains one of above
changes. To avoid damages to your device or DUT board, the system will display an
error message in the report window instead.
Topic 140642

Current and voltage measurement
In DPS operating mode, each channel of a DC Scale card can measure the supplied
current or voltage. See also Hardware view for DPS and VI pins.
Unganged current measurement in DPS mode
To achieve a higher output current, you can gang multiple DC Scale channels (see
Ganging DC Scale channels and DFPS, DFPS? - (DeFine Power Supply). But the higher
current of ganged channels has a negative effect on current-measurement accuracy.
To achieve a higher accuracy, for example for IDDQ-measurements, you can temporarily
ungang channels during measurement.
To temporarily ungang channels in DPS mode, use the MEASURE_CURRENT_UNGANGED
parameter in the DPS_TASK test method API.
Note that on AVI64, DPS128/64, and FVI16 you cannot execute a current compare on a
ganged group of channels if the group is in unganged mode. Already activated
comparators are silently disabled in unganged mode. A user notification (Error or
warning) is omitted in this case, to avoid any interrupt in the testflow. The previous state
of the comparators is automatically restored after the ganged group has been restored.
For further details see the DPS_TASK test method API.

VFIM - Voltage Force / Current Measure
In PMU operating mode you can use DC Scale cards like a standard PMU.
In voltage force mode, to perform current measurements you must specify a clamp
current. Specify both the minimum and maximum pass current values and units (mA or
µA). For further details see "Pass/Fail Pin DC Measurement" and "ADC Pin DC
Measurement" in Hardware view for digital pins and Hardware view for direct DC
measurement.
For test method programming details see SPMU_PIN_TASK.
For the voltage and current range specifications of the DC Scale cards see DC Scale
Device Power Supplies.
VFIM_UNGANGED - Voltage Force / Current Measure
Unganged
To achieve a higher output current, you can gang multiple DC Scale channels (see
Ganging DC Scale channels). But the higher current of ganged channels has a negative
effect on accuracy.
To achieve a higher accuracy, for example for IDDQ-measurements, you can temporarily
ungang channels before measurement.
Note that on AVI64, DPS128/64, and FVI16 you cannot execute a current compare on a
ganged group of channels if the group is in unganged mode. Already activated
comparators are silently disabled in unganged mode. A user notification (Error or
warning) is omitted in this case, to avoid any interrupt in the testflow. The previous state
of the comparators is automatically restored after the ganged group has been restored.
To temporarily ungang channels in PMU operating mode use the VFIM_UNGANGED
parameter of the SPMU_PIN_TASK test method API.
If the current range of a ganging group of DC Scale pins is larger than the measured
current, you can use only part of the pins within this group to perform the
measurement. Selecting the "VFIM_UNGANGED" mode automatically ungangs not
needed channels, based on the min() max() limits.
For details see SPMU_PIN_TASK.

IFVM - Current Force / Voltage Measure
In PMU operating mode you can use DC Scale cards like a standard PMU.
In current force mode, to perform voltage measurements you must specify a clamp
voltage. Specify both the minimum and maximum pass voltage values and units (mV or
V). For further details see "Pass/Fail Pin DC Measurement" and "ADC Pin DC
Measurement" in Hardware view for digital pins and Hardware view for direct DC
measurement.
For the voltage and current range specifications of the DC Scale cards see DC Scale
Device Power Supplies.
For test method programming details see SPMU_PIN_TASK .
VM_HIZ - High Impedance Voltage Measure
In PMU operating mode DC Scale cards support high impedance voltage measurements
(neither voltage nor current is forced).
In high impedance measurement mode (himp) DC Scale power supply cards act like a
voltmeter.
The high impedance measurement mode opens the AC_Force and H_Imp relays, and
closes the AC_Sense relay.
Note  You cannot use this feature for a DPS-slot DPS.
For details on equations see Level Equations.
For a non-equation based setup you must use the PSLR firmware command.

Specific design rules
Specific design rules must be followed when designing a new DUT board for the
DPS128/DPS64:
DPS128/DPS64 power budget: The DPS128/DPS64 card features two power
domains with a dedicated power budget. Each domain is able to deliver half of the
overall power budget. The power domain to channel mapping must be observed
for DPS128 cards when assigning the available channels to the DUT pins.
DPS128 / DPS64 capacitor requirements: For improved noise suppression, we
recommend using small ceramic capacitors. Additional capacitor requirements must
be considered for ganged channels
DPS128 / DPS64 recommendations for use: For safe handling of the DPS128 /
DPS64 card and getting out the best performance follow the recommendations for
designing the DUT board and setting up the test.
Pin assignment for Fast Sync / Fast Match: For fast local synchronization, the
synchronized DUT pins must be assigned to the same group of channels
respectively to the same test processor.

pogo blocks as shown below. For pogo cable assemblies ganging multiple channels
within the cable, refer to section "Assignment of ganged channels ..." in the sub-topics

Automatic down-ranging
DPS128/DPS64 channels feature automatic down-ranging for current measurements.
Automatic down-ranging means that the current range is automatically changed to the
best fit range for the measurement and restored to the original range after the
measurement.
Two parameters define whether the automatic down-ranging is performed or not:
1. The force / clamp current range:
Can be set explicitly or (if not defined)
is automatically derived from the forced or clamped value.
2. The current measurement range:
Can be set explicitly or (if not defined)
is automatically derived from the pass/fail thresholds.
Automatic down-ranging is performed only if the current measurement range is lower
than the force / clamp current range regardless whether the ranges have been set
explicitly or have been selected automatically.
Automatic down-ranging is supported for both code‑based programming using the
SPMU_TASK and DPS_TASK test method APIs and the pattern‑based programming using
the DC events and is also supported by SmartRDI.

DC Scale Limits
DC Scale Limits is a safety feature for the DC Scale power supply cards. The limits cannot
be exceeded. If the voltage or current is too high or too low, an error message is
triggered. See also Setting DC Scale voltage and current limits.
Different limits for source and sink current
For DC Scale DPS128/DPS64 cards, the maximum source current per card or channel is
different to the maximum sink current per card or channel. For the exact values see
DPS128 / DPS64 specifications.
To use all features of the power supply card in DPS mode, especially when operating
close to the power limits, you must use equations. The following DPSPINS resources
were either changed or introduced with the DPS128/DPS64:
ilimit Sets both the source and the sink current limit
ilimit_source Sets only the source current limit
ilimit_sink Sets only the sink current limit
Any specified current limits must be within the current force (clamp) ranges listed in the
DPS128 / DPS64 specifications. For DPS128/DPS64 cards, the iout_clamp_rng is
rounded up to the next current force (clamp) range. If ilimit falls into this range there
is no error or warning if ilimit is larger than the iout_clamp_rng.
For further details see Setting DC Scale voltage and current limits, Level Equations, and
DPSPINS resources (also DPSPINS).

Dynamic behavior - cap‑less mode
DPS 128 pins of both HC variant and HV variant in PMU operating mode can be adapted
to the load capacitance on the DUT board. Two modes are available:
Cap‑less mode:
From an application perspective, the cap‑less mode focuses on VI‑style operation
and affects the DPS128's internal voltage control loop as well as overall
performance, meaning on the slew rate and settling time. Depending on the type of
application, the cap‑less mode is intended to be used for load capacitances from a
few nano‑farads (nF) to a few micro‑farads (μF) per channel.
If oscillations occur, we recommend selecting the normal mode in SmarTest without
changing the capacitance on the DUT board.
Normal mode:
The normal mode focuses on the use as DUT power supply. It is intended to be
used for load capacitances from a few micro‑farads (μF) up to 470 μF per channel.
The normal mode is the default if the capacitance is not defined in SmarTest.
The cap‑less mode can be selected by test method API SPMU_PIN_TASK.loadCap() or
SmartRDI function rdi.dc().loadCap() of SmarTest 7.
The programmed load capacitance defines whether the cap‑less mode or the normal
mode is selected. The threshold for selecting the mode differs for SmarTest 7 and
SmarTest 8:
Cap‑less mode Normal mode
SmarTest 7: = 0.0 μF > 0.0 μF
SmarTest 8: ≤ 2.2 μF > 2.2 μF

Flush vectors at the end of a pattern
Due to inter module communication it is required to keep the pattern running for a
short time after the last ADC measurement related DC event. The actual required time or
number of flush vectors depends on the setup. In case of insufficient number of vectors
before pattern stop, a communication error might occur and measurement results might
be lost.
The number of required flush vectors depends on the average count and the pattern
cycle time as follows:
DGT mode (Measurement):
Minimum number of vectors = 40 + ( (6.12 μs + (5 μs * average) ) / period)
AWG+DGT mode (Force and measurement combined):
Minimum number of vectors = 40 + ( (8.34 μs + (5 μs * average) ) / period)
where: average = Programmed average count
period = Cycle time of the pattern
The calculated number is the minimum number of vectors that is required between the
last measure event and the end of the pattern.
The minimum number of vectors may be higher if TMU measurements are started in the
same pattern as the ADC measurements.
Note that the TSST? - (TeSt STatus) firmware command can be used to check for missing
samples: Bit 8 is set if a measurement is lost.

Multiport setup
The total channel memory of DPS128/DPS64 cards is 28 MB. If you run out of available
channel memory, it is recommended to use a separate port for the DPS128/DPS64. For
details see Typical issues when converting to DPS128 .
The minimum period for DPS128/DPS64 is 20 ns. In case of period incompatibilities in a
test program, it is recommended to use a separate timing port for the DPS128/DPS64.
For details see Typical issues when converting to DPS128 .
For further details see also Multiport testing with multiple clock domains and Minimum
period / maximum frequency of the sequencer.
Multisite setup
In case of a multisite setup you must strictly differentiate between high-current (HC) and
high-voltage (HV) channels. The same device pin on the various sites must be allocated
to a channel of the same type (HC or HV). A device pin cannot be an HV pin on one site
and an HC pin on another site.
Parallel dynamic and static DC actions
The DPS128/DPS64, when starting the sequencer with the SQST RUN firmware
command or with the SEQUENCER_STATUS run() member function, cannot execute
dynamic and static DC actions in parallel. For measurements during a sequencer run use
profiling. Profiling allows to measure in parallel to a dynamic pattern.
Pin configuration
The pin configuration of channel-slot DC Scale cards is slightly different to that of a
DPS-slot device power supply.
To configure a DC Scale pin for DPS operating mode you must specify the pin type as
DPS+. For details see DC Scale pin (DPS mode) setup.

Card configuration in the model file
In the POGOCABLING section of the model file you must specify the installed pogo
cable assembly as defined below.
Note that in SmarTest 7, the card must also be defined in the DPS section of the model
file as shown in the example or for DPS128-HC/HV in the DPS128-HC/HV in the model
file section below.
E8023PA pogo cable assembly: 8 HD pogo blocks (Standard)
The E8023PA pogo cable assembly connects the DPS128/DPS64 via eight HD pogo
blocks to the DUT board.
There are no special rules and no special checks in the software.
The pogo block sequence is defined as follows:
"A,  B,  C,  D,  E,  F,  G,  H"
Example:
112: pogoblocks = "225, 425, 229, 429, 303, 304, 307, 308"
DPS64 channels are connected via the first four pogo blocks. Only these four pogo
blocks must be defined. See also the E8023PH pogo assembly below.
Example:
112: pogoblocks = "225, 425, 229, 429"
E8023PB pogo cable assembly: 2 VHD pogo blocks
The E8023PB pogo cable assembly connects the DPS64 or half of the DPS128
channels via two VHD pogo blocks to the DUT board.
Pogo cable assembly E8023PB is supported by SmarTest 7.5.4.4, 8.3.4.2, and higher.
For channels A1 … A16 on pogo block rows a, b, c, and d, the same mapping
is used as for the HD pogo block. For these channels, the physical pogo block
position is used in the model file .
The additional channels B1 … B16 on pogo block rows e, f, and g are mapped
to virtual pogo blocks. The number of a virtual pogo block is defined by the
physical pogo block position plus an offset of 400.

The pogo block sequence is defined as follows:
"AB,  AB+400,  CD,  CD+400"
The notation in the sequence definition above is as follows:
1)
1)

Physical pogo blocks AB and CD without an offset refer to the channels on
pogo block rows a, b, c, d.
AB+400 and CD+400 refer to the channels on pogo block rows e, f, g and
define two virtual pogo blocks.
Example:
107: pogoblocks = "317, 717, 318, 718",
                        type = REDIRECT, subtype = E8023PB,
                        config = "317=317,717; 318=318,718"
Note that in the model file you have to define twice as many pogo blocks as the
pogo cable assembly has pogo blocks: All physically available pogo blocks and the
same number of virtual pogo blocks that cover the additional channels B1 … B16.
E8023PC pogo cable assembly: 4 HD pogo blocks (DPS128-HC only)
The E8023PC pogo cable assembly connects the DPS128 via four HD pogo blocks
to the DUT board, ganging two DPS128 channels to one channel on the pogo block
side. The pogo cable assembly combines 32 DPS128 channels per pogo block.
Virtual pogo blocks, using an offset of 432 to the physical pogo block locations,
must therefore be defined.
The pogo block sequence is defined as follows:
"A,  A+432,  B,  B+432,  C,  C+432,  D,  D+432"
Example:
112: pogoblocks = "225, 657, 425, 857, 229, 661, 429, 861",
     type=REDIRECT, subtype=E8023PC, 
     config="225=225,657; 425=425,857; 229=229,661; 429=429,861"
SmarTest checks that eight addresses are entered, that the offset for the virtual
pogo blocks is 432 and that the mapping (config) is correctly set up.
E8023PD pogo cable assembly: 2 HD pogo blocks (DPS64 only)
The E8023PD pogo cable assembly connects the DPS64 card via two HD pogo
blocks to the DUT board.

It gangs two DPS64 channels to one channel on the pogo
block side. Virtual pogo blocks, using an offset of 432 to the physical pogo block
locations, are to be defined.
This cable is only used for the half-populated DPS card with 64 channels (equals 4
logical boards).
The pogo block sequence is defined as follows:
"A,  A+432,  B,  B+432"

Example:
112: pogoblocks = "225, 657, 425, 857",
                        type=REDIRECT, subtype=E8023PD,
                        config="225=225,657; 425=425,857"
SmarTest checks that four addresses are entered, that the offset for the virtual pogo
blocks is 432 and that the mapping (config) is correctly set up.
E8023PE pogo cable assembly: 8 MS-DPS style pogo blocks (DPS128-HC only)
The E8023PE pogo cable assembly connects the DPS128-HC via eight MS-DPS style
pogo blocks to the DUT board. It gangs two DPS128 channels to one channel on
the pogo block side.
All DPS128 channels are to be defined by virtual pogo blocks. Pogo blocks such as
"341, 342" are virtual pogo blocks.
The physical MS-DPS pogo block locations are defined by the config statement.
This statement assigns the virtual three-digit DPS128 pogo blocks to the physical
one-digit MS-DPS pogo block locations.
Example:
112: pogoblocks = "341, 342, 343, 344, 345, 346, 347, 348",
     type=REDIRECT, subtype=E8023PE, 
     config="1=341; 2=342; 3=343; 4=344; 5=345; 6=346; 7=347; 8=348"
SmarTest checks that eight addresses are entered and that the mapping (config) is
correctly set up.
E8023PF pogo cable assembly: 2 MS-DPS style pogo blocks (DPS64 only)
The E8023PF pogo cable assembly connects the DPS64 card via two MS-DPS style
pogo blocks to the DUT board. It gangs four DPS64 channels to one channel on the
MS-DPS pogo block side.
All DPS64 channels are to be defined by virtual pogo blocks. Pogo blocks such as
"341, 342" are virtual pogo blocks.
The physical MS-DPS pogo block locations are defined by the config statement.

The physical MS-DPS pogo block locations are defined by the config statement.
This statement assigns the virtual three-digit DPS128 pogo blocks to the physical
one-digit MS-DPS pogo block locations.
Example:

Second cable:
113: pogoblocks = "345, 346, 347, 348",

The E8023PG pogo cable assembly connects the DPS64-HC via four MS-DPS style
pogo blocks to the DUT board: It gangs two DPS128 channels to one channel on
the MS-DPS pogo block side.
All DPS64 channels are to be defined by virtual pogo blocks. Pogo blocks such as
"341, 342" are virtual pogo blocks.
The physical MS-DPS pogo block locations are defined by the config statement.
This statement assigns the virtual three-digit DPS128 pogo blocks to the physical
one-digit MS-DPS pogo block locations.
Example:
First cable:

                        type=REDIRECT, subtype=E8023PG,

113: pogoblocks = "345, 346, 347, 348",
                        type=REDIRECT, subtype=E8023PG,
                        config="5=345; 6=346; 7=347; 8=348"

correctly set up.

The E8023PH pogo assembly connects the DPS64 card via four HD pogo blocks to

E8023PK pogo cable assembly: 4 VHD pogo blocks (DPS128)
The E8023PK pogo cable assembly connects the DPS128 via four VHD pogo blocks
to the DUT board.
Pogo cable assembly E8023PK is supported by SmarTest 7.5.4.4, 8.3.4.3, and higher.
For channels A1 … A16 on pogo block rows a, b, c, and d, the same mapping

The additional channels B1 … B16 on pogo block rows e, f, and g are mapped

"AB,  AB+400,  CD,  CD+400,  EF,  EF+400,  GH,  GH+400"

channel mapping must be observed for DPS128 cards when assigning the available
channels to the DUT pins. For more information refer to DPS128/DPS64 power budget.

Operating modes
DC Scale DPS32 cards have two operating modes:
DPS operating mode (DPS+)
In DPS operating mode you can use DC Scale DPS32 cards like a standard DPS, to
supply devices with power during the execution of a test flow.
To find a summary of all supported resource parameters in the level file, refer to
DPSPINS resources.
PMU operating mode (SIG)
In PMU operating mode you can use DC Scale DPS32 cards like a standard PMU to
temporarily supply power for a single testsuite or for a group of testsuites.
A DPS32 channel can be configured either for the DPS operating mode or for the PMU
operating mode but not for both.
In both operating modes each of the 32 channels of every power supply card can
source and sink current at a programmed voltage,
measure the voltages and currents supplied,
supply power to external circuits on a load board,
be programmed in a testsuite for a certain test,
be shared between different sites (channel sharing),
be ganged to increase the supply current,
do connectivity checks,
check the status of the device power supply.
The DPS operating mode is a superset of the PMU operating mode and has some
additional capabilities. Only in DPS operating mode the DC Scale power supply cards
can
take part in connect and disconnect sequences, and
take part in the set activation.
Note  In PMU mode a DC Scale DPS32 card does not take part in standard
connect and disconnect sequences, and cannot take part in the set activation,
although you can add DC Scale DPS32 cards to user-defined connect and
disconnect sequences.
For further details see DPS operating mode of DC Scale cards and PMU operating mode
of DC Scale cards.

Measurement modes
DC Scale DPS32 cards support voltage and current measurements in both the DPS and
PMU operating modes.
For measurements in DPS operating mode see Measuring current or voltage in DPS
operating mode.
For measurements in PMU operating mode see Measuring current or voltage in PMU
operating mode. These are:
current measurements
unganged current measurements
voltage measurement see
high-impedance voltage measure mode

Ganging DC Scale DPS32 channels
To achieve a higher output current, you can operate multiple channels of DC Scale
DPS32 cards in parallel, known as ganging. Ganging is the combining of multiple DPS
channels to provide a higher current than a single DPS channel could provide.
The actual ganging, that is the physical parallel connection, is done on the DUT board.
For details see Connecting DPS channels in parallel.
To gang DPS32 channels you use either the Pin Configuration tool or firmware
commands.
You can gang any number of successive channels (max. 32) within a DPS32 card.
Ganged channels must be located on the same card. You cannot gang across DPS32
cards.
You can configure these successive channels in up to 16 gang groups.
For details on the setup procedure see Defining DC Scale Pins.
For the firmware commands see DFPS, DFPS? - (DeFine Power Supply) for ganging in
DPS operating mode and DFPN, DFPN? - (DeFine Pin Name) for ganging in PMU
operating mode.
Each gang group consists of a master channel and one or more slave channels. The
master channel distributes two analog signals to the slave channels. One signal is the
target voltage on the output, and the second is a voltage that represents the current of
the master. The slave channels will adjust their own voltage to match the current of the
master channel.
Ganging supplies higher currents to a device. To avoid a negative effect on measure-
current accuracy, for example for IDD-measurements, you can temporarily ungang
channels during measurement. The unganging differs for the DPS and PMU operating
modes. For details see Measuring current or voltage in DPS operating mode and
Measuring current or voltage in PMU operating mode.
Channel sharing
You can share the same DC Scale channel between several sites.
This allows to save DPS channels and to supply external circuits on the DUT board.
See also Test Method Programs and Sharing Channels Between Several Sites.

Pin configuration
The pin configuration of channel-slot DC Scale cards is slightly different to that of a
DPS-slot device power supply.

Level programming rule
If the voltage of more than 20 channels of one or more DPS32 cards, that are connected
to the same card cage DC/DC, is programmed down by more than 3V (see example in
graphic below), the discharge current from the internal capacitances becomes too large
and the card cage DC/DC cannot sink it anymore. The test system shuts down.
To avoid this you must either
sequentially connect/disconnect, or
sequentially change the level.

E8013GUL GULP2 cable
The GULP2 conversion cable E8013GUL connects a DPS32 card to a DUT board designed
for use with MS-DPS cards. The cable provides a 1 DPS32 (32ch) to 4 MS-DPS (4x8ch)
conversion. Thus a GULP2 cable has a DPS32 card connector at one end and four MS-
DPS pogo blocks at the other - these must be installed in the test head.
Physically the pogo cable is connected to an MS-DPS pogo location. Since SmarTest
requires a pogo location within the IO range, appropriate pogo locations need to be
used to address the DPS32 card. These locations are called virtual pogo block locations
(for more information refer to POGOCABLING section and Pogocabling entries for
different card types). For the purposes of this topic the locations 225/425 and 229/429
are used as an example.
The MS-DPS pogo blocks are labeled DPS 1 (4), DPS 2 (5) , DPS 3 (6), DPS 8 (7).
Up to two cables can be used on a Large DUT interface or on a DUT Scale interface, one
cable on the Small DUT interface for ATH, CTH or STH. The cables are referred to as
"GULP2 #1" and GULP2 #2.

E8013QUL QUL cable
The QUL pogo cable (E8013QUL) connects a DPS32 card to a DUT board designed for
use with MS-DPS cards. The cable provides a one DPS32 (32ch) to two MS-DPS (2x8ch, 2
channels are internally ganged) conversion. Thus a QUL cable has a DPS32 card
connector at one end and two MS-DPS pogo blocks at the other. For example, in a large
test head four QUL pogo cables can support eight MS-DPS pogo locations.

requires a pogo location within the IO range, appropriate pogo locations need to be
used to address the DPS32 card. These locations are called virtual pogo block locations
(for more information refer to POGOCABLING section and Pogocabling entries for
different card types).
Up to four cables can be used on a large DUT interface or on a DUT Scale interface, two
cables on the small DUT interface for ATH, CTH or STH.

DC Scale FVI16 card
The FVI16 card is a high-current and high-voltage floating VI source that is optimized
for a wide range of analog power tests. The card belongs to the DC Scale family and can
reside in any channel card slot.
Topic 152680

FVI16 provides 16 fully floating high-current and high-voltage channels. Each channel
can supply voltages from -60 V to +120 V within a floating range of ±200 V and offers
pulse current capability up to ±10 A per channel and ±3 A continuous.
A floating differential high-voltage time measurement unit (TMU) with separate inputs is
available for each channel.

FVI16 safety
WARNING Voltages greater than 60 V DC may be present on this card. Only
trained users are allowed to operate test equipment containing this card. The card
contains a high voltage safety circuit. This must be used in combination with the
DUT board / DUT interface safety circuitry specified below to protect users from
exposure to high voltages.
General safety precautions
The following safety precautions must be observed during all phases of operation,
service and repair of a high voltage power supply card. Failure to comply with these
precautions, or with specific warnings in this manual, violates safety standards and the
intended use of the system. Advantest assumes no liability for the customer's failure to
comply with these requirements.
All safety advice and requirements on the safe handling of DUT boards are applicable to
the Twinning DUT board and the Twinning family board as well.
This is a Safety Class 1 instrument (provided with terminals for protective grounding)
and has been manufactured and tested to international safety standards.
Topic 152682

Operation
WARNING Do not remove isolating covers from the DUT board or the DUT
interface during operation.
High-voltage protection system
A combination of electrical and mechanical protection devices shall be used to protect
users from exposure to high voltages. High voltage power supply cards comprise a
safety circuit. This has to be regarded as part of the entire high-voltage protection
system.
The following devices must be used to fulfill the safety requirements:
All parts of the DUT board must be equipped with isolating covers.
All parts of the DUT interface must be equipped with isolating covers.
Isolating covers that can be removed or opened without the use of tools must be
fitted with a safety interlock.
This safety interlock must be used to control the safety circuit on all high voltage
power supply cards installed in the test system.
WARNING A faulty DUT or DUT board may cause high voltages to be applied
to various parts of the DUT board or DUT interface. To protect users from exposure
to high voltages, all parts of the DUT board and DUT interface shall be equipped
with isolating covers.

Operating modes
DPS operating mode: The channel is typically used for DPS applications to supply
the DUT. The channel is basically programmed using DPS primary sets. The
connection modes NORM, UNGANG, and HIMP are supported. For more information,
refer to FVI16 in DPS operating mode.
To find a summary of all supported resource parameters in the level file, refer to
DPSPINS resources.
PMU operating mode: The channel is typically used for VI applications and is
basically programmed using test methods and APIs. The connection modes for
normal operation and for high impedance voltage measurements are supported.
For more information, refer to FVI16 in PMU operating mode.
An FVI16 channel can be configured either for the DPS operating mode or for the PMU
operating mode but not for both.

Additional features
Kelvin measurement units are available for each channel. The units are used to
verify that the force lines and the sense lines are connected together.
The Voltage drop measurement unit measures and monitors the voltage drop on
the force lines.
Internal force to sense link for time-optimized multiplexing using external switches.
The on-board safety circuit, in combination with related hardware and cover of the
DUT board, prevents the users from being exposed to hazardous voltages.
Surge tracker for detection of voltage or current spikes.
Profiling with Hardware view is supported for voltage and current measurements
and the charging level of the on‑board energy storages.
Spike free connection by Smart connect: An integrated connection sequencer
enables spike free connection to unknown DUT voltages.
Dynamic range switching: The combined force and measure ranges can be changed
without disconnecting and connecting a channel without any spike. This enables
IDDQ measurements in a single pattern run and fast line charge capability for low
current measurements.
Each FVI16 channel features five simultaneously triggered ADCs:
Voltage and current measurement
Voltage drop on the force line (HF#) and on the return line (LF#)
Level of the on-board energy storage
The digital closed loop control of an FVI16 channel triggers not only the main ADCs
for measuring the voltage and current, but also the other three ADCs, thus
providing data for all five ADCs with a fixed temporal relationship.
This feature allows you, determining all five ADC values for single-shot
measurements, with the five values relating all to exactly the same position in the
time line.

Test processor, memory, and data analysis features
Setup and measurement sequences are controlled by test processors. A test
processor features eight cores, each controlling one channel.
The test processor memory is shared between setups, testpoints, waveforms, digital
patterns, and sample data or measurement results.
The memory available per channel for the test program is approximately 107 MB for
a typical setup.
Several alarm flags are available to indicate irregular operating conditions.
Hardware based averaging is available for better accuracy and throughput.
A built-in result analysis is available that checks the measurement data against user
specified test limits.
HV (High-Voltage) protection
The FVI16 card may be connected to low-voltage cards via defective DUTs or
unintentionally closed connections. The card provides enough energy to damage the
low-voltage cards in this case. Therefore, we recommend that you implement a HV
(High-Voltage) protection circuitry on your DUT boards to protect the low-voltage cards.
This will improve the uptime of the test system and the throughput of high-voltage
applications.

FVI16 guard
"Guarding" is a technique to minimize parasitic leakage currents of the signal path to
the DUT. A guard voltage of the same potential as on the signal path is applied to
Topic 152704

parallel traces. This will avoid leakage currents flowing to DUT board ground or other
traces.
For guarding of an FVI16 channel, the high force line (HF#) and the high sense line (HS#)
are shielded by parallel traces connected to the GUARD# pogo pin of the channel.
The GUARD# output is designed as a passive guard: The switched GUARD# pogo pin
and the internal guard lines of the channel are connected to the main driver output via a
current-limiter.
The FVI16 guard requires no additional resources or specific software support. The
guard output relay is automatically closed or opened when a FVI16 channel is connected
or disconnected.
Note  The guard output relay will be opened automatically in high impedance
voltage measure mode (VM_HIZ).

FVI16 internal force to sense (FS) link
FVI16 features an internal programmable force to sense (FS) link that is required for
multiplexing a channel on the DUT board without disconnecting the channel.
Multiplexing FVI16 channels by relays on the DUT board requires normally
disconnecting the channels while the relay settings are changed. Otherwise, the open
force to sense connections of the multiplexed channels may lead to unstable or
disconnected channels. For time-optimized multiplexing of active channels, the internal
FS link can be used to provide temporarily a stable force to sense connection for the
short time while the setup of the external relays is changed.
Characteristics of the internal FS link
The following data are to be observed when using the internal FS link:
The internal FS link consists of two programmable switches from HF# to HS# and
from LF# to LS#.
The two switches are protected by current limiters.
The typical maximum current is 1 mA.
The software opens or closes the two switches at the same time.
The sense connections to the DUT are opened automatically as soon as the internal
FS link switches are closed and vice versa.
The internal FS link is supported only in the PMU operating mode.
Topic 344955
1)

Important points on using the internal FS link
Improper use of internal FS link may lead to incorrect measurements or other unwanted
behavior:
Tests performed with closed FS link may still work and show a passing result but the
forced and measured voltages are not correctly sensed.
The internal FS link should be closed only for the short time while the setup of
external relays is changed. The link must not be closed for the following
measurements.
With closed FS link, the FVI16 voltage drop measurement unit cannot measure the
voltage drop on the force lines.
With closed FS link, monitoring of the maximum voltage drop cannot work
correctly.
The spike free connection by Smart connect as defined in the FVI16 other
specifications works only for newly connected channels. The setup for hot switching
using the internal FS link and external relays needs therefore your special attention.
SmarTest version 7.5.0 only: Overlapped switching, caused by improper switching
sequences, may result in shorted DUT pins and is not recommended.
Application note
Internal FS link is opened at the end of a pattern
The internal force to sense (FS) link is automatically opened and the sense
connection to the DUT is restored whenever a pattern on an FVI16 channel ends.
This is to prevent from erroneous measurements with closed internal FS link.
This behavior can be disabled. For more information, refer to FVI16 programming -

FVI16 Kelvin test unit
The FVI16 card features a Kelvin test unit, also known as sense-connection test unit. The
Kelvin test unit is available per channel for the HS# to HF# connection and for the LS# to
LF# connection.
 For safe operation, we recommend the following switching sequence for SmarTest
7.5.0:
1. Close the internal FS link.
2. Open the old sense connection on the DUT board.
3. Open the old force connection on the DUT board.
4. Close the new force connection on the DUT board.
5. Close the new sense connection ton the DUT board.
6. Open the internal FS link.
2)
Topic 152700

Kelvin test means that the connection from the force lines to the sense lines on the DUT
board or at the DUT pins is verified with a small test current applied. A PASS/FAIL result
is returned.
The Kelvin test unit applies the small test current to the tested force to sense (FS)
connection and measures the voltage drop between the two lines. The measured
voltage is used as criterion for the pass/fail decision and should be near 0.0 V for a good
FS connection.
The Kelvin test unit is available in the PMU operating mode and in the DPS operating
mode.
Note  The purpose of the Kelvin test unit is to ensure that when the DUT is
contacted, the high-impedance sense line is connected to the force line at the DUT
with a sufficiently low contact resistance. Due to the high input impedance of the
sense lines, the fixed threshold of some kilo-Ohms will be sufficiently low.
The Kelvin test unit is the only resource that can perform a reliable sense connection
test with a defined test current applied.
Since connections and hardware on the DUT board can sabotage the test of the
sense connections, we recommend that you check the functionality of the test
without DUT and with open sense connections. All tested sense connections must
fail in this verification.
The purpose of the Kelvin test unit is not to check the low impedance force
connections. The force connections are to be checked by the FVI16 voltage drop
measurement unit in combination with a high test current forced by the PMU. This
force connection test requires that the contact resistance of the sense lines already
has been verified.
Attention: An inadequate sense line connection does not necessarily mean that a
force drop test fails. The input bias current of the line may falsify the measurement
and mask another fatal error like a high voltage drop on the force line.
CAUTION The FVI16 PMU forces the test current via one of the tested lines, the
FS connection, and via the other tested line to ground. For the sense connection
test, one of the lines may be internally connected to ground. Therefore, the DUT
must be powered down before the Kelvin test (or sense connection test) is started in
disconnected mode.

Basic data of the FVI16 Kelvin test unit:
The Kelvin test unit is available per channel.
The threshold for the pass/fail decision is about 5 kΩ.
The test current is maximum about 100 µA.

The maximum capacitance between the force lines and the corresponding sense
lines is 5 nF.
The set up and set down of the test is performed in parallel on all selected pins.
Three measurements are serially performed for the HF# pin, the HS# pin and the
LS# pin.
Testing sixteen FVI16 channels requires a test time of about 15 ms per site.
The test can be performed only in the disconnected state of the selected pins.

Operating principle
The test is divided into three sub-tests for the HF# pin, HS# pin and the LS# pin. The
measurements are performed serially on the pins.
HF# line test
The test current is applied to the high force pin (HF#). The high sense pin (HS#) is
internally connected ground (LF#). The voltage drop from HF# via the FS connection
at the DUT and the HS# or via a possibly existing internal ground connection of the
DUT to LF# is measured and judged.
HS# line test
The connection from HS# to ground is opened and the voltage drop is measured
again with the test current still applied via the HF# pin. The voltage will increase to
the set voltage clamp in case no internal ground connection of the DUT exists: The
previously performed H# line test covers both the HF# line and the HS# line. For the
other case, an internal connection via the DUT is assumed and only the sense line is
tested by applying the test current to the HS# pin.
LS# line test
The test current is applied to the low sense pin (LS#). The voltage drop from HS# via
the FS connection at the DUT to the LF# pin is measured and judged.

For information on how to program a sense connection test, refer to FVI16
programming - Kelvin test / sense connection test.

FVI16 safety circuit
The card includes an on-board safety circuit to protect users from exposure to
hazardous voltages.
WARNING Voltages greater than 60 V DC may be present on this card. Refer to
FVI16 safety for more information.
Topic 152701

On-board safety circuit
The safety circuit consists of the pogo pins SAFETY1_5V, SAFETY2_5V, SAFETY1_GND,
SAFETY2_GND and related on-board hardware. An external control voltage must be
applied to the two pairs of pins to operate the card. Each of the two pairs is assigned to
eight channels:
SAFETY1_5V and SAFETY1_GND are assigned to FVI16 channels 1 to 8
SAFETY2_5V and SAFETY2_GND are assigned to FVI16 channels 9 to 16
The assigned group of channels remains disconnect if the control voltage is not applied.
This applies to all voltage ranges and for all current ranges of the FVI16 channels
regardless of the programmed voltage or current.
Note  The main purpose of the safety circuit is to protect the user from exposure to
hazardous voltages by opening the output switches of the FVI16 channels when the
isolating cover is opened.
The safety circuit cannot take into account parameters such as the programmed slew
rates or bandwidth. This behavior differs from that in normal operation and can lead
to DUT damage.
We therefore strongly recommend keeping the isolating cover closed during
operation.

Behavior with disabled safety circuit
The card behaves as follows if the control voltage is not applied:
The output switches for all channels of the related group of eight channels are
opened immediately.
The Safety line flag is set for the channels of the related group.
An error message is shown in the report window and in the console window as
soon as the channel is accessed the next time.

Error message for an FVI16 channel in DPS operating mode:

voltage has been applied meanwhile.
Behavior with enabled safety circuit
The FVI16 card behaves as follows if the safety circuit is enabled:
The output switches for all channels of the related group of eight channels are
closed.
The next time one of the affected channels is accessed, the error message shown
above is displayed.
Although the affected channels are activated again as soon as the safety circuit is
enabled, each channel must be disconnected and reconnected by SmarTest in order
to clear the error flag and continue with normal operation.
CAUTION The original voltage settings of the channels are restored
automatically as soon as the safety circuit is enabled. As a result, the affected
channels immediately output the programmed force or clamp voltage.

On-board hardware and required DUT board circuitry
To enable the FVI16 card connect a control voltage of +5.0 V DC from an adequate
power supply to the pogo pins SAFETY1_5V, SAFETY2_5V, SAFETY1_GND and
SAFETY2_GND. The supply must be applied via a safety interlock that is open when the
DUT board cover or the DUT interface cover is open.
The user-accessible part of the safety circuit is isolated from the rest of the card; thereby
the parallel connection of two or more cards is supported. Refer to FVI16 safety pogo
pins for information on the characteristics of the pogo pins.

Application notes
Enable the safety circuit while FVI16 channels are connected
The safety circuit has the user protection in the focus. Switching off the safety circuit
control voltage of connected and operating FVI16 channels may result in unwanted
conditions and can damage the DUT. We recommend therefore, keeping the safety
circuit always connected to the control voltage while FVI16 channels are connected
to the DUT.
Other alarm flags triggered by the safety circuit
The safety circuit must be maintained for FVI16 in order to operate properly for
safety reasons. In case of switching off the control voltage of connected FVI16
channels, the Safety line flag is set. Other status flags may also be set when the
safety circuit is disabled during operation.
Emergency shutdown triggered by the HV (High-Voltage) protection circuitry
The FVI16 card may be connected to low-voltage cards via defective DUTs or
unintentionally closed connections. The card provides enough energy to damage the
low-voltage cards in this case. Therefore, we recommend that you implement a HV
(High-Voltage) protection circuitry on your DUT boards to protect the low-voltage
cards.
The energy that can be delivered by the FVI16 channels may exceed the maximum
energy that can be absorbed by the HV protection circuitry. For optimized
dimensioning of the HV protection circuitry, an optional output of the circuitry may
be used to disconnect the control voltage from the FVI16 cards in case the HV
protection circuitry is active. This will minimize the energy that must be absorbed by
the HV protection circuitry.
CAUTION The emergency shutdown by disabling the safety circuitry may be
implemented only for FVI16 cards. This solution must not be used for the legacy
DC Scale PVI8 card.

FVI16 surge tracker
The FVI16 features a surge tracker per channel that monitors the voltage between the
high sense (HS#) and low sense (LS#) pins, between the high-speed TMU inputs
(TMU_H# and (TMU_L#), or the output current of the PMU.
The surge tracker is available in the PMU operating mode and in the DPS operating
mode.
Once the surge tracker is turned on, it monitors the voltage or current unless being
turned off. In a typical use scenario the surge tracker is activated in the very beginning
of a testflow and the status is checked at the end of the testflow.
The surge tracker checks against both high (positive) and low (negative) voltage or
current thresholds, which can be set individually. Two flags indicate if thresholds have
been exceeded. These flags are latched (stored) and can be retrieved any time in the
testflow.
Refer to the section Surge tracker in FVI16 other specifications for specification data of
the surge tracker.
Voltage surge tracker
FVI16 features two comparators for the voltage surge tracker:
High-resolution voltage comparator
The surge tracker in high-resolution voltage sensing mode uses the voltage
measure values of the digital control loop as input. The voltage threshold values are
independent of the actual measure range. The same value can be maintained over a
complete test suite or testflow regardless of the used measure range.
High-speed voltage comparator
The surge tracker in high-speed voltage sensing mode utilizes the TMU comparator
inputs. The TMU pogo pins must be wired on the DUT board for using the high
speed voltage comparator. In high-power mode of the PMU, the available threshold
range depends on the programmed compliance voltage. in high-voltage mode of
the PMU, the threshold range depends on the programmed output voltage. For
detailed information, refer to High-speed comparator inputs in FVI16 TMU
specifications.

Current surge tracker
The surge tracker in current sensing mode uses the current measure values of the digital
control loop as input. The current threshold values are independent of the actual
measure range. The same value can be maintained over a complete test suite or testflow
regardless of the used measure range.
Application notes
TMU and surge tracker
The TMU (Time measurement unit) and the surge tracker cannot be used in parallel.
The two functionalities use the same comparators that can be assigned to only one
of them at the same time.
Surge tracker is silently disabled in temporarily unganged mode
Note that on AVI64, DPS128/64, and FVI16 you cannot execute a current compare on
a ganged group of channels if the group is in unganged mode. Already activated
comparators are silently disabled in unganged mode. A user notification (Error or
warning) is omitted in this case, to avoid any interrupt in the testflow. The previous
state of the comparators is automatically restored after the ganged group has been
restored.

FVI16 time measurement unit (TMU)
The FVI16 card features a time measurement unit (TMU) per channel that is available in
the PMU operating mode.
The TMU allows you to accurately measure frequency, period length, pulse width, rise
and fall times, and propagation delay of periodic and non‑periodic output signals.
The TMU measures the time elapsed between the arming (activation of the TMU) and
the occurrence of a certain event. Events are defined by a slope (rising or falling edge) of
the DUT signal, and by a threshold. The event occurs at every rising or falling slope of
the DUT signal when the threshold is crossed.
An upgrade license is required for all TMU measurements. For more information, refer to
Licensing in FVI16 specific setup tasks.
Topic 152703

TMU characteristics
The following items must be considered when using the TMU:
The TMU is supported in the PMU operating mode.
The TMU is not supported in the DPS operating mode.
For ganged pins, the time measurement unit (TMU) is supported but only the
high‑speed voltage comparator and the high‑resolution voltage comparator of the
PMU can be used. The measurement is performed on the master channel. The
high‑resolution current comparator of the PMU is not supported.
The default connection set must be used for TMU measurements.
The TMU uses features that are designed for digital pins. Therefore, the DC Scale
specific connection sets cannot be used. TMU measurements can be applied only
on pins defined in the default connection set.
For more information regarding the default connection set refer to Digital Pins
editor and DFPN, DFPN?.

TMU block diagram
The following drawing highlights the complete TMU structure in the FVI16 block
diagram.

TMU front end
The TMU input signal is derived from the voltage at the TMU_H# pin or the ADC values
of the PMU. The TMU features the high-speed comparator and high-resolution
comparators. All comparators are window comparators with two programmable
thresholds.
High-speed voltage comparator
The channel compares the DUT output voltage with high bandwidth and tracking
slew rate against VOL and VOH thresholds. The threshold voltages are referenced to
the channel specific ground sense pin LS#.
Both the TMU_H# pin and the TMU_L# pin needs to be wired on the DUT board as
shown in FVI16 TMU pogo pins if the high‑speed voltage comparator should be
used.
In high-power mode of the PMU, the available threshold range depends on the
programmed compliance voltage. in high‑voltage mode of the PMU, the threshold
range depends on the programmed output voltage. For detailed information, refer
to High-speed comparator inputs in FVI16 TMU specifications.
The high‑speed voltage comparator features
a switchable hysteresis of about 25 mV and
a programmable hold-off time that can be set to 0.0 ... 20.475 µs.
Note  Comparator events that occur within the programmed hold-off time will
be ignored regardless of the selected TMU measurement mode. For more
information, refer to FVI16 TMU measurement modes.
High‑resolution comparators of the PMU
The channel compares the DUT voltage or current with the full PMU single shot
accuracy and limited bandwidth against the two thresholds:
Voltage compare: The threshold voltages are referenced to the voltage that is
measured differentially between the high sense pin HS# and the channel
specific ground sense pin LS#. This compare mode supports all voltage
measurement ranges of the PMU.
Current compare: The channel compares the DUT output current with full
PMU single shot accuracy and limited bandwidth against ICL and ICH
thresholds. This compare mode supports all current measurement ranges of
the PMU.

Hysteresis and sample frequency of the high‑resolution
comparators
The high-resolution comparators feature a programmable hysteresis that is defined in
percent of the measurement range. Half of the resulting value is symmetrically applied
to the programmed thresholds:
A programmed threshold of 15 V and 1 % hysteresis in the ±30 V range results in a
difference of 0.3 V.
The effective thresholds are
15.15 V for the rising edge and
14.85 V for the falling edge.
A programmed threshold of -2.0 mA and 5 % hysteresis in the ±3 mA range results
in a difference of 0.15 mA.
The effective thresholds are
-1.925 mA for the rising edge and
-2.075 mA for the falling edge.
A programmed threshold of 50 V and 3 % hysteresis in the -60 ... +120 V range
results in a difference of 3.6 V.
The effective thresholds are
51.8 V for the rising edge and
48.2 V for the falling edge.
The hysteresis calculation for the -60 ... +120 V range uses always 120 V as range
regardless of the polarity of the threshold.
The sample frequency of the ADCs used for the high-resolution comparators is 1 MHz.
Interpolation between two samples provides an optimized resolution of 5 ns.
Measurement filters
FVI16 channels feature programmable anti‑aliasing, low‑pass measurement filters for all
ADCs.
For available filters, refer to
Measurement filters in FVI16 programming - Measure voltages or
Measurement filters in FVI16 programming - Measure currents.

Note  The high-resolution comparators of the TMU utilize the continuous data
stream of the ADCs. The measurement filter setting has therefore also an effect on
the TMU measurements.
For high-speed TMU measurements using the high-resolution comparators, we
therefore recommend setting the measurement filter to the maximum value.

FVI16 voltage drop measurement
The FVI16 card features a voltage drop measurement (or Kelvin measurement) unit per
channel.
Voltage drop measurement means that the voltage drop on the force lines is monitored
during high current tests. The measured value can be read back and is also used to
trigger the disconnection of a channel if the user defined limit is exceeded.
The voltage drop measurement (or Kelvin measurement) unit monitors the voltage drop
on the HF# line and on the LF# line. The continuously measured voltage is compared
against a programmable limit. An alarm flag is set for a channel that exceeds the
programmed limit. If the channel is set to the 3 A or 10 A range, it is immediately
disconnected to protect the probes.
The voltage drop measurement unit is supported only for the High‑power mode.
For ganged channels, voltage drop measurements are uploaded only from the master
channel. However, continuous monitoring of the voltage drop is active on all channels
and the entire ganging group is disconnected if only one channel exceeds the threshold.
For information on how to setup a voltage drop measurement, refer to FVI16
programming - Voltage drop measurement.
Topic 355298
1)

Operating principle
Monitoring the voltage drop with the voltage drop measurement unit ensures that the
force connections to the DUT have a sufficiently low resistance for the programmed
current. It also ensures that there is enough voltage headroom left for proper work of
the power stage.
The following drawing shows an example of an optional voltage drop measurement that
is carried out in preparation for a subsequent high current test. The programmed test
current of 1 A will not damage the probes in case the contact resistance exceeds the
assumed value of 100 mΩ.
The voltage drop on the force lines HF# and LF# is rated from the pogo pin to the F-S
connection on the DUT board or at the DUT pins. The internal voltage drop needs not to
be considered.
Note  The resistance of the force lines is defined by the contact resistance of the
pogo pins, the traces on the DUT board, and by the DUT socket or probes.
Contaminated pogo pads and DUT sockets or insufficient contact pressure of the
probes may significantly increase the voltage drop.
CAUTION A sufficiently low contact resistance of the sense connections is a
precondition for a reliable Kelvin measurement. We therefore strongly recommend
performing a sense connection tests once per test run using the FVI16 Kelvin test
unit.
For information on how to use the voltage drop measurement unit, refer to FVI16
programming - Voltage drop measurement.

Specific design rules
Specific design rules must be followed when designing a new DUT board and assigning
FVI16 channels:
FVI16 power budget and energy budget: The available power and energy budgets
must be considered when assigning FVI16 channels to DUT pins. The available
power budget and energy budget on FVI16 cards is defined as follows:
The maximum total power budget is 400 W.
The maximum total energy budget is 3.2 J.
The two budgets are equally distributed to two channel groups 1 … 8 and
9 … 16 providing 200 W and 1.6 J per group.
Within the two groups, the budgets are shared by all eight channels.
Pin assignment for Fast Sync / Fast Match: For fast local synchronization, the
synchronized DUT pins must be assigned to the same group of channels
respectively to the same test processor.
HV (High-Voltage) protection: Since the FVI16 card may be connected to low-
voltage cards via defective DUTs or unintentionally closed connections, we
recommend that you implement a HV (High-Voltage) protection circuitry on your
DUT boards to protect the low-voltage cards.

FVI16 operating modes
The FVI16 channels feature the PMU operating mode and the DPS operating mode.
The FVI16 operating mode is defined by the pin type that has been selected in the Pin
setting editors. The operating mode can be set individually for each channel of the card.
The combination of the operating mode and the selected connection state defines the
characteristics, the dynamic behavior, and the basic programming mode of the channels.
PMU operating mode
An FVI16 channel is configured for the PMU operating mode if the channel is defined as
DC Scale pin using the Digital Pins editor. In PMU operating mode, the channel is used
like a standard PMU to temporarily supply power during the execution of a single test
suite or a group of test suites. An FVI16 channel in PMU operating mode is programmed
using test methods and APIs. The connection state is set by additional parameters in the
level setup or by APIs.
DPS operating mode
An FVI16 channel is configured to operate in DPS mode if it is defined as a device power
supply using the DPS Pins editor. In DPS mode, the channel behaves like a DPS-slot
device power supply and is normally used to supply devices with power during the
execution of a testflow. An FVI16 channel in DPS operating mode takes part in the
standard connect and disconnect sequences and is programmed using DPS primary
sets.
Supported features in DPS operating mode and PMU
operating mode
The PMU functionality including the AWG and DGT mode is supported in the DPS
operating mode and in the PMU operating. Some other features are supported only in
the PMU operating mode.
The following features are supported only in the PMU operating mode and not in the
DPS operating mode:
Stacking and ganging on the fly
Time measurement unit (TMU)

FVI16 in DPS operating mode
In DPS operating mode, an FVI16 channel behaves like a DPS-slot device power supply
and is used to supply devices with power during the execution of a testflow.
An FVI16 channel is configured to operate in DPS mode if it is defined as a device power
supply using the DPS Pins editor.
To find a summary of all supported resource parameters in the level file, refer to
DPSPINS resources.
Characteristics
The channel is typically used for DPS applications to supply the DUT. The channel
provides a positive or negative voltage up to the programmed clamp current and is
programmed using DPS primary sets. Programming an FVI16 channel by DC events is
also supported.
An FVI16 channel in DPS operating mode supports the PMU functionality including
the AWG and DGT mode.
An FVI16 channel in DPS operating mode does not support
the high-voltage mode (-60 V ... +120 V),
the time measurement unit (TMU),
"ganging on the fly", and
software‑controlled "stacking" and "stacking on the fly".
The pulsed operating mode is not supported in the DPS operating mode with
activated power budget management. The FVI16 channels can consume only the
available power budget for DC operation in the DPS operating mode. The
maximum power budget for DC operation is 200 W per group of eight channels.
Note  The assessed power of the individual channels is defined by the
compliance voltage and the programmed clamp or force current. The assessed
power includes therefore the power consumption of the main driver, the power
consumption that is caused by the voltage drop on the force and return line
and finally the power that is available at the DUT.

Connection state
The connection state defines the behavior of the channel in the DPS operating mode.
The following connection states are supported:
norm
ungang
himp
The connection states FAST and PULSE are supported for compatibility with the DC
Scale PVI8 card but FVI16 stays in the norm connection state if FAST or PULSE are
selected.
Refer to the FVI16 programming - DPS operating mode for the information how to set
the connection state.

Connecting and disconnecting channels in DPS operating
mode
An FVI16 channel behaves like a DPS-slot device power supply when connecting and
disconnecting channels in DPS operating mode.
When connected, the channel forces the programmed voltage. The current is limited to
the programmed clamp current.
Unlike other DC Scale cards in DPS operating mode, an FVI16 channel in DPS operating
mode needs not to be disconnected for changing the force voltage range or the force
current range. FVI16 supports changing the voltage force range and current force range
in connected state both for the DPS operating mode and for the PMU operating mode.

FVI16 in PMU operating mode
In PMU operating mode, an FVI16 channel is used like a standard PMU to temporarily
supply power during the execution of a single test suite or a group of test suites.
Configuration
An FVI16 channel is configured for the PMU operating mode if the channel is defined as
a DC Scale pin using the Digital Pins editor.
Characteristics
An FVI16 channel in PMU operating mode is typically used for VI applications. The
channel provides a positive or negative voltage or current up to the programmed clamp
current or voltage and is basically programmed using test methods and APIs.
The static and dynamic behavior is defined by a combination of the connection state,
the measurement mode, and the execution mode as described below. For more
information refer to the FVI16 programming - PMU operating mode.
Topic 152707

FVI16 block diagram
Measurement mode
The measurement mode defines the force mode and the measurement mode of the
channel when it is configured for the PMU operating mode. For more information and a
list of all supported measurement modes, refer to FVI16 programming - PMU operating
mode.

Execution mode
The execution mode defines the measurement behavior of the channel when it is
configured for the PMU operating mode. For more information refer to
SPMU_PIN_TASK.execMode().
The following execution modes are supported:
"SER": Serial measurements are performed per device, but in multisite tests
multiple sites are tested in parallel whenever possible.
"PAR": Parallel measurements are performed per device and on all sites whenever
possible.
Connecting and disconnecting channels in PMU operating
mode
An FVI16 channel in PMU operating mode does not take part in standard connect and
disconnect sequences and cannot take part in the set activation, although the channel
can be added to user-defined connect and disconnect sequences.
Unlike other DC Scale cards in DPS operating mode, an FVI16 channel in PMU operating
mode needs not to be disconnected for changing the force voltage range or the force
current range. FVI16 supports changing the voltage force range and current force range
in connected state both for the DPS operating mode and for the PMU operating mode.

FVI16 force, clamp, and measure voltages
The FVI16 card features a PMU per channel for forcing, clamping, and measuring
voltages. The PMUs provide five combined force, clamp, and measure voltage ranges.
FVI16 modes
FVI16 channels feature two modes that define the usable voltage and current ranges:
High‑power mode:
This mode provides four voltage ranges from ± 3 V to ± 60 V and seven current
ranges from ±30 μA to ±10 A. Continuous operation is supported up to a current of
±3 A. Currents up to ±10 A are supported in pulsed operation. The following
voltage and current ranges are supported:
Voltage ranges: ± 3 V, ± 10 V, ± 30 V, ± 60 V
Current ranges: ± 30 μA, ± 300 μA, ± 3 mA, ± 30 mA, ± 300 mA, ± 3 A, ± 10 A
High‑voltage mode:
This mode provides a single voltage range -60 V ... +120 V and four current ranges
from ±30 μA to ±30 mA:
Voltage range: -60 V ... +120 V
Current ranges: ± 30 μA, ± 300 μA, ± 3 mA, ± 30 mA
FVI16 channels must be disconnected before they are changed from the high‑power
mode to the high‑voltage mode and vice versa.
The voltage and current ranges are common for forcing, clamping, and measuring
voltages or currents with the PMU. The force or clamp range is always the same as the
measurement range.
For power diagrams of the two modes, refer to FVI16 voltage and current capability
specifications.
Topic 152708
1)

Forcing or clamping voltage
The FVI16 PMUs are digitally regulated VI supplies with remote sense lines. Each channel
features it's own return path and is fully floating. The output voltage is referenced to the
channel specific low sense pin of each channel.
The digital controller of a PMU in force voltage mode will adjust the control value so
that the voltage between the high sense pogo pin (HS#) and the low sense pogo pin
(LS#) is equal to the programmed voltage as long as the output current stays within the
programmed clamp current limits.
The digital controller of a PMU in force current mode will adjust the control value so
that the output current at the high force pogo pin (HF#) is equal to the programmed
current as long as the voltage between the high sense pogo pin (HS#) and the low sense
pogo pin (LS#) stays within the programmed clamp voltage limits.
For more information refer to FVI16 force and clamp voltages.
Measuring voltage
The voltage is measured differentially between the high sense pogo pin (HS#) and the
low sense pogo pin (LS#). The digital controller measures voltages and currents
continuously, uses the measured values as feedback for the control loop, and provides
the measured values for software controlled or pattern controlled measurements.
For more information refer to FVI16 measure voltages.
High-impedance voltage measurement mode (HIMP)
A high-impedance operation mode is available. This mode is used to measure the
voltage with no voltage or current applied. The force output is switched to a high-
impedance mode. The voltage is measured differentially between the high sense pogo
pin (HS#) and the low sense pogo pin (LS#).
Note  The low force (LF_#) pin must still be connected in the high-impedance
voltage measurement mode for correct common mode operation of the LS_# pin
versus the LF# pin.

Power budget
The FVI16 card comprises a limited power budget and features on-board energy
storages for delivering the energy for high-power pulses. The utilization of the power
budget and the charging state of the on-board energy storages is constantly monitored.
Warning flags are set in case the utilization of the power budget or the charging state of
the energy storages reaches a critical level. An error message is issued and the involved
channel or channels are disconnected if the power budget or energy budget is
exceeded. The programmed force or clamp current and the programmed compliance
voltage are used to calculate the utilization of the available budgets.
For more information, refer to FVI16 power budget and energy budget

1)

Compliance voltage
FVI16 channels in high‑power mode feature a programmable compliance voltage. The
compliance voltage is the voltage to which the raw power supply of a channel is set. The
programmable range of the compliance voltage is +10 V ... +65 V.
Two competing rules must be observed when setting the compliance voltage:
The maximum output voltage of the channel is limited by the programmed
compliance voltage.
The compliance voltage has an effect on the power dissipation of the main driver
and the consumed energy and should be set as low as possible.
The recommended compliance voltage can be calculated as follows:
VCompliance = 2.5 V + 1 Ω * IForce/Clamp + VForce drop + VReturn
drop + VDUT/Clamp
where VCompliance = Compliance voltage to be set
VForce drop = Maximum voltage drop on the high force line
VReturn drop = Maximum voltage drop on the return / low force line
VDUT/Clamp = Force voltage mode: Forced voltage
Force current mode: Clamp voltage
IForce/Clamp = Force voltage mode: Clamp current
Force current mode: Forced current
SmarTest shows the recommended compliance value in the UI report window if the
programmed compliance voltage is lower than the recommended voltage.
See also the FVI16 Kelvin measurement unit specifications for the programmable range
of the voltage drop. If the voltage drop is not programmed, default values as defined in
the APIs linked in FVI16 programming - Voltage drop measurement are used.
CAUTION  Compliance voltage dependent oscillation
An FVI16 channel driving a resistive load may oscillate under the following
conditions if the compliance voltage is set too high:
Compliance voltage > (DUT voltage + 30 V) 
Current flow > 100 mA and < 2 A
Load capacitance < 47 nF
To avoid oscillation under the above conditions, set the compliance voltage as low
as possible.
2)

Minimum clamp voltage distance
An FVI16 PMU needs a minimum distance between the positive and negative clamp
voltage to avoid oscillation. For more information, refer to the Minimum clamp voltage
distance section in FVI16 programming - Force and clamp voltages.
Dynamic behavior in force voltage or clamp voltage mode
An FVI16 PMU features some filters that can be used to modify the dynamic behavior.
For available filters, refer to the Dynamic behavior section in FVI16 programming - Force
and clamp currents.
Load step response
The load step response of an FVI16 channel depends on the selected filters, the actual
current range, the impedance of the high force and low force traces on the DUT board,
and on the capacitive load on the DUT board.
The selected voltage bandwidth and the set load capacitance value have an effect
on the load step response for an FVI16 channel that is forcing or clamping voltage.
The selected current bandwidth has an effect on the load step response for an
FVI16 channel that is forcing or clamping current.
Voltage sense lines
The forced or clamped voltage is measured differentially between the high sense pogo
pin (HS#) and the low sense pogo pin (LS#). The measured value is the voltage feedback
value for the digital controllers and is used to adjust the forced or clamped voltage.
Refer to Voltage sense lines in FVI16 measure voltages for a detailed description of the
voltage sense lines.
The voltage difference between HF# and HS# and between LF# and LS# must not
exceed ±7 V. The voltage difference between the force pins and sense pins is typically
caused by voltage drop produced by current flow over parasitic resistances on the DUT
board. An active FVI16 channel that violates this rule will be disconnected. For more
information, refer to FVI16 Kelvin measurement unit specifications and to FVI16 voltage
drop measurement.

DC Scale voltage limits
The FVI16 card supports the DC Scale voltage and current limits. Both SmarTest and the
control logic of the FVI16 card ensure that the defined voltage and current limits cannot
be exceeded by programming higher or lower force or clamp values.
Note  At FVI16, the DC Scale voltage limits are applied to the output stage DAC.
The set limits are therefore independent of the voltage measured differentially
between the HS# and LS# pogo pins.
Since the measured voltage feedback has no effect, the voltage drop on both the
high force line and the low force line must be added to the DC Scale voltage limits.
We recommend setting the DC Scale voltage limits at least the sum of the
programmed maximum voltage drops (Force + return line) higher than the
maximum programmed force or clamp voltage.
The defined DC Scale voltage limit ensures that the forced voltage cannot exceed the
DUT specific voltage limits for abnormal operating conditions. The following examples
for abnormal operating conditions are covered by the DC Scale voltage limits:
An irregular operating sequence of external switches such as the PMUX01 Power
MUX or relays causes that a sense line temporarily is tied to another DUT pin than
the related force pin. This will result in a high output voltage if the DC Scale voltage
limits are not set.
A user defined test method calculates a force value that exceeds the compliance
range of the DUT.

Dynamic range switching
The FVI16 PMU features dynamic force and measurement range switching. The
combined force and measurement ranges can be changed without disconnecting and
connecting a channel.
This feature is supported for the API based (static) programming and for programming
by DC events in pattern.
The dynamic current range switching minimizes the glitches when changing the current
force and measurement range of an already connected channel. The dynamic current
range switching can therefore easily be used to implement IDDQ tests or similar tests
