setting up the DUT in a higher current range.

Automatic down-ranging
FVI16 channels feature automatic down-ranging for current measurements.
Automatic down-ranging means that the current range is automatically changed to the
best fit range for the measurement and restored to the original range after the
measurement.
Two parameters define whether the automatic down-ranging is performed or not:
1. The force / clamp current range:
Can be set explicitly or (if not defined)
is automatically derived from the forced or clamped value.
2. The current measurement range:
Can be set explicitly or (if not defined)
is automatically derived from the pass/fail thresholds.
Automatic down-ranging is performed only if the current measurement range is lower
than the force / clamp current range regardless whether the ranges have been set
explicitly or have been selected automatically.
With automatic down‑ranging active, the next lower current range is activated only if
the measured current does not exceed 90 % of the next lower current range.
Automatic down-ranging is supported for both code‑based programming using the
SPMU_TASK and DPS_TASK test method APIs and the pattern‑based programming using
the DC events and is also supported by SmartRDI.

FVI16 power budget and energy budget
The FVI16 card comprises limited power budgets and features on-board energy
storages for delivering the energy for high-power pulses. SmarTest limits the overall
power usage of an FVI16 card and the power-usage of the individual FVI16 channels to
the maximum available power and energy.
Topic 152719

Power budget
The power budget of an FVI16 card is defined as follows:
The maximum total power budget is 400 W.
This budget is equally distributed to two channel groups 1 … 8 and 9 … 16
providing 200 W per group.
Within the two groups, the power budget is shared by all eight channels.
The power budget applies to all DC operations in PMU operating mode and in DPS
operating mode. The power budget applies also for re-charging the on-board energy
storages for pulsed operation.
Note  The assessed power of the individual channels is defined as follows:
Force voltage mode: Compliance voltage * programmed clamp current in force
voltage
Force current mode: Compliance voltage * programmed force current
The compliance voltage is the voltage to which the raw power supply of the channel
is set.
The assessed power includes therefore the power consumption of the main driver,
the power consumption that is caused by the voltage drop on the force and return
line and finally the power that is available at the DUT.
A status flag will be set and all eight channels of the related group will be disconnected
if the total power budget of the group is exceeded. For more information, refer to Low
headroom in FVI16 status flags.

Energy budget
The FVI16 channels are able to deliver a multiple of the DC power in the pulsed mode.
The energy for the high current pulses is provided by two on-board energy storages.
The available energy budget of an FVI16 card is defined as follows:
The maximum total energy budget is 3.2 J.
This budget is equally distributed to two channel groups 1 … 8 and 9 … 16
providing 1.6 J per group.
Within the two groups, the power budget is shared by all eight channels.
Note  The assessed energy of the individual channels is defined as follows:
Force voltage mode: Compliance voltage × programmed clamp current × pulse
time
Force current mode: Compliance voltage × programmed force current × pulse
time
The compliance voltage is the voltage to which the raw power supply of the channel
is set.
The assessed energy includes therefore the power consumption of the main driver,
the power consumption that is caused by the voltage drop on the force and return
line and finally the power that is available at the DUT.
The maximum energy budget is available only if the on-board energy storages are fully
charged.
A warning flag will be set if the consumed energy budget reaches a critical level. For
more information, refer to Power budget 1 in FVI16 status flags.
All eight channels of the related group will be disconnected if the energy storage has
been discharged or cannot be recharged from the available power budget. The flag Low
headroom will be set in this case.
1)

Duty cycle and recharging of the on-board energy storages
The ratio of the maximum pulse power and the available power budget results in a duty
cycle of about 10 % for high current pulses.
The on-board energy storages are recharged only if the power budget is not fully
utilized by the channels of the related group. Recharging the 1.6 J of a fully discharged
energy storage needs maximum 15 ms if the complete power budget is available.
We recommend, checking the charging state of the on‑board energy storages before
current pulses are driven that exceed the available power budget. The status flag
"Battery full" will be set if the related energy storage is fully charged. For more
information, refer to flag Battery full in FVI16 status flags.
Power budget management
As noted above, all channels of an eight channel group will be disconnected if the total
power budget or energy budget of the group is exceeded.
The power budget management allows you assigning power budget or energy budget
to individual channels according to the needs of the testflow. If the power budget
management is activated, only channels that exceed the assigned budget will be
disconnected.
The power budget management is enabled by default.
For more information, refer to FVI16 power budget management.

FVI16 power budget management
The power budget management of FVI16 allows you assigning power budget or energy
budget to individual channels according to the needs of the testflow. Only channels that
exceed an assigned budget will be disconnect if the power budget management
functionality is activated.
 One J (Joule) corresponds to the derived unit of one Ws (Watt-second). One Ws is the
energy equivalent to the power of one watt sustained for one second.
 The Java Runtime Environment (JRE) must already be installed.
1)
2)
Topic 346267

The available budgets of an FVI16 card are defined as follows:
The maximum total power budget is 400 W.
The maximum total energy budget is 3.2 J.
The two budgets are equally distributed to two channel groups 1 … 8 and 9 … 16
providing 200 W and 1.6 J per group.
Within the two groups, the budgets are shared by all eight channels.
Power budget management
Managing the power budget means that you can assign power budget or energy
budget to individual channels:
The assigned power budget and energy budget can be changed at any position in
the flow.
The utilization of the assigned budgets is constantly monitored.
Only channels that exceed an assigned budget are disconnected.
Power budget or energy budget violations caused by failing DUTs are therefore isolated
and have no effect on passing sites.
Reset state
The power budget management is activated by default.
In reset state, the power budget and energy budget is equally distributed to all
channels. The default values are therefore defined as follows:
Default power budget per channel in PMU operating mode: 25 W
Default power budget per channel in DPS operating mode: 0 W if disconnected
Default energy budget per channel in PMU operating mode: 200 mJ
2)
2)

Calculating the budget utilization: High‑power mode
The utilization of the budgets is calculated at run-time by the on‑board controller. The
following channel specific parameters define the utilization of the power budget:
The programmed compliance voltage of the channel and
the programmed clamp current (VF mode) or programmed force current (IF mode).
In PMU operating mode, current pulses that exceed the assigned power budget
contribute to the utilization of the energy budget. The utilization of the energy budget is
defined by the calculated power, as defined above, and the timing of the pulse. The
assessed pulse time is the time span where the programmed compliance voltage and
the programmed current (force current or clamp current) are set to the target value.
Slew rate and force filter settings are ignored for the pulse time.
CAUTION The required power and consumed energy is always calculated from
the programmed values:
The power is calculated from
the programmed compliance voltage of the channel and
the programmed clamp current (VF mode) or programmed force current (IF
mode).
The consumed energy is calculated from the calculated power and the time
span where the programmed compliance voltage and the programmed current
are set to the target value. Slew rate and force filter settings are ignored for the
pulse time.
CAUTION In force voltage mode, the required power is always calculated from
the programmed clamp current even if the real current flowing is lower than the
programmed current. We recommend therefore, setting the clamp current to the
lowest possible value.
For minimizing the consumed energy, the clamp should be set to the high target
value only for the short time where the current is really required.

Calculating the budget utilization: High‑voltage
mode or HIZ mode
In high‑voltage mode or high‑impedance voltage measure mode, the utilization of the
budget is calculated as follows:
Power budget: The utilized power budget is not monitored in these modes but a
minimum power budget of 4.0 W must be assigned.
Energy budget: Channels in these modes cannot utilize the energy budget. The
assigned energy budget can be set to 0.0 J.
Budget utilization for the PMU and DPS operating mode
The evaluation of the budget utilization differs for FVI16 channels in PMU operating
mode and in DPS operating mode:
PMU operating mode DPS operating mode
Power budget for DC operation and energy budget for
pulsed tests can be assigned.
Only power budget for DC operation can be utilized.
Channels in PMU operating mode contribute to the
power budget utilization all the time, whether
connected or not.
Channels contribute to the power budget utilization
only if they are connected.
The assigned power budget and energy budget can be
changed at any position in the flow.
The power budget for connected channels is calculated
from the active DPS set, automatically acquired and
considered for the overall power budget utilization.
The compliance voltage can be set by an API to
minimize the utilized power budget and consumed
energy.
The compliance voltage is set automatically based on
the programmed voltage, current and maximum
voltage drop on the force and return line. For more
information, refer to FVI16 in DPS operating mode in
FVI16 programming - Force and clamp voltages.

Managing the budgets in PMU operating mode
The power budget and energy budget must be adapted to the needs of the testflow for
optimizing the performance and minimizing the test time.
Some hints for optimizing the utilization of the budgets:
The assigned budgets of a disconnected channel in PMU operating mode must be
set to 0 W and 0 J to reuse the budgets for other channels.
A virtual, channel specific energy storage reflects the assigned energy budget.
Assigned power budget that is not used due to lower settings of the channel or a
disconnected channel will automatically be used to recharge the virtual, channel
specific energy storage.
The charging state of a virtual energy storage is calculated and monitored in
connected and disconnected mode.
Note  For high-current pulses, we recommend increasing not only the assigned
energy budget but also the assigned power budget. The assigned power budget
increases the total available energy and enables a channel forcing higher currents for
a longer time.
Status flags
Several status flags are available to report errors or critical conditions.
Refer to section Power budget monitoring and status flags in FVI16 programming -
Power budget management.

In PMU operating mode, the assigned energy budget corresponds to a virtual, channel
specific energy storage. This energy storage can be charged and discharged like the
physical on‑board energy storages for the two channel groups channel groups 1 … 8
and 9 … 16:
An empty virtual energy storage results in disconnection of the related channel.
The ratio of the assigned and required power budget defines whether the virtual
energy storage is charged or discharged:
Required power < Assigned power budget: Virtual energy storage is charged.
Required power > Assigned power budget: Virtual energy storage is
discharged.
The time for charging the virtual energy storage depends on the assigned energy
budget and the available power budget:
Big energy budget and small power budget: Long time.
Small energy budget and big power budget: Short time.
Some time for charging the energy storage is also required if the assigned energy
budget is increased at runtime.
The time for charging a virtual energy storage can be calculated as follows:
time = energy / power
with energy = Energy in Joule or Watt-second to charge
power = Assigned and available power in Watt
time = The time in seconds to increase or decrease the charging level of the virtual energy
storage to the new energy level
The formula above applies only for the virtual energy storages with enabled power
budget management. For recharging the physical energy storage of an
eight‑channel group, the tolerance in capacitance must be considered. Recharging
the 1.6 J of a fully discharged physical energy storage needs maximum 15 ms if the
complete power budget of 200 W is available.
Note  All the power budget that is available after supplying all channels will be
used to recharge the on-board energy storage of the related eight‑channel group
until it is fully charged. Properly assigning the power budget to the channels will
minimize the time for recharging the on-board energy storages.

Offline power and energy analyzer
We provide an analyzer that helps you offline calculating the utilization of the power
and energy budget. The HTML page supports defining and calculating all relevant
parameters for handling the two budgets. For more information and the download link,
refer to section Offline power and energy analyzer - FVI16 PowerAnalyst in FVI16 power
budget and energy budget.
Example
Typical sequence
The following diagram shows how the budget utilization is calculated for a typical
sequence:
The state of labels 1 to 9 is defined as follows:

1. The initial state: Compliance voltage is 10 V and the force current is 1 A. This results
in a calculated power of 10 W that is covered by 25 W that are assigned per default.
The overhead of 15 W is used to charge the virtual energy storage of the channel.
2. The assigned power budget is increased to 80 W. The virtual energy storage can be
charged by 70 W.
3. The compliance voltage is increased to 50 V that results in a required power of
50 W. The maximum power to charge the virtual energy storage is 30 W.
4. The programmed current is increased to 5 A. This results in a required power of
50 V * 5 A = 250 W. The virtual energy storage is now discharged by
250 W (required) - 80 W (assigned) = -170 W. The channel will be disconnected if a
charging level of 0 % is reached.
5. The programmed current is decreased to 0 A resulting in a required power of 0 W.
The assigned power of 80 W is now used to recharge the virtual energy storage.
6. The assigned power budget is set to 0 W to reuse the power for other channels of
the group. The charging level of the virtual, channel specific energy storage is no
more changed.
7. The compliance voltage is reset to the minimum value of +10 V. The forced current
has already been set to 0 A and therefore, minimizing the compliance voltage has
no more effect on the calculated power.
8. The two areas (8a) and (8b) show the difference between the programmed current
and the applied current if very low slew rates or filter settings are set:
(8a) on the rising edge means that the calculated values are higher than the
really required power and consumed energy.
(8b) on the falling edge means that the calculated values are lower than the
really required power or consumed energy.

In best case, the consumed energy of the falling edge that is defined by (8b) is
equal to the unused energy of the rising edge that is defined by (8a). In worst case,
if the slew rate or filter settings of the falling edge are much more lower, the
consumed energy of the falling edge is not compensated by the unused energy of
the rising edge, the physical energy storage of the related group may be
discharged too much and all channels of the related group may be disconnected.
For reliable power budget management, we recommend therefore always using
high slew rates and filter settings. For a more information and a workaround see
application note Using low slew rates or force filter settings in FVI16 programming -
Power budget management.

User Operating Point
The operating point of a channel that is defined by the needs of your testflow or your
DUT respectively is to be entered in this section.
Enter the desired DUT voltage and the desired DUT current. The desired DUT
power is calculated automatically from these two values.
Note  For the force voltage mode, you should enter the programmed clamp
current as desired DUT current. For the force current mode, you should enter
the programmed clamp voltage as desired DUT voltage. For minimizing the
calculated (and consumed) power and energy, set the clamp values as low as
possible for a reliable test.
Enter the desired pulse length based on DUT requirements.
The maximum pulse length that can be processed by the FVI16 PowerAnalyst is
10 ms. Longer times must be treated as DC test by enabling the DC check box.
Enter the force kelvin resistance and the return kelvin resistance. The two values
define the resistance from the pogo pins to the DUT. The FVI16 voltage drop
measurement unit allows you measuring the force/return voltage drop at a defined
test current to determine the resistance.
Invalid settings such are highlighted in red. You can use units like "mV", "mA", "us" or
"mΩ" to enter the values on this area.

FVI16 Channel Conditions
This section holds internal setups of the FVI16 channels.
Enter the forceDropMax voltage and the returnDropMax voltage. The two values
define the maximum voltage drop on the force line and the return line from the
pogo pins to the DUT. We recommend setting values minimum 250 mV above the
required value to avoid disconnection of channels.
Note  The FVI16 PowerAnalyst cannot consider all combinations of the given
parameters. When defining the maximum voltage drops, you must therefore
also take into account the maximum voltage drop defined in the FVI16 Kelvin
measurement unit specifications. This applies to DUT voltages > 7 V in the 10 V
range and for DUT voltages > 48.5 V in the 60 V range.
Enter the assigned dcPowerBudget in Watt (W) and the pulseEnergyBudget in
Joule (J). Default values are 25 W and 200 mJ per channel. You must decrease
these values for other channels if more power or energy is required. The maximum
total values are 200 W and 1.6 J per group of eight channels.
Invalid settings such as exceeding the available budgets for power and energy are
highlighted in red.

FVI16 Channel Operating Point
The section shows calculated values that define the operating point of the channel.
voltage: The output voltage of the power stage includes the desired DUT voltage,
the forceDropMax voltage and the returnDropMax voltage.
compliance voltage: The value defines the desired supply voltage of the power
stage. Some headroom is required for the closed loop control. This voltage is
therefore always some volts higher than the output voltage of the power stage. The
maximum programmable compliance voltage is 65 V.
After activating the check box for the compliance voltage, you can define your
own value.
Note  The calculated or user defined compliance voltage must be programmed
using the related API. Programming a different compliance voltage may cause
the channel to disconnect as more power and energy is consumed, or
headroom for the power stage is insufficient.
The actual power dissipation of the output stages is constantly monitored by
the hardware. A compliance voltage set higher than required increases this
power dissipation Neither the power budget management of the FVI16 nor the
FVI16 PowerAnalyst can take this behavior into account, as it is based on the
actual values and not on programmed values. For more information, refer to
Power dissipation in topic FVI16 pulsed operation.
primary power: The required power is calculated from the desired DUT current
and the compliance voltage.
The primary power therefore includes the desired DUT power and the entire
internal power dissipation for the setup.
pulse energy: To determine the required pulse energy, the difference between the
primary power and the assigned dcPowerBudget is calculated and the result is
multiplied by the desired pulse length.
The following rules apply to the values displayed in this section:
For DC tests, the assigned dcPowerBudget must be higher than or equal to the
primary power.
For pulsed tests, the assigned pulseEnergyBudget must be higher than or equal to
the pulse energy.

The pulse energy is provided by the combination of the assigned dcPowerBudget
and the assigned pulseEnergyBudget. The primary power can therefore be
ignored.
FVI16 Operating Considerations
This section contains information on discharging and recharging the on-board energy
storage.
duty cycle: The nominal duty cycle that is to be applied if the consumed power
exceeds the available power in pulsed operation.
hopper discharge: The percentage of energy take from the on-board energy
storage of the related eight channel group.
pulse recovery time: The calculated time is the maximum of
the time that is defined by the duty cycle and
the time required for recharging the energy storage.
A small dcPowerBudget in combination with a high pulse energy will significantly
increase this time.
Note  The calculated value is valid only if no energy is consumed after the
pulse and the entire assigned dcPowerBudget can be used for recharging the
energy storage.

FVI16 stacked, ganged, or in pulsed operation
Multiple FVI16 channels can be combined by stacking or ganging to get a higher
voltage or a higher current. The FVI16 channels are also able forcing short high-current
pulses.
Stacking
In order to achieve a higher output voltage, serial connection of up to three FVI16
channels is allowed. This is called "stacking". For more information, refer to FVI16
stacked.
Ganging
In order to achieve a higher output current, parallel connection of multiple FVI16
channels in high-power mode is supported. This is called "ganging". For more
information, refer to FVI16 ganged.
Stacking and ganging on the fly
The floating high-current channels of the card are a limited resource and must be
multiplexed to different DUT pins in most applications. This is normally done via
additional relay multiplexers on the DUT board. "Stacking on the fly" and "Ganging on
the fly" means that the group of stacked or ganged channels can be disbanded and the
individual channels can be assigned to other pins of the DUT according to the needs of
the testflow. For more information, refer to FVI16 stacked or ganged on the fly.
Pulsed operation
Each channel of the card is able to force a multiple of the continuous current in pulsed
operation. The energy for such a high current pulse is provided by on-board energy
storages. For more information, refer to FVI16 pulsed operation.

FVI16 stacked
To increase the output voltage, multiple FVI16 channels can be connected in series. This
is called "stacking".
All channels of an FVI card are fully floating, meaning that the channels feature
individual return pins (LF#) and behave like batteries. The return pins can be connected
to DUT ground or any bias voltage that may also be provided by another FVI16 channel.
Stacking
Stacked FVI16 channels can be setup under user control or under software control:
User‑controlled stacking:
Maximum three channels are simply connected in series. Setups and measurement
are programmed individually for each of the stacked channels. Measured voltages
must be added together to get the total voltage of the stack. Special setups are
required for forcing current by stacked channels.
Software‑controlled stacking:
The serial connected channels are defined as stacking group in the pin definitions
of SmarTest. The stacking group is accessed as single pin. The on‑board-stacking
controller distributes the total output voltage equally between the stacked
channels. This solution will show a stable output signal and provides reliable
voltage measurements without applying special setups as required for stacking
under user control.
We recommend therefore, always setting up the software‑controlled stacking.

Stacking characteristics
The following rule applies to both software‑controlled stacking and to stacking under
user control:
Stacking is allowed up to a maximum floating range of ±200 V with respect to the
DUT board ground.
The following items must be considered when using software‑controlled stacking of
FVI16 channels:
Stacking is allowed for any combination of up to three channels within a card.
Stacking is supported only in the high‑power mode. Stacking is not supported in
the high‑voltage mode.
Stacking is not supported for channels that are ganged under software control.
The time measurement unit (TMU) is not supported for software‑controlled
stacking.
The voltage surge tracker is not supported for software‑controlled stacking.
Stacking groups can be disbanded and the individual channels can be assigned
within the same testflow. For more information, refer to FVI16 stacked or ganged
on the fly.
On-board stacking controller
The on-board stacking controller is used to balance the total output voltage between
the stacked channels.
In a stacked configuration, the uppermost channel acts as the master channel. The
master channel feeds the measured voltage to the slaves and each slave uses this value
to adjust its own voltage to be identical with the master's voltage.
1)

DUT board connections
The following connections are required for a stack of two channels:
The high force (HF#) pin and the high sense (HS#) pin of the upper channel must be
connected together at the DUT.
The low force (LF#) pin and the low sense (LS#) pin of the lower channel must be
connected together at a stable reference like ground or the supply voltage of the
DUT.
Low force and low sense of the upper channel and high force and high sense of the
lower channel are to be connected together at a star point.
The same scheme is to be applied for a stack of three channels: Force and sense lines of
the middle channel are to be connected to the other channels via star points to ensure,
that the voltage of the stacked group can be measured correctly.
CAUTION "Upper channel" in this context means towards the DUT while the
"lower channel" means towards a stable reference like ground or the supply voltage
of the DUT. This rule applies both for positive and for negative voltages.
All of the required DUT board connections may be routed via optional relay
multiplexers.
The TMU connections need some more attention for stacked channels:
Pin TMU_L# must always be connected to low force (LF#) pin and the low sense
(LS#) pin of the related channel. A series termination resistor of 50 Ω is mandatory
for the TMU_L# pin.
The TMU_H# pin can be connected to the high force (HF#) and the high sense
(HS#) pin of the related channel. The pin may also be connected to any other DUT
pin as far as the maximum compliance voltage of the TMU_H pin is maintained. For
more information, refer to "High speed comparator inputs (TMU _H / TMU_L)" in
FVI16 TMU specifications.
Note  The ground reference of the TMU comparator thresholds is always the low
sense (LS#) pin.

Ganging
Ganged FVI16 channels can be setup under user control or under software control:
User‑controlled ganging:
Several channels are simply connected in parallel and similar settings are applied.
This can lead to an undefined distribution of the current to the individual channels
and may result in unstable output voltages and invalid current measurements.
Modifying the settings may improve the behavior but needs more attention of the
user.
Software‑controlled ganging:
The parallel connected channels are defined as ganging group in the pin definitions
of SmarTest. The ganging group is accessed as single pin. The on‑board-ganging
controller distributes the total output current equally between the ganged channels.
This solution will show a stable output signal and provides reliable current
measurements without applying special setups as required for ganging under user
control.
We recommend therefore, always setting up software‑controlled ganging.
Ganging characteristics
The following items must be considered when using software‑controlled ganging of
FVI16 channels:
Any combination of up to sixteen ganged channels is supported within one card.
Each FVI16 card supports up to 8 independent ganging groups.
Ganging is supported only in the high‑power mode. Ganging is not supported in
the high‑voltage mode.
Ganging is not supported for channels that are stacked under software control.
The time measurement unit (TMU) is supported but only the high‑speed and
high‑resolution voltage comparators can be used. The measurement is performed
on the master channel. The high‑resolution current comparator is not supported.
Ganging groups can be disbanded and the individual channels can be assigned
within the same testflow. For more information, refer to FVI16 stacked or ganged
on the fly.

On-board ganging controller
The on-board ganging controller is used to balance the total output current between
the ganged channels.
In a ganged configuration, the channel with the lowest number acts as the master
channel. The master channel feeds the measured current to the slaves and each slave
uses this value to adjust its own current to be identical with the master's current.
DUT board connections
Some connections of the force lines and sense lines of ganged channels are required on
the DUT board:
The HF# (high force) pins of the ganged channels and the LF# (low force) pins of
the ganged channels must be connected together on the DUT board.
The same parallel connection is required for the HS# (high sense) pins and the LS#
(low sense) pins of the ganged channels.
The combined force lines and sense lines must be connected together at the DUT.
These DUT board connections may be routed via optional relay multiplexers.
The guard line (GUARD#) may be used to shield the high fore and high sense lines
up to the DUT. The guard lines of ganged channels may also be routed via optional
relay multiplexers. The guard lines of the individual channels of a ganging group
must not be connected together. For more information, refer to FVI16 wiring of
guard.
Power budget and ganging groups
The available power budget and energy budget on FVI16 cards is defined as follows:
The maximum total power budget is 400 W.
The maximum total energy budget is 3.2 J.
The two budgets are equally distributed to two channel groups 1 … 8 and 9 … 16
providing 200 W and 1.6 J per group.
Within the two groups, the budgets are shared by all eight channels.
For ganging groups in high energy applications, we recommend therefore utilizing the
budgets of both channel groups: The channels of each ganging group should equally be
distributed to both groups. For more information, refer to FVI16 power budget and
energy budget.

Resolution of the clamp current
All channels of a ganged group are programmed to the same values. The resolution
of the programmed clamp current is the resolution of a single channel multiplied by
the number of ganged channels.

FVI16 stacked or ganged on the fly
Multiple FVI16 channels can be connected in series or in parallel to increase the output
voltage or current. This is called "stacking" and "ganging". "Stacking on the fly" and
"Ganging on the fly" means that the group of stacked or ganged channels can be
disbanded and the individual channels can be assigned to other pins of the DUT
according to the needs of the testflow.
Software
Reusing FVI16 channels requires the definition of another connection set in the Digital
Pins editor and therefore is supported for FVI16 channels in PMU operating mode. The
connection sets are used like different DUT board traces.
An FVI16 channel must be disconnected before it can be reused in another ganging
group or as single pin.
 The digital pins editor automatically sorts the channel numbers of a ganging group
from the lowest value to the highest value. The channel number in this context means
the combination of the three digit pogo number and the two digit channel number of
the pogo block.
 One J (Joule) corresponds to the derived unit of one Ws (Watt-second). One Ws is the
energy equivalent to the power of one watt sustained for one second.

Required DUT board hardware
"Stacking onf the fly" or "Ganging on the fly" needs the same DUT board hardware as
stacking or ganging with fixed channel assignment to stacking or ganging groups:
Stacked channels must be connected serially.
Ganged channels must be connected in parallel at the related DUT pins.
Additional hardware is required for "Stacking on the fly" or "Ganging on the fly" to
provide different DUT board traces:
The connections from the pogo pins of the card to the DUT must be routed via
additional relays.
These relays must be inserted for the force lines and the sense lines.
Additional relays may be used for the guard lines.
Note  The pins HF# and HS# and the pins LF# and L#S are part of the digital closed
loop control of the same channel. HF# and HS# must therefore always be connected
to the same DUT pin. The same rule applies for LF# and LS#. Violating this rule may
result in an unpredictable behavior.

For pins that use connection sets, pattern containing DC events must be set up as a
multiport burst. A port can only contain pins with the same connection set or only
pins with the default connection set. The use of a multiport timing is required if

FVI16 pulsed operation
Each channel of the FVI16 card can force a current pulse of up to ±10 A in pulsed mode
for a short time of some milliseconds. The available energy budget of the on-board
energy storages, the power dissipation of the main driver and a maximum duty cycle
must be considered for the high current pulses.
The pulsed operation is supported for the PMU operating mode. The programmable
bandwidth and slew-rate are to be used to optimize the dynamic behavior for different
types of pulsed tests and measurements.
Topic 152718

Energy storages
The energy for pulses up to ±10 A is provided by two on-board energy storages that are
shared by groups of eight channels. The FVI16 card monitors the energy consumption of
the individual channels and immediately disconnects a channel if the consumed energy
exceeds the assigned energy budget. For more information, refer to section Energy
budget in FVI16 power budget and energy budget.
Power dissipation
The power dissipation of the main driver is calculated from the voltage drop at the main
driver and the current. It depends therefore on the programmable compliance voltage,
the output voltage, and the actual current.
Each FVI16 channel features an on-board monitor that checks the power dissipation of
the main driver. A channel that exceeds the maximum power dissipation will
immediately be disconnected and must be connected again.
We recommend therefore, setting the compliance voltage always to the minimum
possible value. This will also minimize the stored energy that is consumed.
Maximum duty cycle
The consumed energy and the power dissipation at the main driver limit the maximum
duty cycle. The energy storage must be recharged from the available power budget and
the main driver needs some time for cooling down. For more information, refer to
section Duty cycle and recharging of the on-board energy storages in FVI16 power
budget and energy budget.

Configuration - model file
The FVI16 card and pogo blocks must be defined in the POGOCABLING section and in
the DPS section of the model file.
As shown in FVI16 pogo pin assignment, the sixteen channels of the FVI16 card are
routed to four pogo blocks "A" ... "D":
Pogo block "A": Channel 1 ... 4
Pogo block "B": Channel 5 … 8
Pogo block "C": Channel 9 … 12
Pogo block "D": Channel 13 … 16
The FVI16 pogo blocks are to be defined in the model file as follows:
Only the first pogo block "A" must be defined by keyword pogoblocks.
The following type = REDIRECT and subtype = E8026PVP define the type of the
pogo cable.
All four physical pogo blocks "A" ... "D" are to be defined in the following config
statement for the pogo cable "E8026PVP" using the prefix A= that again points to
the physical pogo block "A".
POGOCABLING syntax for the E8026PVP pogo cable:
POGOCABLING
    ###: pogoblocks = "A", type = REDIRECT, subtype = E8026PVP, config = "A=A,B,C,D"
with ### Three‑digit slot number
A, B, C, D Three‑digit number of the physical pogo block
Example:
POGOCABLING
    110: pogoblocks = "405", type=REDIRECT, subtype=E8026PVP, config="405=405,406,407,408"
    ...
    ...
DPS
    40501-40516: type = DCS-FVI16, tmu, vrange = 120
The example above shows pogo block "A" on position 405. Pogo blocks "A" ... "D" on positions 405, 406, 407, and 408
must be defined by type=REDIRECT, subtype=E8026PVP, and config where the subtype defines the FVI16 pogo
cable "E8026PVP".

Note  With SmarTest 7, for the definition of the pins, all sixteen channels are
assigned to pogo block "A" although they are physically wired to the pogo blocks
"A" ... "D" via the "E8026PVP" pogo cable.
Note  FVI16 can replace the legacy PVI8, but the FVI16 and PVI8 cannot be
operated at the same time in the same system.

Licensing
Licenses are required to enable the basic functionality of the FVI16 channels. The basic
functionality includes the AWG and the DGT, the Kelvin test unit,the surge tracker, and
profiling. The voltage ranges are limited to ±3 V, ±10 V, and ±30 V.
The following licenses cover the basic functionality of the FVI16 channels:
N8040BC - DC Scale FVI16 - Base capability license (8 channels, 30V power range):
The license enables the basic functionality of an FVI16 card for eight channels and
for voltages up to ±30  V.
N8040BCX - DC Scale FVI16 - Base capability extension license (8 to 16 channels,
30V power range):
The license extends the basic functionality of an FVI16 card from eight channels to
sixteen channels.
These basic capabilities can be extended by some upgrade licenses:
N8042 - DC Scale FVI16 - 30V to 60V power range upgrade license:
The license enables the ±60 voltage range of the FVI16 channel.
N8043 - DC Scale FVI16 - 60V to 120V high voltage mode upgrade license:
The license enables the -60 V … +120 V voltage mode of the FVI16 channel.
Using this upgrade license requires that the "N8042 - DC Scale FVI16 - 30V to 60V
power range upgrade license" is also available.
N8041 - DC Scale FVI16 - Time measurement unit (TMU) license:
The license enables the Time measurement unit of the FVI16 channel.
Upgrade licenses for FVI16 channels need to be configured via the model file or via the
device license file. For more information, refer to the two sections Configuration - model
file and Licensing - Device license file.
The already configured upgrade licenses are to be enabled for the currently loaded
device:
Upgrade license needs for the FVI16 channels must manually be enabled manually
for the assigned pins using the DC Scale Extensions editor.
Data that are defined by the DC Scale Extensions Editor are stored in the Pin
configuration file using the firmware command DFDM.
For a complete list of available licenses, refer to V93000 License Master Look-up Table.

Operating modes
The FVI16 card supports the DPS operating mode and the PMU operating mode. The
FVI16 operating mode is defined by the pin type that has been used in the Pin setting
editors. The operating mode can be set individually for each channel of the card.
Pin configuration for the DPS operating mode
The pin configuration of channel-slot DC Scale cards is slightly different to that of a
DPS-slot device power supply. To configure an FVI16 pin for the DPS operating
mode you must specify the pin as DPS with positive polarity. For details see DC
Scale pin (DPS mode) setup.
Pin configuration for the PMU operating mode
An FVI16 pin is configured for the PMU operating mode if the channel is defined as
DC Scale pin using the Digital Pins editor. The pin type has to be set to dc and the
pin mode to SIG. Refer to Digital Pins editor for more information.

Ganging.

Action: The flag is for information only.

energy storage.
Availability: Two on-board energy storages are available for the two channel groups

Enabling a channel after it has been disconnected
The procedure described below should be followed for channels that have been
disconnected by the channel controller for reasons of safety or for the self-protection of
the card:
Ensure that the reason for the disconnection has been eliminated. Possible actions
are:
Apply the control voltage to both safety circuits.
The following actions are required in case a channel has been disconnected in the
testflow:
Check the state of the flags using the APIs described in DPS power flags - get...
() functions.
Disconnect the channel by SmarTest. The related error message will be shown
in the report window and the status flags will be cleared.
Connect the channel.
The following actions are required in case a channel has been disconnected when
working with the hardware view:
For a channel in the PMU operating mode: Start a dummy measurement in the
ADC sub-panel with the relay action set to NT.
For a channel in the DPS operating mode: Click onto the Disconnect button in
the toolbar of the SmarTest Work Center.
Disconnecting the channel will cause that the related error message is shown in
the report window and will clear the status flags.
Connect the channel.

DC event status
The command TSST? - (TeSt STatus) returns global information about the DC event
related results of the last executed test, and also provides the accumulated status
information about all recorded measurements. A test point pattern must have been
executed for DC Scale pins. The accumulated information is cleared at the begin of a
functional test. The accumulated flags remain then valid until the begin of the next
functional test.
TSST? returns a twofold reply. One informs about the test results, the other about the
test status:
Test result flags:
The functionality of some test result related flags can be enabled or disabled for
specific measurement events using member functions of the DC events. Functions
to enable or disabled the flags are for example
...clampChecks()
...outOfRangeCheck()
The flags are cleared with the start of the next functional test.
Test status flags:
The test status related flags cannot be enabled or disabled. These flags are
accumulated for the complete functional test. The flags are cleared with the start of
the next functional test.

Application note
Open safety line triggers more flags than expected
An open safety circuit may cause that already connected and active FVI16 channels
are disconnected immediately for safety. This will always trigger the Safety Line flag
but disconnecting an active channel may also trigger other alarm flags.
Therefore, the interlock switch that connects the control voltage to the two safety
circuits must always be closed for operating any of the FVI16 channels. All other
alarm flags may be ignored in case the Safety Line flag has been triggered and the
safety circuits must first be activated again before the FVI16 channels are checked
for other flags.

For a minimized test time we recommend, not to reuse pattern with DC events that

Application note
Flush vectors at the end of a pattern
Due to inter module communication it is required to keep the pattern running for a
short time after the last ADC measurement related DC event. The actual required
time or number of flush vectors depends on the setup. In case of insufficient number
of vectors before pattern stop, a communication error might occur and
measurement results might be lost.
The number of required flush vectors depends on the average count and the pattern
cycle time as follows:
Minimum number of vectors = 37 + ( average / (1 MHz * period) )
where: average = Programmed average count
period = Cycle time of the pattern
The calculated number is the minimum number of vectors that is required between
the last measure event and the end of the pattern.
The minimum number of vectors may be higher if TMU measurements are started in
the same pattern as the ADC measurements.
Note that the TSST? - (TeSt STatus) firmware command can be used to check for
missing samples: Bit 8 is set if a measurement is lost.

FVI16 programming - DPS operating mode
An FVI16 pin in the DPS operating mode can be programmed via level setups, APIs or
SmartRDI.
Topic 152727

We recommend programming the basic settings with the level setup and applying
changes in the pattern‑based mode of SmartRDI or with DC events.
An FVI16 pin in DPS operating mode supports a subset of the features in PMU operating
mode:
An FVI16 channel in DPS operating mode supports the PMU functionality including
the AWG and DGT mode.
An FVI16 channel in DPS operating mode does not support
the high-voltage mode (-60 V ... +120 V),
the time measurement unit (TMU),
"ganging on the fly", and
software‑controlled "stacking" and "stacking on the fly".
The pulsed operating mode is not supported in the DPS operating mode with
activated power budget management. The FVI16 channels can consume only the
available power budget for DC operation in the DPS operating mode. The
maximum power budget for DC operation is 200 W per group of eight channels.
Note  The assessed power of the individual channels is defined by the
compliance voltage and the programmed clamp or force current. The assessed
power includes therefore the power consumption of the main driver, the power
consumption that is caused by the voltage drop on the force and return line
and finally the power that is available at the DUT.
SmartRDI overview
The complete functionality to set up an FVI16 pin in the DPS operating mode is covered
by the dc() API of SmartRDI. Both the code‑based mode and the pattern‑based mode
are supported. For more information refer to Setting up DC Scale pins with SmartRDI
and the related member functions of the dc() API.

Force and clamp settings and the dynamic behavior of an FVI16 pin in the DPS
operating mode are controlled by the level setup. To access most features of the card
you must use equations. For details see the Equation based level setup and DPSPINS
resources.
The dynamic behavior of an FVI16 pin in DPS operating mode is defined by the
following DPSPINS resources:
voltage_filter_frequency
current_filter_frequency
FVI16 pin in DPS operating will be disconnected if the voltage drop on the force line
(HF#) or return line (LF#) exceeds the programmed limits. The maximum voltage drop is
set by the following DPSPIN resources:
max_voltage_drop_force
max_voltage_drop_return
Supported connection states, defined by DPSPINS resource connect_state:
norm
ungang
himp
pulse
Note  The mode pulse is supported for compatibility with the legacy DC Scale
PVI8 card. FVI16 accepts this mode but stays in the mode norm.
Note  The default value norm of DPS pin resource connect_state can be selected

Minimum clamp current distance
An FVI16 PMU needs a minimum distance between the positive and negative clamp
current to avoid oscillation.
Current range Minimum clamp distance

The minimum clamp distance means that both the negative and the positive clamp
current can be set within the full range from the minimum respectively the maximum
value to 0.0 A if the minimum distance of the two values is maintained. Asymmetrical
clamp current definitions with one of the values set to 0.0 A are supported.
For reasons of compatibility with other cards, FVI16 supports the measurement mode
"IFVM". Also for reasons of compatibility, this mode is set so that voltage is forced and
the clamp current limits the current to the required value. Therefore, in "IFVM" mode
you must observe the minimum clamp current distance for setting the forced current.
If you need to set a current that is less than the minimum clamp current distance, you
must use the real current forcing modes "CFVM" or "CFIM".

Application notes

The FVI16 card comprises a limited power budget and features on-board energy
storages for delivering the energy for high-power pulses. The utilization of the
power budget and the charging state of the on-board energy storages is constantly
monitored. Warning flags are set in case the utilization of the power budget or the
charging state of the energy storages reaches a critical level. An error message is
issued and the involved channel or channels are disconnected if the power budget
or energy budget is exceeded. The programmed force or clamp current and the
programmed compliance voltage are used to calculate the utilization of the available
budgets.
The utilization of the power budgets depends on the behavior of the DUT and will
vary from test to test. The power budgets of the FVI16 card need therefore always
your attention regarding possibly set warning flags. The flags should be checked at
least at the end of the testflow. For more information refer to FVI16 status flags.
DC events in reused pattern
For a minimized test time we recommend, not to reuse pattern with DC events that
are to be applied for different FVI16 ranges. The recommendation applies to pattern
that are manually created using the related test method APIs but not to the
automatically created SmartRDI pattern.
The FVI16 channels feature several force ranges. The pattern data of related DC
events must be reloaded in case the containing pattern is reused for another range.
This may significantly increase the test time.
The recommendation applies to all DC events that change the force- or clamp value
or range or the measurement range.

and clamping voltages.
FVI16 channels must be disconnected before they are changed from the high-power

1)

Compliance voltage
FVI16 channels in high‑power mode feature a programmable compliance voltage. The
compliance voltage is the voltage to which the raw power supply of a channel is set. The
programmable range of the compliance voltage is +10 V ... +65 V.
Two competing rules must be observed when setting the compliance voltage:
The maximum output voltage of the channel is limited by the programmed
compliance voltage.
The compliance voltage has an effect on the power dissipation of the main driver
and the consumed energy and should be set as low as possible.
The recommended compliance voltage can be calculated as follows:
VCompliance = 2.5 V + 1 Ω * IForce/Clamp + VForce drop + VReturn
drop + VDUT/Clamp
where VCompliance = Compliance voltage to be set
VForce drop = Maximum voltage drop on the high force line
VReturn drop = Maximum voltage drop on the return / low force line
VDUT/Clamp = Force voltage mode: Forced voltage
Force current mode: Clamp voltage
IForce/Clamp = Force voltage mode: Clamp current
Force current mode: Forced current
SmarTest shows the recommended compliance value in the UI report window if the
programmed compliance voltage is lower than the recommended voltage.
See also the FVI16 Kelvin measurement unit specifications for the programmable range
of the voltage drop. If the voltage drop is not programmed, default values as defined in
the APIs linked in FVI16 programming - Voltage drop measurement are used.
CAUTION  Compliance voltage dependent oscillation
An FVI16 channel driving a resistive load may oscillate under the following
conditions if the compliance voltage is set too high:
Compliance voltage > (DUT voltage + 30 V) 
Current flow > 100 mA and < 2 A
Load capacitance < 47 nF
To avoid oscillation under the above conditions, set the compliance voltage as low
as possible.

Minimum clamp voltage distance
An FVI16 PMU needs a minimum distance between the positive and negative clamp
voltage to avoid oscillation.
Voltage range Minimum clamp distance

± 10 V 1.0 V
± 30 V 3.0 V
± 60 V 6.0 V
High-voltage mode -60 V ... +120 V 12.0 V
The minimum clamp distance means that both the negative and the positive clamp
voltage can be set within the full range from the minimum respectively the maximum
value to 0.0 V if the minimum distance of the two values is maintained. Asymmetrical
clamp voltage definitions with one of the values set to 0.0 V are supported.

The following force voltage filters are available for an FVI16 channel in force voltage or
clamp voltage mode:

This value defines a voltage bandwidth that has an effect on the dynamic behavior

Represents the load capacitance on the DUT board. The parameter is used to adapt
the dynamic behavior of an FVI16 channel to different load capacitors. This filter has
an effect on the dynamic behavior when a channel is forcing or clamping the
voltage.
Voltage slew rate:
The parameter defines the slew rate for changes of the programmed voltage force

Setting the load capacitor
The load capacitance settings must be handled carefully. Setting the wrong load
capacitance may result in an oscillating channel. The load capacitance should be set
only if the related hardware on the DUT board is already connected.
The following example sequence for an IDDQ test assumes that two capacitors are
connected to the supply pin of the DUT:
C0 is a small hardwired capacitor or the parasitic capacitance of the DUT board
traces to the DUT pin.
C1 is a switched bigger capacitor that is required for the normal operation of
the DUT.
We recommend using the following sequence for the IDDQ test:
1. Connect C1; close all required DUT board connections.
2. Connect the FVI16 channel with the required supply voltage set and with the
load capacitance set to C0 + C1.
3. Set the DUT to the required state for the IDDQ measurement.
4. Set the load capacitance of the FVI16 channel to C0.
5. Disconnect the switched capacitor C1.
6. Change the FVI16 current range to the range that is required for the IDDQ
measurement.
7. Measure the IDDQ in the new current measure range.

8. Restore the original current range.
9. Connect the switched capacitor C1.
10. Restore the load capacitance of the FVI16 channel to C0 + C1.

is called "ganging". FVI16 cards support software controlled ganging of any
combination of up to sixteen channels is within one card.

Ganging
Ganged FVI16 channels can be setup under user control or under software control:
User‑controlled ganging:
Several channels are simply connected in parallel and similar settings are applied.
This can lead to an undefined distribution of the current to the individual channels
and may result in unstable output voltages and invalid current measurements.
Modifying the settings may improve the behavior but needs more attention of the
user.
Software‑controlled ganging:
The parallel connected channels are defined as ganging group in the pin definitions
of SmarTest. The ganging group is accessed as single pin. The on‑board-ganging
controller distributes the total output current equally between the ganged channels.
This solution will show a stable output signal and provides reliable current
measurements without applying special setups as required for ganging under user
control.
We recommend therefore, always setting up software‑controlled ganging.
Ganging characteristics
The following items must be considered when using software‑controlled ganging of
FVI16 channels:
Any combination of up to sixteen ganged channels is supported within one card.
Each FVI16 card supports up to 8 independent ganging groups.
Ganging is supported only in the high‑power mode. Ganging is not supported in
the high‑voltage mode.
Ganging is not supported for channels that are stacked under software control.
The time measurement unit (TMU) is supported but only the high‑speed and
high‑resolution voltage comparators can be used. The measurement is performed
on the master channel. The high‑resolution current comparator is not supported.
Ganging groups can be disbanded and the individual channels can be assigned
within the same testflow. For more information, refer to FVI16 stacked or ganged
on the fly.

Defining pins
DPS operating mode>:
Ganging groups for FVI16 channels in DPS operating mode are defined in the DPS
Pins editor. You can specify the range of channels to be ganged by "-" (hyphen) or a
list of channels with the channels separated by "," (comma). For more information
refer to DC Scale pin (DPS mode) setup.
PMU operating mode:
Ganging groups for FVI16 channels in PMU operating mode are defined in the
Digital Pins editor. You can specify the range of channels to be ganged by "-"
(hyphen) or each channel separated by "," (comma). For more information refer to
DC Scale pin (PMU mode) setup.
Ganging on the fly
Ganging on the fly" means that a group of ganged channels can be disbanded and the
individual channels can be assigned to other pins of the DUT according to the needs of
the testflow.
Reusing of FVI16 channels requires different connection set definitions. These
connection sets are defined in column Connection Set of the Digital Pins editor.
Therefore, ganging on the fly requires setting up the FVI16 channels for the PMU
operating mode.
For more information on how to set up reused channels, refer to DC Scale pin (PMU
mode) setup.
An FVI16 channel must be disconnected before it can be reused in another ganging
group or as single pin.

Software overview
No special APIs are required to control ganged FVI16 channels. The complete
functionality is covered by APIs SPMU_TASK and SPMU_PIN_TASK for an FVI16 in PMU
operating mode or by the Equation based level setup and API DPS_TASK for an FVI16 in
DPS operating mode.
Temporarily unganged channels
Current measurements with temporarily unganged channels are supported by the
following APIs and keywords:
API SPMU_PIN_TASK.mode("VFIM_UNGANGED")
API DPS_PIN_TASK.measurementMode(TM::MEASURE_CURRENT_UNGANGED)
SmartRDI API rdi.dc().ungang()
Current measurements with temporarily unganged channels are supported in
the code‑based mode using the API as defined above. Current measurements
with temporarily unganged channels are not supported in the pattern‑based
mode.
Per‑channel results
With normal APIs, the result for ganged pins is read from the master channel of the
ganging group.
The following APIs support per‑channel results for ganged FVI16 pins in PMU
operating mode, which means that results for each individual channel of ganged
pins can be read from the hardware:
returnChannelGangSequence()
rdi.dc().perChannelResults() and rdi.id().getPerChannelValue()
enableChannelResults() and getValues() of SPMU_TASK
Per‑channel results are also supported by the Per‑channel results display of the
Hardware view for DPS and VI pins.
Note that the best throughput can be achieved by uploading results only from the
master channel of a ganged pin. Uploading the results per channel increases the test
time.

Application notes
Surge tracker is silently disabled in temporarily unganged mode
Note that on AVI64, DPS128/64, and FVI16 you cannot execute a current compare on
a ganged group of channels if the group is in unganged mode. Already activated
comparators are silently disabled in unganged mode. A user notification (Error or
warning) is omitted in this case, to avoid any interrupt in the testflow. The previous
state of the comparators is automatically restored after the ganged group has been
restored.
Dynamic behavior of the surge tracker in ganged mode
The digital closed loop control leads always to a small delay of minimum one sample
from the master channel of a ganging group to the slave channels: The slave
channels react to the measured values of the master channel and adjust their
outputs to drive the same current.
This may lead to a certain hypersensitivity for fast changes of the signal level.
The thresholds of the surge tracker must therefore be adjusted accordingly to
compensate this behavior.
Ganging on the fly and DC events in pattern
For pins that use connection sets, pattern containing DC events must be set up as a
multiport burst. A port can only contain pins with the same connection set or only
pins with the default connection set. The use of a multiport timing is required if
connection sets are defined for the related pins.
For more information regarding the default connection set, refer to Digital Pins
editor and DFPN, DFPN?
Battery level measurements of ganged FVI16 channels
FVI16 features two on-board energy storages for pulsed high-current tests that are
assigned to the channel groups 1 … 8 and 9 … 16. Ganging across these two groups
is supported. For ganging groups that cover both channel groups and therefore
utilize both energy storages, the battery level measurement returns the lower of the
two charging levels if per‑channel results for ganged channels have not been
explicitly enabled by rdi.dc().perChannelResults() or
SPMU_TASK.enableChannelResults().

For more information, refer to parameter FVI16_connectionState in
SPMU_PIN_TASK.connectState(), Special events for FVI16 inEVENT_... - DC events API
reference and the SmartRDI function rdi.dc().vMeasBattery().

The FVI16 channels feature a Kelvin test unit (or sense-connection test unit), a voltage
drop measurement (or Kelvin measurement) unit and an internal force to sense (FS) link.
Kelvin test means that the connection from the force lines to the sense lines on the
DUT board or at the DUT pins is verified.
Voltage drop measurement means that the voltage drop on the force lines is
monitored.
The internal force to sense (FS) link connects the force lines internally with the sense
lines to keep the control loop closed when optional external switches on the DUT
board are open temporarily.

For more information, refer to FVI16 internal force to sense (FS) link.
CAUTION Use the internal force to sense (FS) link with caution. Improper use of
internal FS link may lead to incorrect measurements or other unwanted behavior:
The force and return drop measurements and monitoring of the maximum force
and return drop will not work while the internal FS link is closed.
This applies to the alarm thresholds set for the Voltage drop force and Voltage
drop return status flags, to SmartRDI APIs rdi.dc().vMeasForceDrop() and
rdi.dc().vMeasReturnDrop() , to SPMU_PIN_TASK.connectState() settings
"MEAS_KELVIN_HIGH" and "MEAS_KELVIN_LOW" and to the FVI16 specific DC
events "...FDM..." and "...RDM...".
With closed internal FS link, all voltage measurements are referenced to the
internal connection. The voltage drop on the force and return line to the DUT
cannot be compensated or monitored in this case and the measured voltage is
wrong.
Note  The internal force to sense (FS) link is automatically opened and the sense
connection to the DUT is restored whenever a pattern on an FVI16 channel ends.
This is to prevent from erroneous measurements with closed internal FS link.
This applies also for the RDI block of SmartRDI. In addition, the execution mode
TA::SINGLE of RDI_BEGIN() must be used with caution: The single step execution
will cause that the internal FS link is opened after each step.
This behavior can be disabled using the following APIs and keywords:
Test method API: SPMU_PIN_TASK.connectState() with the parameter set to
"FS_OVERRIDE_ALWAYS".
SmartRDI function: rdi.dc().connectState() with the parameter set to
TA::FORCE_SENSE_LINK_KEEP.
Although the automatic opening of the FS link affects only the pattern‑based
programming mode, the behavior can be disabled only in code‑based mode using
the functions mentioned above. This applies to both the test method API and the
SmartRDI function.

FVI16 programming - Kelvin test / sense
connection test
The FVI16 card features a Kelvin test unit (or sense-connection test unit). Kelvin test
means that the connection from the force lines to the sense lines on the DUT board or
at the DUT pins is verified.
 Requires SmarTest 7.5.1 or higher versions.
1)
Topic 346050

The Kelvin test unit applies a small test current to the tested force to sense (FS)
connection and measures the voltage drop between the two lines. The measured
voltage is used as criterion for the pass/fail decision and should be near 0.0 V for a good
F-S connection. For more information, refer to FVI16 Kelvin test unit.
Note  The purpose of the Kelvin test unit is to ensure that when the DUT is
contacted, the high-impedance sense line is connected to the force line at the DUT
with a sufficiently low contact resistance. Due to the high input impedance of the
sense lines, the fixed threshold of some kilo-Ohms will be sufficiently low.
The Kelvin test unit is the only resource that can perform a reliable sense connection
test with a defined test current applied.
Since connections and hardware on the DUT board can sabotage the test of the
sense connections, we recommend that you check the functionality of the test
without DUT and with open sense connections. All tested sense connections must
fail in this verification.
The purpose of the Kelvin test unit is not to check the low impedance force
connections. The force connections are to be checked by the FVI16 voltage drop
measurement unit in combination with a high test current forced by the PMU. This
force connection test requires that the contact resistance of the sense lines already
has been verified.
Attention: An inadequate sense line connection does not necessarily mean that a
force drop test fails. The input bias current of the line may falsify the measurement
and mask another fatal error like a high voltage drop on the force line.
CAUTION The FVI16 PMU forces the test current via one of the tested lines, the
FS connection, and via the other tested line to ground. For the sense connection
test, one of the lines may be internally connected to ground. Therefore, the DUT
must be powered down before the Kelvin test (or sense connection test) is started in
disconnected mode.

Basic data
Basic data of the FVI16 Kelvin test unit:
The Kelvin test unit is available per channel.
The threshold for the pass/fail decision is about 5 kΩ.
The test current is maximum about 100 µA.
The maximum capacitance between the force lines and the corresponding sense
lines is 5 nF.
The set up and set down of the test is performed in parallel on all selected pins.
Three measurements are serially performed for the HF# pin, the HS# pin and the
LS# pin.
Testing sixteen FVI16 channels requires a test time of about 15 ms per site.
The test can be performed only in the disconnected state of the selected pins.
API overview
Two APIs support a parallel go/no-go Kelvin test on all active sites and pins and a
detailed Kelvin test on the site in focus. Both APIs perform two measurements for the
HF# to HS# connection and for the LF# to LS# connection.
Function HW_STATE.checkKelvinStatusParallel()
The function checkKelvinStatusParallel() of class HW_STATE initiates a sense
connection test on the defined pins to verify that the force lines and sense lines are
connected together on the DUT board or at the DUT pins. The test is performed in
parallel for all active sites. The function returns a go/no-go result for each
configured site in a single integer array.
The go/no-go result of the function is set to 0 (Kelvin test has failed) if any of
the tested pins has returned a failing result for any of the performed
measurements.
The go/no-go result of the function is set to 1 (Kelvin test has passed) if all
tested pins have successfully finished all measurements on all active sites.
Function HW_STATE.checkKelvinStatus()
The function initiates a sense connection test for the site in focus. The function
returns individual results for all tested pins in two integer arrays for the HF# to HS#
connections and for the LF# to LS# connections.
For ganged pins, the Kelvin test / sense connection test is performed for each individual
channel.

Kelvin test unit operating principle
For the operating principle, refer to HF# line test, HS# line test and LS# line test in FVI16
Kelvin test unit.
Test Method Library overview
The DC test method DpsConnectivity of the Test Method Library is provided to control
the Kelvin test unit and to read and judge the state of the measurement.
Application note
Kelvin test / sense connection test in a testflow
A continuity test, which is normally performed at the beginning of a test flow, may
use FVI16 channels. The continuity test will show a reliable result only if both the
force and sense pins of the FVI16 channels are connected properly. Therefore, we
recommend implementing a Kelvin test / sense connection at the beginning of a
testflow before the continuity test is performed.

FVI16 programming - Voltage drop
measurement
The FVI16 card features a voltage drop measurement (or Kelvin measurement) unit.
Voltage drop measurement means that the voltage drop on the force lines is monitored.
For high-current tests, the total voltage drop on the force lines must be monitored by
the voltage drop measurement unit for proper operation of the FVI16 channels. The
continuously measured voltage is compared against a programmable limit. An alarm
flag is set for a channel that exceeds the programmed limit. If the channel is set to the
3 A or 10 A range, it is immediately disconnected to protect the probes. For more
information, refer to FVI16 voltage drop measurement.

LAST measurements
Each channel of a DC Scale FVI16 card features five ADCs for voltage measurements,
current measurements, voltage drop measurements on the force line and on the return
line and battery level measurements at the on-board energy storage. The ADCs are
always triggered simultaneously but only the measured value that is defined by the
individual measurement command is transferred from the front-end to the test
processor and can be uploaded later.
For pattern‑based measurements, additional APIs or parameters that are named "…
LAST ..." provide the functionality to transfer and upload the measured values of all five
ADCs without initiating a new trigger. The values of the last synchronous measurement
of the five ADC are therefore available until the next measurement is triggered.
Averaging of LAST measurements:
If average is used for the primary measurement, then the "… LAST ..." measurements
will also return an averaged value.
Voltage and current measurements are performed every 1 us.
Battery level and force/return drop measurements are performed every 5 us. These
measurements will return a value every 1 us; however, the value is refreshed only
once every 5 us.

Maximum voltage drop in DPS operating mode
FVI16 channels support the DPSPINs resources max_voltage_drop_force and

Status flag
The voltage drop on the force line and on the return lines is constantly monitored. If
the channel is set to the 3 A or 10 A range, it is immediately disconnected to protect
the probes. This condition is indicated by two flags:
Voltage drop force indicates that the voltage drop on the force line was too
high.
Voltage drop return indicates that the voltage drop on the return line was too
high.
Voltage drop measurements on ganged channels
If per‑channel results for ganged channels have not been explicitly enabled by
rdi.dc().perChannelResults() or SPMU_TASK.enableChannelResults(), the result of a
voltage drop measurement is uploaded only from the master channel. However,
continuous monitoring of the voltage drop is active on all channels and the entire
ganging group is disconnected if only one channel exceeds the threshold.
Due to different routing of the individual channels on the DUT board and the
unavoidable measurement error, a single channel can trigger an alarm and the entire
group will be disconnected, even if the measurement on the master channel shows
that the programmed maximum voltage drop is not exceeded.

Averaging
All channels of the card feature hardware based averaging of measurements. The
average of multiple consecutive ADC samples is calculated and stored on
board.Hardware based averaging can be utilized for code‑based and pattern‑based
measurements.

Some hints to consider:
The sample time for averaged measurements must be taken into account.
Pattern‑based measurements require a minimum number of vectors after the
trigger has been initiated. For more information, refer to Timing of DC events and
the related sub-topics.
The effective maximum sample frequency is the ADC sample frequency of 1 MHz
divided by the number of averaged samples.
The "measurement filter" may be used instead of averaging if a high effective
sample frequency is required. This filter behaves like a simple RC filter. The settling
time is to be considered but the filter setting has no effect on the effective
maximum sample frequency.
The dynamic behavior of the force output is independent of the settings for
averaging.

Automatic down-ranging
FVI16 channels feature automatic down-ranging for current measurements.
Automatic down-ranging means that the current range is automatically changed to the
best fit range for the measurement and restored to the original range after the
measurement.
Two parameters define whether the automatic down-ranging is performed or not:
1. The force / clamp current range:
Can be set explicitly or (if not defined)
is automatically derived from the forced or clamped value.
2. The current measurement range:
Can be set explicitly or (if not defined)
is automatically derived from the pass/fail thresholds.
Automatic down-ranging is performed only if the current measurement range is lower
than the force / clamp current range regardless whether the ranges have been set
explicitly or have been selected automatically.
With automatic down‑ranging active, the next lower current range is activated only if
the measured current does not exceed 90 % of the next lower current range.
Automatic down-ranging is supported for both code‑based programming using the
SPMU_TASK and DPS_TASK test method APIs and the pattern‑based programming using
the DC events and is also supported by SmartRDI.

Application notes
Flush vectors at the end of a pattern
Due to inter module communication it is required to keep the pattern running for a
short time after the last ADC measurement related DC event. The actual required
time or number of flush vectors depends on the setup. In case of insufficient number
of vectors before pattern stop, a communication error might occur and
measurement results might be lost.
The number of required flush vectors depends on the average count and the pattern
cycle time as follows:
Minimum number of vectors = 37 + ( average / (1 MHz * period) )
where: average = Programmed average count
period = Cycle time of the pattern
The calculated number is the minimum number of vectors that is required between
the last measure event and the end of the pattern.
The minimum number of vectors may be higher if TMU measurements are started in
the same pattern as the ADC measurements.
Note that the TSST? - (TeSt STatus) firmware command can be used to check for
missing samples: Bit 8 is set if a measurement is lost.
Measure filter settling time
The programmable digital low-pass measure filters for all ADCs behave like simple
RC filters. A short settling time is to be applied or some samples are to be ignored to
settle to an acceptable difference to the input signal.
The required settling time of the filter or the number of samples to be ignored
depends on the accepted maximum relative error and the effective filter frequency
and is calculated as follows:
Settling time = -1.0 * ln (Maximum relative error) / (2 * π * Filter frequency)
Number of samples = Settling time * Sample frequency
where: Maximum relative error = Maximum accepted relative error at the end of the settling time
Filter frequency = Programmed filter frequency
Sample frequency = ADC sample frequency
ln = Natural logarithm

Settling time for the minimum achievable error
Sample frequency [kHz] Programmed filter frequency [kHz] Settling time [µs]
1000 250 8.8
50 44.1
10 220.6
Some notes on the table above:
The minimum achievable error for a fully settled filter is defined by one LSB of
the used ADC.
The sample frequency in the normal operating is always derived from the free
running 1 MHz clock of the digital closed loop control. This results in an
effective jitter of up to 1 µs for the DGT samples.
For more typical values, refer to section Programmable measurement filter for
voltage and current in the FVI16 load capacitance and measurement filter
specifications.

Application note
DC events in reused pattern
For a minimized test time we recommend, not to reuse pattern with DC events that
are to be applied for different FVI16 ranges. The recommendation applies to pattern
that are manually created using the related test method APIs but not to the
automatically created SmartRDI pattern.
The FVI16 channels feature several force ranges. The pattern data of related DC
events must be reloaded in case the containing pattern is reused for another range.
This may significantly increase the test time.
The recommendation applies to all DC events that change the force- or clamp value
or range or the measurement range.
Examples
The following examples demonstrate how to set up an FVI16 pin for a standard current
measurement.
The three example are set up in a three-step sequence of connecting the pin and
applying the basic setup, measuring the requested parameter, and disconnecting in a
separate task. This sequence is suitable for FVI16‑specific tests, since very often more
than one setup has to be applied and more than one measurement has to be carried
out before the pin is disconnected again.
These examples are available in the following sections:
Example 1: SmartRDI, pattern‑based programming
Pattern‑based programming using SmartRDI is the recommended solution that
requires the least amount of code and on the other hand delivers the most stable
result in terms of timing.
Example 2: SmartRDI, code‑based programming
Code‑based programming using SmartRDI needs some more code and must follow
the structure of the wrapped test method APIs.
Example 3: Test method API SPMU_TASK
This example is based on the test method APIs and is strongly tied to the structure
of the underlying commands.
The code of the three examples generates the same measurement sequence for the
programmed pin. If you use the Trace Function to compare the code‑based SmartRDI
example and the example based on the test method APIs, you will get the same output
in the MCDLog file.

complete measurement sequences including connecting and disconnecting the
programmed pins.
The tasks spmuTask_connect as well as spmuTask_measure of the example must therefore
define the same mode() and connectState() and ensure that the same ranges are
used, although the first task is used only to connect and activate the pin while the
second task is used only for the measuring:
spmuTask_connect: The combination of relay("NT") and
execMode(TM::FORCE_ON) of the connect task enables switching of the output
relays and activation of the pin. A measurement is not supported by this task.
spmuTask_measure: Relay control is set to "NO" to inhibit actions of the output
relays. The pin remains therefore connected after the task has been performed.
execMode(TM::PVAL) causes that the requested value is measured and returned
as per pin value and pass/fail results.
spmuTask_disconnect: The combination of relay("NT") and
execMode(TM::FORCE_OFF) causes that the pin is disconnected. Although no
