PVI8 ganged
Multiple PVI8 channels can be connected in parallel to increase the output current. This
is called "ganging".
Topic 143546

Ganging
Ganged PVI8 channels can be setup under user control or under software control:
User‑controlled ganging:
Several channels are simply connected in parallel and similar settings are applied.
This can lead to an undefined distribution of the current to the individual channels
and may result in unstable output voltages and invalid current measurements.
Modifying the settings may improve the behavior but needs more attention of the
user.
Software‑controlled ganging:
The parallel connected channels are defined as ganging group in the pin definitions
of SmarTest. The ganging group is accessed as single pin. The on‑board-ganging
controller distributes the total output current equally between the ganged channels.
This solution will show a stable output signal and provides reliable current
measurements without applying special setups as required for ganging under user
control.
We recommend therefore, always setting up software controlled ganging.
Ganging characteristics
The following items must be considered when ganging PVI8 channels:
PVI8 cards support ganging up to eight consecutive channels.
Ganging is supported across two cards.
The serial connection (stacking) of two groups of ganged channels is allowed.
Ganging is supported in the 10 A force current range.
Ganging is supported in the bipolar (±40 V) force voltage range.
Reusing of ganged pins as single pins or in other ganging groups is supported in
the PMU operating mode. For more information refer to PVI8 ganged on the fly.
The time measurement unit (TMU) is not supported for software‑controlled
ganging.

On-board ganging controller
The on-board ganging controller is used to balance the total output current between
the ganged channels. This is done by varying the forced voltages of the individual
channels a little. The clamp current retains the original functionality and has no effect on
this current-balancing process.
In a ganged configuration, the channel with the lowest number acts as the master
channel. The master channel creates an analog signal which is proportional to his
output current and feeds this signal to the first slave. Each slave transmits this signal to
the next slave in the group and uses the signal to adjust its own current to be identical
with the master's current. The analog signal is routed via internal connections if the next
slave is located on the same card and must be routed via a DUT board connection if the
next slave is located on another card.
Four pogo pins are available to feed the master's signal to the slaves. The GANG_IN_H
and GANG_IN_L pins of the pogo interface are connected to the ganging controller
input of the first channel of the card. Internal connections are used for the following
channels of the card: The ganging controller output of each channel is connected to the
ganging controller input of the next channel. The ganging controller output of the last
channel is connected to the GANG_OUT_H and GANG_OUT_L pogo pins.
Additional DUT board connections for the ganging controller may be required:
No additional ganging controller connections are required if all ganged channels of
the group are located on the same card.
Additional connections are required if the ganged channels of the group are
located on two cards. The GANG_OUT_H and GANG_OUT_L pogo pins of the card
where the master channel is located must be connected to the GANG_IN_H and
GANG_IN_L pogo pins of the other card.
The ganging controller connections do not replace the connections of the force lines
and sense lines of the ganged channels as described below. These connections are
independent of the ganging controller connections and are required for each of the
ganged channels.
1)

DUT board connections
Some connections of the force lines and sense lines of ganged channels are required on
the DUT board:
The HF# (high force) pins of the ganged channels and the LF# (low force) pins of
the ganged channels must be connected together on the DUT board.
The same parallel connection is required for the HS# (high sense) pins and the LS#
(low sense) pins of the ganged channels. The combined force lines and sense lines
must be connected together at the DUT.
These DUT board connections may be routed via optional relay multiplexers.
The guard line (GUARD#) may be used to shield the high fore and high sense lines
up to the DUT. The guard lines of ganged channels may also be routed via optional
relay multiplexers. The guard lines of the individual channels of a ganging group
must not be connected together. for more information, refer to PVI8 wiring of
guard.
Application notes
Resolution of the clamp current
All channels of a ganged group are programmed to the same values. The resolution
of the programmed clamp current is the resolution of a single channel multiplied by
the number of ganged channels.
Loopback to the same card is not supported
A loopback connection of the ganging control lines from the last channel of a card
to the first channel of the same card is not supported by the software. The master
channel and the last slave channel must always be located on different cards if cross-
card ganging is used.

PVI8 ganged on the fly
Multiple PVI8 channels can be connected in parallel to increase the output current. This
is called "ganging". "Ganging on the fly" means that channels may be ganged,
unganged, and reused in other configurations according to the needs of the test flow.
Different settings can be applied to the individual channels of the disbanded ganging
groups and the channels may be connected to different pins of the DUT or used in other
ganging groups.
Software
Reusing PVI8 channels requires the definition of another connection set in the Digital
Pins editor and therefore is supported for PVI8 channels in PMU operating mode. The
connection sets are used like different DUT board traces.
A PVI8 channel must be disconnected before it can be reused in another ganging group
or as single pin.
 The digital pins editor automatically sorts the channel numbers of a ganging group
from the lowest value to the highest value. The channel number in this context means
the combination of the three digit pogo number and the two digit channel number of
the pogo block.

Topic 143722

Required DUT board hardware
"Ganging on the fly" needs the same DUT board hardware as ganging with fixed
channel assignment to ganging groups:
The ganged channels must be connected in parallel at the related DUT pins.
The ganging controller lines must be connected in case the ganged channels are
located on two different cards.
Additional hardware is required for "Ganging on the fly" to provide different DUT board
traces:
The connections from the pogo pins of the card to the DUT must be routed via
additional relays.
These relays must be inserted for the force lines and the sense lines.
Additional relays may be required for the guard lines.
Additional relays may be required for the ganging controller lines if cross-card
ganging is used and the participating cards change in different ganging groups.
The ganging controller connections between the cards require no additional hardware
to support the "Ganging on the fly": Internal switches are opened in case the channels
operate in "unganged" mode.
The ganging controller connections for ganging within one card require no additional
hardware to support the "Ganging on the fly": Internal switches are opened or closed in
case the channels operate in "unganged" mode or in other ganging groups.
Application note
Ganging on the fly and DC events in pattern
For pins that use connection sets, pattern containing DC events must be set up as a
multiport burst. A port can only contain pins with the same connection set or only
pins with the default connection set. The use of a multiport timing is required if
connection sets are defined for the related pins.
For more information regarding the default connection set, refer to Digital Pins
editor and DFPN, DFPN?

PVI8 pulsed operation
Each channel of the PVI8 card can force a current pulse of up to ±10 A in pulsed mode
for a short time of some milliseconds. The available energy budget of the on-board
Topic 143856

energy storages, the power dissipation of the main driver and a maximum duty cycle
must be considered for the high current pulses.
The pulsed operation is supported for all operating modes and connection states as
described in topic PVI8 operating modes. This means that a PVI8 channel always can
drive a current of up to ±10 A for a short time. The PVI8 operating modes and
connection states are used to optimize the dynamic behavior for different types of
pulsed tests and measurements.
Energy storages
The energy for pulses up to ±10 A is provided by an on-board battery of capacitors as
energy storage.
The PVI8 card monitors the energy storage and immediately disconnects a channel if the
available energy is not sufficient for the regulation of the output voltage or current.
Power dissipation
The power dissipation of the main driver is calculated from the voltage drop at the main
driver and the current. It depends therefore on the raw supply voltage, the output
voltage, and the actual output current.
Each PVI8 channel features an on-board monitor that checks the power dissipation of
the main driver. A channel that exceeds the maximum power dissipation will
immediately be disconnected and must be connected again.

Maximum pulse time
The maximum pulse time depends on the maximum power dissipation of the main
driver and the available energy that is stored in the on-board energy storage.
The diagram above shows the relationship between the output current, the output
voltage, and the maximum pulse length. The shown waveforms are defined by the
maximum power dissipation of the main driver and the discharge characteristics of the
on-board energy storage.
The peaks of some of the waveforms are caused by the maximum power dissipation at
the main driver. A higher output current will discharge the on-board energy storage
faster and therefore reduce the power dissipation at the driver faster. This results
partially in an increased maximum pulse length for higher currents. The waveform on
the right side of the peaks depends mainly on the discharge characteristics of the on-
board energy storage.

Maximum duty cycle
The maximum average duty cycle of a PVI8 channel is 10 % at a current of 10 A. A
maximum value of the duty cycle must be considered to allow the channel to recharge
the on-board energy storage and to let the main drivers cool down. The duty cycle is
considered separately for sourcing and sinking currents.
The duty cycle is the ratio of time when the channel sources or sinks the current and the
time when no current is flowing. For example a current pulse of 1 ms followed by 19 ms
in the high-impedance state results in 5.0 % duty cycle.
The actual output current must be considered for the calculation of the duty cycle. The
maximum duty cycle of a PVI8 channel varies between 10 % for 10 A output current and
100 % (or continuous operation) for a output current of 1 A. The following diagram
shows some examples how the duty cycle is calculated:
The upper waveform shows a 10 A current pulse with a length of 1 ms that is followed
by the next pulse 12 ms after the beginning of the first pulse. This results in a duty cycle
of 1 ms / 12 ms = 8.3 %.
The lower waveform shows a 10 A current pulse with a length of 1 ms followed by
another 1 ms pulse of 5 A. The third pulse is started again 12 ms after the first pulse.
This configuration results in a duty cycle of 12.5 % for force current of 10 A. The delay
from the beginning of the first pulse to the beginning of the third pulse must be
changed from 12 ms to 15 ms to fulfill the requirements of the PVI8 channel.

PVI8 specific setup tasks
This section describes some of the typical setup tasks for the DC Scale PVI8 card.
Topic 149007

PVI8 operating modes
The PVI8 card supports the DPS operating mode and the PMU operating mode. The
PVI8 operating mode is defined by the pin type that has been used in the Pin setting
editors. The operating mode can be set individually for each channel of the card.
Pin configuration for the DPS operating mode
The pin configuration of channel-slot DC Scale cards is slightly different to that of a
DPS-slot device power supply. To configure a PVI8 pin for the DPS operating mode
you must specify the pin as DPS with positive polarity. For details see DC Scale pin
(DPS mode) setup.
Pin configuration for the PMU operating mode
A PVI8 pin is configured for the PMU operating mode if the channel is defined as
DC Scale pin using the Digital Pins editor. To configure a PVI8 pin for the PMU
operating mode you must specify the pin type as dc and the pin mode as SIG.
Please refer to DC Scale pin (PMU mode) setup for more information.

PVI8 configuration in the model file
The PVI8 card and pogo blocks must be defined in the POGOCABLING section and in
the DPS section of the model file as follows:
The eight channels of the PVI8 card are routed to two pogo blocks A and B. Pogo block
A is used for channel 1 to 4. Pogo block B is used for channel 5 to 8. For more
information refer to PVI8 pogo pin assignment. For PVI8, only pogo block A is to be
defined in the model file. SmarTest assigns all eight channels to this block.
These rules are to be followed:
Only the first pogo block A must be defined in the model file. The second pogo
block B must not be defined in the model file.
Pogo block A must be mounted at a location with an odd number.
Pogo block B must be mounted at the location with the next even number. This will
be pogo block A location + 1.
Example:
POGOCABLING
    311: pogoblocks="305"
    ...
    ...
DPS
    30501-30508: type = DCS-PVI8
The example above shows pogo block A on position 305. Pogo block B on position 306
must not be defined in the model file.
Note  The DPS section shows that all eight channels are assigned to pogo block 305
although they are physically wired to the two blocks 305 and 306 via the PVI8 pogo
cable.
Summary:
Pogo cable: The eight channels are assigned to two pogo blocks A and B.
For more information refer to PVI8 pogo pin assignment.
Installation: Pogo block A must be mounted at a location with an odd number.
Pogo block B must be mounted at block A location + 1.
Model file: Only the first pogo block A must be defined in the model file.
SmarTest: All eight channels are assigned to pogo block A.
Note  Although PVI8 can be replaced by the new DC Scale FVI16 card, the FVI16
and PVI8 cannot be operated at the same time in the same system.

Channel memory, minimum period, and multiport setup
The total memory per PVI8 channel is 56 MB. If you run out of available channel
memory, we recommend using a separate port for the PVI8 pins to minimize the
number of vectors.
The minimum vector period for a PVI8 channel is 20 ns. In case of period
incompatibilities in a test program, we recommend using a separate timing port for the
PVI8 pins.
For further details see also Multiport testing with multiple clock domains and Minimum
period / maximum frequency of the sequencer.

Safety and self-protection
The safety of the user and the self-protection of the card require that actions are
performed automatically by the control logic of the card or channels. These actions
cannot be blocked or disabled. Some flags indicate these irregular operating conditions.
For more information refer to DPS power flags - get...() functions.
Flag Description
Low headroom Trigger: The floating on-board energy storage provides not enough headroom
for the correct function of the output buffer.
Action: The related channel is disconnected.
Availability: The flag is available per channel.
API: DPS_AUX_TASK.getLowHeadroom()
Overpower / Overcurrent /
Power budget exceeded
Trigger: The maximum power dissipation of the output buffer is exceeded.
Action: The related channel is disconnected.
Availability: The flag is available per channel.
API: DPS_AUX_TASK.getOvercurrent()
Safety line Trigger: No external control voltage is applied to the safety circuit. The on-board
safety circuit is disabled.
Action: The unipolar (0.5 V to 80 V) force voltage range is disabled for all
channels.
All channels of the card are disconnected.
Availability: The safety circuit is available per card. The flag can be read per channel
and always shows the same state for all channels of the card.
API: DPS_AUX_TASK.getSafetyLine()
Unregulated Trigger: The output buffer is outside the normal operating range and cannot
maintain the force value.
Action: The related channel is disconnected.
Availability: The flag is available per channel.
API: DPS_AUX_TASK.getUnregulated()

Enabling a channel after it has been disconnected
The procedure described below should be followed for channels that have been
disconnected by the channel controller for reasons of safety or for the self-protection of
the card:
Ensure that the reason for the disconnection has been eliminated. Possible actions
are:
Apply the control voltage to the safety circuit.
Ensure that the floating on-board energy storage has been charged before a
new pulse is started.
Reduce the high current pulse length to reduce the power dissipation.
The following actions are required in case a channel has been disconnected in the
test flow:
Check the state of the flags using the APIs described in DPS power flags - get...
() functions.
Disconnect the channel by SmarTest. The related error message will be shown
in the report window and the status flags will be cleared.
Connect the channel.
The following actions are required in case a channel has been disconnected when
working with the hardware view:
For a channel in the PMU operating mode: Start a dummy measurement in the
ADC sub-panel with the relay action set to NT.
For a channel in the DPS operating mode: Click onto the Disconnect button in
the toolbar of the Eclipse Work Center.
Disconnecting the channel will cause that the related error message is shown in
the report window and will clear the status flags.
Connect the channel.

DC event status
The command TSST? - (TeSt STatus) returns global information about the DC event
related results of the last executed test, and also provides the accumulated status
information about all recorded measurements. A test point pattern must have been
executed for DC Scale pins. The accumulated information is cleared at the begin of a
functional test. The accumulated flags remain then valid until the begin of the next
functional test.
TSST? returns a twofold reply. One informs about the test results, the other about the
test status:
Test result flags:
The functionality of some test result related flags can be enabled or disabled for
specific measurement events using member functions of the DC events. Functions
to enable or disabled the flags are for example
...clampChecks()
...outOfRangeCheck()
The flags are cleared with the start of the next functional test.
Test status flags:
The test status related flags cannot be enabled or disabled. These flags are
accumulated for the complete functional test. The flags are cleared with the start of
the next functional test.

PVI8 programming - Ganging
Multiple PVI8 channels can be connected in parallel to increase the output current. This
is called "ganging". PVI8 cards support ganging up to eight consecutive channels across
two cards. Ganging is supported in the 10 A force current range.
Ganging characteristics
The following items must be considered when ganging PVI8 channels:
PVI8 cards support ganging up to eight consecutive channels.
Ganging is supported across two cards.
The serial connection (stacking) of two groups of ganged channels is allowed.
Ganging is supported in the 10 A force current range.
Ganging is supported in the bipolar (±40 V) force voltage range.
Reusing of ganged pins as single pins or in other ganging groups is supported in
the PMU operating mode. For more information refer to PVI8 ganged on the fly.
The time measurement unit (TMU) is not supported for software‑controlled
ganging.
DPS operating mode
Ganging groups for PVI8 channels in DPS operating mode are defined in the DPS Pins
editor. For more information refer to DC Scale pin (DPS mode) setup.

PVI8 programming - Kelvin test unit / sense
connection test
The PVI8 card features a Kelvin test unit (or sense-connection test unit), which can be
used to verify that the force lines and sense lines are connected together on the DUT
board or at the DUT pins.
Basic data
Some basic data must be considered when using the Kelvin test unit:
The Kelvin test unit is available per channel.
The threshold for the pass/fail decision is about 50 kΩ.
The test current is about 5 µA.
The maximum capacitance between the force lines and the corresponding sense
lines is 5 nF.
The internal 100 kΩ resistor between the force lines and the corresponding sense
lines limits the maximum test voltage of the open connection to about 0.5 V.
The test is done serially for the high sense line and the low sense line.
The floating test current supplies allow a parallel test on all available PVI8 channels.
The test can be performed only in the disconnected state of the selected pins.
API overview
The function checkKelvinStatusParallel() of class HW_STATE initiates a sense connection
test on the defined pins to verify that the force lines and sense lines are connected
together on the DUT board or at the DUT pins. The test is performed in parallel for all
active sites. The function returns a go/no-go result for each configured site in a single
integer array.
Function HW_STATE.checkKelvinStatus() initiates a sense connection test for the site in
focus. The function returns individual results for all tested pins in two integer arrays for
the positive and for the negative line.
Test Method Library overview
The DC test method DpsConnectivity of the Test Method Library is provided to control
the Kelvin test unit and to read and judge the state of the measurement.
Topic 146288

Application note
Kelvin connection test in a test flow
A continuity test, which is normally performed at the beginning of a test flow, may
use PVI8 channels. The continuity test will show a reliable result only if both the force
and sense pins of the PVI8 channels are connected properly. Therefore, we
recommend implementing a Kelvin test at the beginning of a test flow before the
continuity test is performed.

PVI8 supports hardware based averaging of measurements. The average of multiple

the related sub-topics.
The effective maximum sample frequency is the ADC sample frequency of ~ 500
ksps divided by the number of averaged samples.

Application notes
Minimize parasitic leakage currents by guarding
The card provides one guard line per channel. This guard line should be used to
shield the HF# and HS# lines on the DUT board. The guard line carries the same
voltage as the HF# line and therefore minimizes the parasitic leakage current and
improves the accuracy of low-current measurements. For more information refer to
PVI8 guard.
Averaging over a defined sample time
PVI8 supports hardware based averaging. The sample frequency is defined by the
ADC and the number of settable samples is limited to power of 2 values. Therefore,
the pattern‑based sampling of the PVI8 digitizer must be used if averaging for an
exactly defined time like a power line cycle is required.

Minimize the input current in high impedance measurement mode
In the high impedance voltage measurement mode the forced voltage should be set
to the expected voltage to minimize the input leakage in case the DUT board
connection from the HF# line to the HS# line is closed for the measurement.
Averaging over a defined sample time
PVI8 supports hardware based averaging. The sample frequency is defined by the
ADC and the number of settable samples is limited to power of 2 values. Therefore,
the pattern‑based sampling of the PVI8 digitizer must be used if averaging for an
exactly defined time like a power line cycle is required.
Surge tracker and HIMP mode
When using PVI8 in high impedance (HIMP) measurement mode, the surge tracker is
silently disabled. A user notification (Error or warning) is omitted, to avoid any
interrupt in the test flow. The old status of the surge tracker is automatically restored
if another measurement mode is selected.

Application notes
Open the safety interlock with unipolar force voltage range selected
In some applications, the safety interlock will be opened normally at the end of a test
flow. The reason may be that a manually operated DUT socket with isolation cover is
used or that a handler or prober opens the connection at the end of the test. In
these cases, it is recommended to change the force voltage range from the
unidirectional mode to the bidirectional mode at the end of the flow before the
safety interlock is opened.
Using the hardware view to clear active flags of a PVI8 in PMU operating mode
The output relays of a PVI8 channel in PMU operating mode may be sometimes
locked without any error message shown and disconnecting and reconnecting all
pins does not change this behavior. The ADC sub-panel of the hardware view must
be used in this case to start a dummy measurement with the relay action set to NT.
This will disconnect the channel, read and clear possibly active flags and show the
related error message. The following connection will then work as expected and the
relays are accessible again.
Using the 80 V range after the safety circuit has been toggled
In case the safety line will be opened and closed again while the PVI8 is
disconnected but the test program is already loaded, the PVI8 can only proceed in
the 40 V range. This behavior may be occur if the DUT board is changed with the test
program already loaded.
In this case, you must unlocked the supply by executing a setup or measurement in
the 40 V range and disconnecting the supply again. After that, you can proceed in
the originally selected 80 V range.

Application notes
TMU and surge tracker
The TMU (Time measurement unit) and the surge tracker cannot be used in parallel.
The two functionalities use the same comparator set that can be assigned to only
one of them at the same time.
Dummy vectors between EVENT_TMU_MEAS and the edge to be measured
Some dummy vectors are required to set up and activate the measurement unit.
Minimum four vectors are required between the EVENT_TMU_MEAS and the first
comparator event to be recorded. Comparator events are not recorded and will be
lost if these vectors are omitted.
Number of vectors before pattern end
Due to inter module communication it is required to keep the pattern running for a
short time after the last TMU related DC event. The actual required time depends on
the setup. In case of insufficient number of vectors before pattern stop, a
communication error might occur.
Rules:
Do not specify less than 41 vectors.
60 vectors should work for most of the applications.
If the test execution stops with a communication error, add additional vectors at the
end of the pattern to ensure the error is not caused by an insufficient number of
vectors.
The TMU and the DC event controlled measurements utilize the same path to
transfer data from the front end to the test processor. The combination of the two
kinds of measurements in the same pattern burst on the same pin may increase the
required number of vectors before the pattern end.
TMU and API "waitTMUFinished"
Executing API TMU_PINS.waitTMUfinished() after running the TMU measurement
pattern is mandatory but you cannot rely on the returned status information. The API
TMU_RESULTS.getNumberOfMeasuredSamples() is to be used for checking the
number of valid samples.
The PVI8 TMU is optimized for single shot measurements. The front end will
automatically append eight dummy samples at the end of a measurement to enable
the TMU handling single shot measurements. The dummy samples cannot be
uploaded but are taken into account by API TMU_PINS.waitTMUfinished().
Missing samples

PVI8 TMU is able to handle up to eight missing samples. If the sample count,
programmed by API TMU_PINS.setNumSamples(), cannot be acquired, the following
behavior will be observed:
1 … 8 samples missing: The captured values can be uploaded.
More than eight samples missing: No values can be uploaded. The API
TMU_RESULTS.getNumberOfMeasuredSamples() will return 0 for the respective
pin and all measurements.

PVI8 Use Case - Stacking
In order to achieve a higher output voltage, serial connection of multiple PVI8 channels

down
The TMU should be disconnected after the measurement.
Setup
We strongly recommended disconnecting the PVI8 TMU after the measurement. This
will minimize the bias current of the related DUT pins, prevent the TMU from being
damaged by voltages that exceed the maximum operating range and avoids potential
issues with the PVI8 surge tracker.
Topic 146644

Sample data
The PVI8 TMU provides no ready-to-use results but raw sample data that must be
converted into the required results like pulse-time or rise-time. The sample values of
one pattern refer all to the same origin that has been defined by one
EVENT_TMU_START in the pattern.
The diagram above shows the forced input signal that is referenced to the origin of the
pattern time scale. The recorded TMU samples are marked with red circles and are
referenced to the red time scale of the recorded samples. The delay between the two
time scales is defined by the position of the EVENT_TMU_START in the pattern.
Arming of the TMU is assigned to edge r7 of the vector cycle where the
EVENT_TMU_START is placed. The default (and fixed) edge position for DC Scale pins is
the beginning of the cycle.

mode
This section describes the setting to be done using EVENT_TMU_MEAS.mode().
Events of mode TM::END_MEAS must be used once per pattern execution. The event
marks the end of the TMU measurements for the actual pattern. You cannot close a
measurement window by using this mode. A dummy measurement event can be used
instead and the samples of the dummy event need to be ignored. Using more than one
event of mode END_MEAS may lead to unexpected results.

PVI8 Use Case - DC events and vectors
This section describes the structure of DC events and the pattern required for the
capturing of the time stamps.
DC events
PVI8 TMU is mainly controlled by DC events.
Event sequence
For proper function of PVI8 TMU, it is mandatory to keep the following event sequence:
EVENT_TMU_CONF
EVENT_TMU_START
EVENT_TMU_MEAS (This event may appear multiple times)
EVENT_TMU_MEAS with mode set to TM::END_MEAS (Must appear once)
Violation of this event sequence can lead to DPS communication error and loss of data.
Event EVENT_TMU_START
The EVENT_TMU_START has two functions. First it arms the PVI8 TMU and secondly it
marks the origin of the TMU samples.
Note  Wavetable modifications which are required for TMUs of digital pins are not
required and not possible for PVI8.
Topic 146655

Event EVENT_TMU_MEAS.mode(TM::END_MEAS)
The EVENT_TMU_MEAS with mode set to TM::END_MEAS is a special event to terminate
the active measurements and prepare data upload. It triggers the PVI8 to generate a
number of dummy samples. The PVI8 will generate 8 dummy samples to achieve proper
data transfer to the capture memory. The samples are not visible for the users.
Application note
Number of vectors before pattern end
Due to inter module communication it is required to keep the pattern running for a
short time after the last TMU related DC event. The actual required time depends on
the setup. In case of insufficient number of vectors before pattern stop, a
communication error might occur.
Rules:
Do not specify less than 41 vectors.
60 vectors should work for most of the applications.
If the test execution stops with a communication error, add additional vectors at the
end of the pattern to ensure the error is not caused by an insufficient number of
vectors.
The TMU and the DC event controlled measurements utilize the same path to
transfer data from the front end to the test processor. The combination of the two
kinds of measurements in the same pattern burst on the same pin may increase the
required number of vectors before the pattern end.

Root cause
No samples have been recorded for example, due to wrong comparator settings).
No samples of any measurement are available from the selected shot.
The first measurement does not contain at least one sample.
The pattern was not terminated with EVENT_TMU_MEAS.mode(TM::END_MEAS) and
there is just one measurement event in the pattern. The correct root cause cannot
be detected in this case.
Recommended steps
Ensure first that the measurement creates samples. As long as the first
measurement has not at least one sample, no data can be retrieved.
Check the input signal.
Check the thresholds.
Confirm the DC event sequence in the pattern:
1. EVENT_TMU_START
2. EVENT_TMU_MEAS
3. EVENT_TMU_MEAS.mode(TM::END_MEAS)

If this error occurs, no samples of any measurement are available; even if some
measurements were executed successfully.

warning: TDC MeasEnd event is missing

The number of vectors after the end event was not sufficient.
Recommended steps
Add EVENT_TMU_MEAS with mode TM::END_MEAS to the pattern.
Increase the number of vectors between the end event and the pattern end to 60.
Depending on the actual setting, a lower number of vectors may also be sufficient.

1st measurement terminated without any timestamp
Message
error: 1st measurement terminated without any timestamp.
Root cause
The first measurement of several measurements did not contain any measurement.
Recommended steps
Check the input signal and comparator settings of the first measurement.
Check the DC event sequence in the pattern.
Details
If this error occurs, no samples of any measurement are available.
Result memory contains less samples than expected
Message
error: Result memory contains less samples than expected
Root cause
The TMU frontend piped more samples to the TMU backend than expected. The TMU
backend is not able to process all received samples.
Possible reasons for this behavior:
The number of samples has been set to different values in APIs
TMU_PINS.setNumSamples() and EVENT_TMU_MEAS.samples().
The time difference between two samples of the measurement signal was less than
20 ns and the backend was not able to record all events.
The number of samples is not stable due to noise of the signal or non-deterministic
behavior of the DUT.
Recommended steps
Verify that TMU_PINS.setNumSamples() and EVENT_TMU_MEAS.samples() are set to
the same value.
Optimize the TMU thresholds to minimize the effect of the noise.

Details
The uploaded data may contain invalid samples that are caused by noise.

TMU status
APIs that read the status of the PVI8 TMU need to be treated carefully. The API
implementation currently relies on the behavior of digital pin TMUs. As PVI8 introduced
some new features, the full functionality of the status APIs may not be given or

Topic 146660

Application notes
TMU and API "waitTMUFinished"
Executing API TMU_PINS.waitTMUfinished() after running the TMU measurement
pattern is mandatory but you cannot rely on the returned status information. The API
TMU_RESULTS.getNumberOfMeasuredSamples() is to be used for checking the
number of valid samples.
The PVI8 TMU is optimized for single shot measurements. The front end will
automatically append eight dummy samples at the end of a measurement to enable
the TMU handling single shot measurements. The dummy samples cannot be
uploaded but are taken into account by API TMU_PINS.waitTMUfinished().
Time stamps are late and the measurements show a time difference of about 25 ns
This debugging hint applies to SmarTest versions before 7.3.1.1.
Root cause
The time stamps are no real samples but dummy samples that are generated by
EVENT_TMU_MEAS.mode(TM::END_MEAS) to fit to the needs of the test
processors.
How to deal with
To confirm that the samples are dummy samples, insert some dummy
vectors before the end event and confirm that the time stamps move
respectively.
Ensure always, that time stamps are smaller than the dummy stamps, to
avoid miss judgments. This is especially important, when using calculated
values for judgments.
The reason why dummy cycles are returned is the lack of other samples in
the first arming.
DC Scale UHC4 / UHC4T card
 Download specifications PDF: V93000 SOC Device Power Supplies
The DC Scale UHC4 / UHC4T is a device power supply card that addresses your needs
for ultra high currents.
The UHC4 version is not supported with SmarTest 7.10.
There are two versions of the UHC4. Both are part of the DC Scale power supplies family:
UHC4: Supported with SmarTest 6.5.0 and up to, but excluding, 7.10.0
UHC4T: Supported with SmarTest 7.3.2 and later
Topic 106867

A V93000 test system can contain only one or the other version, but not both at the
same time. Both versions provide the same functionality.
Although both UHC4 and UHC4T are DC Scale cards and can be installed in V93000
Smart Scale systems, UHC4 is no Smart Scale card. This affects some test configurations
such as matchloops. UHC4T features the next generation test processor and is a Smart
Scale card.
The DC Scale UHC4 / UHC4T power supply card has 4 channels per card that provide a
maximum current of 40 A each (160 A per card). The ganging of channels across UHC4 /
UHC4T cards allows even higher currents.
During the execution of a test flow the UHC4 / UHC4T acts like a normal device power
supply (DPS). The main difference between a normal DPS and an ultra high current DPS
is the need to protect the ATE equipment in case of a shortage, for example the needles
on a probe card. Therefore, the UHC4 / UHC4T card provides additionally:
Several alarms to protect your test equipment
A high-speed sampler for differential voltage monitoring
Measurement of voltage drop on force/return line

UHC4 / UHC4T functionality and features
The DC Scale UHC4 / UHC4T has four channels per card, which provide a maximum
current of 40 A each (160 A per card).
The DC Scale UHC4 / UHC4T is compatible to the DC Scale cards VI32 and DPS32. Like
these, the UHC4 / UHC4T can be used configured for the DPS operating mode and used
as device power supply (DPS) and as voltmeter. Unlike the other DC Scale cards, the
UHC4 / UHC4T does not support the PMU operating mode.
To find a summary of all supported resource parameters in the level file, refer to
DPSPINS resources.
The UHC4 / UHC4T supports static and dynamic (sequencer‑controlled) measurements
mode. In DPS operating mode you can use UHC4 / UHC4T like a standard DPS to supply
devices with power during a test flow. It takes part, for example, in connect/disconnect
sequences and in the set activation.

Power modes
Furthermore the DC Scale UHC4 / UHC4T operates in two power modes:
High power mode with a maximum current capability of 40 A
Precision mode with a maximum current capability of 1.5 A, but with a higher
current measurement accuracy
For details see UHC4 / UHC4T power modes.
Measurement modes
UHC4 / UHC4T supports current and voltage measurements. Both measurement modes
can be programmed as static measurement or as dynamic measurement.
For details see UHC4 / UHC4T measurement modes.
For voltage measurements you must apply the high impedance (himp) connect state.
UHC4 features
Special features of the UHC4 / UHC4T include:
Ganging of any number of installed channels across either UHC4 or UHC4T cards in
a free selectable sequence to achieve even higher currents
High-speed sampler (digitizer) on each channel for differential voltage
measurements and waveform capturing
Protection features like alarms and measurement of voltage drops
Fast preload mode
Peak mode
For details see UHC4 / UHC4T features.
Equations
To use all features of DC Scale UHC4 / UHC4T cards you must use equations. The
equation based level setup provides UHC4 / UHC4T specific parameters, for example
several connect states. For details see Equation based level setup and DPSPINS
resources.
Channel sharing
You can share the same DC Scale UHC4 / UHC4T channel or gang of channels between
several sites. This allows to save DPS channels by supplying external circuits on the DUT
board with just one channel. See also Test Method Programs and Sharing Channels
Between Several Sites.

Profiling in Hardware view
Profiling (DC profiling) allows you to measure and display current and voltage
waveforms during pattern execution in the Hardware perspective. Current and voltage
profiling is supported for all channels.
On DC Scale UHC4T cards (not UHC4), profiling for multiport setups does not stop when
the DPS part is finished. On these cards, profiling stops when the longest running port is
finished. This allows to minimize DPS memory consumption. You need to create an
empty port pattern though.
On UHC4T cards you can also do profiling when the pattern contains CLEV or CTIM
commands. This is different to the UHC4 card, where static measurements are not
allowed in this case.
Software identifier
The return of the OPT? query differs depending on the installed version:
The software identifier for the DC Scale UHC4 is DCS-UHC4.
The software identifier for the DC Scale UHC4T is DCS-UHC4T.
Test processor, memory, and data analysis features
Setup and measurement sequences are controlled by test processors. There are two
test processors, each with multiple cores. Each channel is controlled by a separate
core.
The test processor memory is shared between setups, testpoints, waveforms, digital
patterns, and sample data or measurement results.
The memory available per UHC4 channel for the test program is approximately 112
MB for a typical setup.
The memory available per UHC4T channel for the test program is approximately
216 MB for a typical setup.
Several alarm flags are available to indicate irregular operating conditions.
Hardware based averaging is available for better accuracy and throughput.
A built-in result analysis is available that checks the measurement data against user
specified test limits.

UHC4 / UHC4T power modes
The DC Scale UHC4 / UHC4T supports two power modes that define the maximum
current capability and the current measurement accuracy.
The two power modes are defined as follows:
High-power mode
In the high-power mode the maximum current capability is 40 A per channel. In
high-power mode you can force and measure.
Precision mode
In the precision mode the maximum current capability is 1.5 A per channel, but with
a higher current measurement accuracy than in high-power mode. In precision
mode you can force and measure small currents for continuity checks and Idd
measurements.
You can switch between both modes without limitation. A disconnect is required except
for unganged measurements.
Selecting the power modes
The system chooses automatically the applicable power mode depending on the
specified current. One of the modes, either the high-power mode or the precision mode,
is always active for force and measure. During the range transition from 1.5 A to 40 A
both modes are active to avoid glitches.
Topic 107323

Selecting the Precision mode temporarily
The following APIs may be applied for measuring the current temporarily in the
Precision mode:
Use API DPS_PIN_TASK.measurementMode(TM::MEASURE_CURRENT_UNGANGED)
for changing to the unganged measurement mode and activating the Precision
mode.
Note: The unganged measurement mode removes temporarily ganged channels
from a ganged group and additionally activates the Precision mode for a single
channel. The measurement mode must therefore be set to
TM::MEASURE_CURRENT_UNGANGED although the measurement is performed on a
single channel.
Limit the maximum current to a 1500 mA or lower using APIs DPS_PIN_TASK.min().
Selecting the Precision mode permanently
The following setup can be applied for measuring the current permanently in the
Precision mode:
Specify an iout_clamp_rng = 1500 (or smaller) and connect_state = ungang in
the DPSPINS block of the level equations.
CONNECT (or DISCONNECT followed by CONNECT if already connected).

UHC4 / UHC4T measurement modes
UHC4 / UHC4T supports current and voltage measurements. Both measurement modes
can be programmed as static measurement or as dynamic measurement. And both can
be run in high-power mode and in precision mode (see UHC4 /UHC4T power modes).
Static measurement
Static current measurements
When programming a static current measurement for UHC4 or UHC4T, keep in
mind:
A pin name may refer to a gang.
Topic 107324

Depending on the DPS-set, different current ranges can be active.
All connected channels, except those that are unganged, participate in the
measurement.
Static current measurements are supported for the connect states norm
(normal), and ungang (unganged).
For hdig norm_hdig,and himp connect states (sampler/digitizer, normal with
sampler/digitizer, high impedance), current measurements are not supported.
For static measurements the UHC4 / UHC4T has a special ungang connect
state. In this state only those channels of a gang are connected, which are
necessary to supply the device with the required current. You can use this
connect state, for example, to detect a DUT board or device with shorts. For
details on this "unganging" see UHC4 / UHC4T features.
Static voltage measurements
In the connect states norm and himp (normal, high impedance), the master
channel of a gang is used for static voltage measurements.
In the connect states hdig and norm_hdig (sampler/digitizer, normal with
sampler/digitizer) you can select the first sampler of a channel gang (master
channel) or all connected samplers.
For static measurements refer also to PSLR, PSLR? - (Power Supply Level Ranges) and
DPSPINS resources.
Dynamic measurement
To set up dynamic measurements you can use the Pattern Tools. The setup is similar to
Pin Scale digital card measurements.
Dynamic measurements are supported for the connect states norm, himp, hdig,and
norm_hdig. There is a special "ungang" mode for dynamic measurements which
switches to precision mode (see UHC4 power modes). You can use this "unganging" to
improve accuracy for current measurements.
Dynamic current measurements
For hdigand himp connect states, current measurements are not supported.
Dynamic voltage measurements
For normand himp connect states the master channel of a gang is used.
For hdigand norm_hdig connect states you can select the master channel or
all connected channels. In a second step you can select the results of any single
channel.

High-Speed sampler
The UHC4 / UHC4T features a high-speed sampler for differential voltage monitoring.
You can use the UHC4 / UHC4T high-speed sampler (also referred to as high-speed
digitizer) to measure, for example, the supply voltage drop during the execution of
critical device patterns.
You can use the high-speed sampler alternatively to the UHC4/UHC4T-ADC. When the
high-speed sampler is active, the ADC is inactive.
You can execute high-speed sampler measurements while the DPS part, the
UHC4/UHC4T-ADC, is connected or disconnected. The high-speed sampler has its own
signal pogo pins. For details see UHC4 / UHC4T pogo pin assignment.
In high-power mode and in precision mode, the UHC4 / UHC4T card uses the same
high-power pogo pins.
A typical application for the high-speed sampler are AC scan tests. During an AC scan, a
device sometimes sinks a large current before the UHC4 / UHC4T can react. To prove the
test for these drops, which can be the reason for marginal tests, you can use the high-
speed sampler.

Fast preload mode
The fast preload mode allows to charge large capacities in a short time.
If the 40 A current force range is selected, a current of 40 A maximum is forced for a
programmable time (0 - 10 ms with a resolution of 0.001 ms), independent of the actual
current limit setting. The preload starts when the DUT is connected. Afterwards the
UHC4 / UHC4T returns to its previous state. The fast preload settings are identical for all
channels of a gang group. You cannot use this mode for voltage changes.
The fast preload mode must be either enabled with a firmware command (the default is
disabled) or with a programmed time in an equation. For details see ms_fast_preload in
DPSPINS resources.
CAUTION For the time the fast preload mode is active, the overvoltage
protection is inactive.

Peak mode
In peak mode a peak current is delivered for a few microseconds. The peak current can
be larger than 40 A.
This mode minimizes the step response time after a load change. The peak mode
cannot be switched off.
In constant current mode the maximum current is equal to the actually programmed
current limit.
Voltmeter mode
To use the voltmeter mode you must apply the himp connect state (high impedance
measurement mode).
The high impedance measurement mode opens the AC_Force and H_Imp relays, and
closes the AC_Sense relay. In this mode neither voltage nor current is forced.
The input leakage currents determine the impedance. See also UHC4 specifications and
UHC4T specifications.

Ganging and unganging DC Scale UHC4 or UHC4T channels
To achieve a higher output current, you can operate multiple channels of DC Scale cards
in parallel, known as ganging. Ganging is the combining of multiple DPS channels to
provide a higher current than a single DPS channel could provide.
The UHC4 and the UHC4T supports the channel ganging on the card and the ganging of
channels across multiple cards of the same type. You cannot gang UHC4 channels with
UHC4T channels.
You also cannot gang UHC4 and UHC4T channels with other DPS channels.
Each UHC4 / UHC4T card has an input and an output line, which must be connected via
the DUT board. The UHC4 / UHC4T has a "double" pogo assembly, one with the input
line, the other with the output line (see UHC4 / UHC4T pogo pin assignment).
When ganging on the card, the input and output lines of each channel are connected in
the order:
Card: input -> channel1 -> output channel1 -> input channel2 -> channel2 -> .... ->
channel4 -> output
To gang across either UHC4 or UHC4T cards you must build a non-interrupted ganging
chain. The sequence of the cards is freely definable. The channel with the open input
connection is the master of the ganged channels. For further details see UHC4 / UHC4T
specific setup tasks and UHC4 / UHC4T pogo pin assignment.
The following rules apply when ganging UHC4 / UHC4T channels:
You can switch every output/input connection for example, ganging of channel 1,2
and channel 3,4 is possible).
You can gang any number of either UHC4 or UHC4T cards within a system without
any order restriction.
You cannot exceed the maximum current per UHC4 / UHC4T card (160 A @ 2.0 V).
For the "unganging" of UHC4 / UHC4T cards you have to differentiate between two
cases:
Unganging during measurement (see also DPS32 and VI32):

In this case the low and high pass/fail limits of the current measurement tell the
system which current is expected. The gang is reduced to the smallest gang (or
measurement range) which can provide the expected (measurement) current.
This unganging of UHC4 / UHC4T channels does not disrupt the supply of voltages
to the device.
Ungang connect state:
This state cannot be combined with the above "Unganging during measurement".
The current limits (force setup) tell the system which current is expected. The gang
is reduced to the smallest gang (or measurement range) which can provide the
(expected) force current. This kind of unganging is a safety feature, because during
connect the current clamp is not active (see "Peak mode" above). So only the
number of channels in a gang or the precision mode (if there is only one channel)
limit the current flowing.
You can use the ungang connect state as part of a power-on sequence. First
activate a setup with small currents and try to connect in ungang connect state. If
there is no shortage disconnect again, and then activate a setup with a larger
current.
Sink power < Source power
Within limits, the sink power on UHC4 / UHC4T cards, that are connected to the same
DC-DC, can be larger than the source power. The limits for each channel of a card are:
0.6 V: 40 A
1.0 V: 7 A
2.5 V: 4 A
4.0 V: 2 A
If the sink power is higher, the test system shuts down. See also UHC4 specifications and
UHC4T specifications.

UHC4 / UHC4T protection features
The main difference between an ultra high current DPS and a normal DPS is the need to
protect the ATE equipment in case of a shortage, for example the needles on a probe
card.
Therefore, the UHC4 / UHC4T DPS provides a disconnect flag and additional features to
protect your test equipment, for example:
Overvoltage protection
Safety line
Current limiter protection (UHC4T only) avoids that the system is switched of due to
overpower.
Disconnect flag
If any of the protection features triggers a disconnection of a UHC4 / UHC4T channel, it
also sets a disconnect flag.
For example, if a user-defined voltage drop is reached (that is, the absolute value is too
high), the AC relay is opened, the channel disconnects, and the disconnect flag is set.
When the disconnect flag was set, you must reconnect before you can continue.
Overvoltage protection (sense line per channel)
The overvoltage protection provided by UHC4 / UHC4T continuously measures and
compares the force voltage at output and the force voltage at load. If the difference
between the two voltage values is above the limit, the output channel disconnects after
a time delay. In this case both the overvoltage protection flag and the disconnect flag
are set.
The voltage limit for the disconnect can be programmed from 0 mV to 500 mV in steps
of 1 mV. The overvoltage protection is always on, in all current ranges, except for the
time the fast preload mode is on.
There are separate comparators for both the force and the return line on both the
source and the sink path (4 in total). They compare the voltage drop on the source path
and voltage drop on the return path at sense point.
For a force drop the UHC4 / UHC4T measures the voltage drop between force
(AC_Force) and sense+ (AC_Sense) at output of the UHC4 /UHC4T card. For a return
drop it measures between sense- and ground (PGND).
See also DPSPINS resources (max_voltage_drop_force/return).

Safety line
A safety line on the UHC4 / UHC4T is fed to the DUT board and pulled high by +5 V. To
operate the UHC4 / UHC4T this voltage must be constantly high. The safety lines of
several UHC4 / UHC4T cards can be connected on the DUT board. When the voltage
drops, all UHC4 / UHC4T channels of the involved cards are disconnected. In this case,
the DUT board disconnect flag is set.
Since the disconnection is controlled by the hardware and cannot be delayed or
prevented by the software, it reliably protects the DUT, the probes or DUT sockets and
the DUT board. The hardware‑controlled shutdown must be very fast and is therefore
always a high‑impedance (HIZ) disconnect. This means that any capacities cannot be
discharged by the DPS but only through the DUT or a resistor on the DUT board.
You can use this mechanism to simultaneously disconnect all UHC4 / UHC4T channels
by an external switch.
The safety line is independent from the DUT board connect sensor. But this mechanism
can also be used to detect a DUT board which is not properly connected or assembled.
In this case the UHC4 / UHC4T disconnects.
Channel overpower/overcurrent
The maximum current per UHC4 card cannot be exceeded. The channel disconnects in
case the current rises above the limit. Only the UHC4T provides a current limiter
protection mode (see below).
Current limiter protection (UHC4T only)
The UHC4T provides an integrated current limiter protection mode. When activated, the
shutdown of the system due to too high power consumption of the UHC4T card can be
avoided. When a protection case occurs, a flag is set and the related channel is
disconnected to interrupt the current flowing into the DUT before the maximum power
consumption of the card is exceeded.
Note that a protection case indicates an overload of the 12V card cage power rail which
supplies up to two UHC4T cards installed in adjacent card cage slots.

In case one UHC4T
triggers the protection mode, an UHC4T present in the neighbor slot (even/odd slot
pair) is affected in its operation as well. Triggering of the protection mode should
therefore be seen as an indicator of an overload condition which must be avoided by
defining slower voltage ramps.
For more information, see section Current limiter protection (UHC4T only) in UHC4 /
UHC4T specific setup tasks.

Other flags and alarms
The following security features also set the disconnect flag:
Constant current flag and constant voltage flag
The constant current check is always active. You can specify a delay of up to 0.065
seconds before the channel disconnects.
See also DPSPINS resources (disable_const_curr_check / ms_const_curr_disconnect).
Unregulated state
In case of an unregulated state condition, the affected channel is reported and
disconnected.
Sense connection test
The UHC4 / UHC4T channels features a sense connection test unit, which is also know as
Kelvin test unit.
Kelvin test or sense connection test means that the connection from the force lines to
the sense lines on the DUT board or at the DUT pins is verified with a small test current
applied. A PASS/FAIL result is returned.
The Kelvin test unit applies a small test current to the tested force to sense (FS)
connection and measures the voltage drop between the two lines. The measured
voltage is used as criterion for the pass/fail decision and should be near 0.0 V for a good
FS connection.
For information regarding the sense connection check, refer to DC test method
DpsConnectivity and to API HW_STATE.checkKelvinStatusParallel().
See also Sense connection test in UHC4 / UHC4T recommendations for use.

UHC4 / UHC4T hardware overview
The DC Scale UHC4 / UHC4T is a device power supply card for ultra high currents. It has
four channels per card, which provide a maximum current of 40 A each (160 A per card)
in high-power mode; in precision mode the maximum current capability is 1.5 A per
channel.
A high-speed sampler (digitizer) on each channel allows differential voltage
measurements and waveform capturing. The high-speed sampler has its own signal
pogo pins.

The UHC4 / UHC4T cards must be defined in the DPS section and in the POGOCABLING
section of the model file. The software identifiers in the DPS section differ depending on
the installed version:

DCS-UHC4T
Note  UHC4 and UHC4T cannot be operated at the same time in the same system.
Two different pogo cable assemblies are available for the UHC4 / UHC4T card. The two
pogo cable assemblies must be defined in the POGOCABLING section of the model files
as follows:
DC Scale UHC4/UHC4T with E8013UHP cable
The four channels are routed to two pogo blocks that are combined into a single
unit, thereby occupying an S1/S2 pogo block pair. Only the S1 position must be
entered in the model file, the software blocks the adjacent S2 position
automatically.

POGOCABLING

    ...
    ...
DPS

    ...
    ...
The example above shows that only pogo block A is defined as block 230 in the
POGOCABLING section. Pogo Block B is automatically assigned to the adjacent S2
position 430.
Note  The DPS section shows that all four channels are assigned to pogo block
230 although they are physically wired to the two blocks 230 and 430.
DC Scale UHC4/UHC4T with E8024UHPS cable
In contrast to E8013UHP cable, the four channels are routed to two pogo blocks

Ganging
The parallel connection of DC Scale UHC4 / UHC4T channels is supported for any
number of successive channels within a card and any number of cards within a test
head.
Cross-card ganging requires a daisy chain connection from the last channel of a card to
the first channel of the next card within the ganging group: On the DUT board, the
"Gang_out" pin is to be wired to the "Gang_in" pin of the next card.
The combination of UHC4 and UHC4T within the same ganging group is not supported.
For more information, refer to section Ganging and unganging DC Scale UHC4 or
UHC4T channels in UHC4 / UHC4T features.
Ganging groups are defined in the DPS Pins editor:
To specify ganging on the same card, you can specify the range of channels to be
ganged by "-" (hyphen).
To specify ganging across UHC4 / UHC4T cards, separate the channel ranges on the
cards by comma (,):
On the DUT board, pin "Gang_out" on physical pogo block "A" must be connected
to "Gang_in" on physical block "B" of the next card. This will connect the ganging
controller output of the first card (P4 = Tester channel ...04) to the ganging
controller input (P1 = Tester channel ...01) of the next card.
Alternatively you can use the DDIC, DDIC? - (Define DUT Interface Connection) and
DFPS, DFPS? - (DeFine Power Supply) commands in the pin configuration file to specify
the ganging across either UHC4 or UHC4T cards. For example:
hp93000,config,0.1
DDIC CONN,(230GO,227GI)
...
DFPS (23004,22701),POS,(VDDCI)

At the beginning of the pin configuration file the DDIC command describes the DUT
board traces that are needed to support ganging across either UHC4 or UHC4T cards.
First the DDIC command must define, which connections are available on the DUT
board, then the gang can be defined by the DFPS command.
Flush vectors at the end of a pattern (UHC4T)
Due to inter module communication it is required to keep the pattern running for a
short time after the last ADC measurement related DC event. The actual required time or
number of flush vectors depends on the setup. In case of insufficient number of vectors
before pattern stop, a communication error might occur and measurement results might
be lost.
The number of required flush vectors depends on the average count and the pattern
cycle time as follows:
Minimum number of vectors = 40 + ( (2.2 μs * average) / period )
where: average = Programmed average count
period = Cycle time of the pattern
The calculated number is the minimum number of vectors that is required between the
last measure event and the end of the pattern.
Note that the TSST? - (TeSt STatus) firmware command can be used to check for missing
samples: Bit 8 is set if a measurement is lost.

Load changes
The peak mode of the UHC4 / UHC4T minimizes the step response time after a load
change, but the load change delivers a peak current for a few microseconds.
One of the UHC4 / UHC4T protection features is the automatic disconnection of a
channel if the currents increase too high during connect or disconnect (load change).
The voltage ramp parameters (vout_rise_..., vout_fall_...) allow you to specify setup times
and slew rates separately for rising and falling DPS voltage transitions, and thus avoid
disconnection of channels due to too high currents.

Topic 343699

Layout recommendations
"Fail safe" protection
The card features a "+5V" pin that must be connected to an adequate +5 V supply
to operate the card. The pin may be used to ensure, that the DUT board is correctly
connected: No DUT board = no fire up!
For more information, refer to the +5 V pin in UHC4 / UHC4T DUT board wiring
schemes.
Sense lines
Run sense the lines to the DUT.
Kelvin sockets or separate probes for the power / force lines and the sense lines are
to be used to ensure that the force and sense lines are connected directly at the
DUT.
Note  Add 100 Ω ... 1 kΩ force to sense bypass resistors on the DUT board to
protect against open loop.
We recommend also, adding 4.7 … 10 nF bypass capacitors for high-frequency
feedback. These capacitors are required only to minimize high-frequency noise
on the sense lines.
CAUTION The UHC4 / UHC4T channels feature integrated sense connection
test units (a.k.a. Force Sense Check or Kelvin test unit) for both the power sense
pin and the ground sense pin. These units provide the only way to check the
connection of the sense lines at the DUT by applying a small test current. Bypass
resistors on the DUT board prevent this sense connection test.
We recommend therefore, connecting normally closed solid-state relays in series
to the bypass resistors. The normally closed relays should be opened only for
performing the sense connection test.
Some hints for dimensioning the bypass resistors:

The value of the bypass resistor should fit to the residual sense path resistance
from the bypass resistor to the DUT.
The value of a bypass resistor should be as close as possible to the 100 Ω but
must be at least ten times bigger than the residual sense path resistance from
the bypass resistor to the DUT.
With passive copper traces and regular sockets, the resistance from the bypass
resistor to the DUT will likely be in the low Ohms range, so 100 Ω for the bypass
resistor will work well. Nevertheless there may be more sophisticated circuitry
like switches, leading to a residual resistance of some tens of ohms in the sense
path. A sense path resistance of 50 Ω leads to a minimum bypass resistor of 500
Ω to met the "ten times bigger" rule.
Bulk- and bypass capacitors
Keep capacitors "in range". Do not use the "if in doubt take 10x more" classic power
supply rule.
Recommended values for the capacitors are 1000 .. 2000 μF per 40 A rail.
Capacitors types
Use only the recommended ceramic capacitors and electrolytic capacitors. For more
information, refer to UHC4 / UHC4T capacitor requirements.

Test setup recommendations
Sense connection test
Carefully perform the sense connection check using the on-board Kelvin test unit.
The Kelvin test unit applies a small test current to the sense lines to evaluate the
resistance from the sense path via the sense probe or the sense contact of a Kelvin
socket and via the DUT back to the force line.
Note  The purpose of the Kelvin test unit is to ensure that when the DUT is
contacted, the high-impedance sense line is connected to the force line at the
DUT with a sufficiently low contact resistance. Due to the high input impedance
of the sense line, the fixed threshold of several kilo-Ohms will be sufficiently low.
The Kelvin test unit is the only resource that can perform a reliable sense
connection test with a defined test current applied.
Since connections and hardware on the DUT board can sabotage the test of the
sense connections, we recommend that you check the functionality of the test
without DUT and with open sense connections. All tested sense connections
must fail in this verification.
Note  The sense connection test cannot return a meaningful result if bypass
resistors connect the force lines to the sense lines on the DUT board. We strongly
recommend, connecting normally closed solid-state relays in series to the bypass
resistors. The relays should be opened only for the sense connection test.
SmarTest 7 only: For information regarding the sense connection check, refer to DC
test method DpsConnectivity and to API HW_STATE.checkKelvinStatusParallel().
We recommend verifying the results of the sense connection with open connections
at least once while the test program is debugged: No DUT must be connected for
the verification and Kelvin sockets should temporarily be removed from the
receptacles. The verification should ensure, that the Kelvin test unit can detect all
open sense connections and is not obstructed by bypass resistors or other
connections between force and sense lines.
Maximum voltage drop on the force lines
Monitor the force to sense voltage drop.
SmarTest 7 only: For information regarding the force to sense voltage drop, refer to
parameters max_voltage_drop_force and max_voltage_drop_return in
DPSPINS resources.

Power up / down sequence
Power up and power down sequencing and stepping needs your attention. Your
device may not like reverse biasing, like one rail up, the other down!

Current limit and current clamp settings
In SmarTest 7, use the DC Scale limits settings and the clamp current settings with
care. The nominal current settings define the DC current but the supply can handle
up to 2 … 3 times the set value as surge currents!
Slew rate control
Use gradual ramp statements (slew rate control) with large capacitors.
Discharging capacitors
Use active disconnect mode for discharging capacitors.
SmarTest 7 only: For more information, refer to keyword offcurr and option
act_min in DPSPINS resources.

General recommendations
Ganging
The UHC4 / UHC4T card nicely gangs, also across cards, as long as the gang group
members are adjacent in consecutive order. For the assignment of the channels,
refer to UHC4 / UHC4T pogo pin assignment.
If the design permits power granularities: Take advantage of it!
Most preferred solution would be a "per core supply rail", realistically the package or
design may not have such flexibility, so a 16 core design may have 4 rails.
Do not gang UHC4 / UHC4T channels, unless you expect to touch 70 … 80% of the
rated current. The card works well with 30 A static current and you still have lots of
headroom for charge peaks.
At the same time: The maximum source/sink current per channel of 40 A per channel
is a hard limit.
Further information
There is some more information available in the TDC that will help you designing a
DUT board for the UHC4 / UHC4T card:
UHC4 / UHC4T capacitor requirements introduces to capacitor network design.
UHC4 / UHC4T capacitor examples shows some typical capacitors and their
measured attributes.
UHC4 / UHC4T low-level high-current design shows some basics for correctly
design the UHC4 / UHC4T connections on the DUT board and provides the
UHC4 / UHC4T impedance calculation spreadsheet which spills out decoupling
requirements (bulk capacitors and ceramic bypass capacitors) for a given load
condition.
Topic Layout considerations for UHC4 / UHC4T elaborates on power planes
stack-up, low inductance power plane and socket design, footprint
recommendations, capacitor placement and sense line routing.
Finally, the application paper Stability of ATE supplies with different ATE test
fixtures - UHC4 Stability and special features discusses the challenges of stability
of high speed ATE DUT supplies.

Things to watch out
To our experience, the following items are the most commonly areas of failure which
lead to undesired behavior of the UHC4 / UHC4T card.
Bulk capacitance
Too small bulk capacitance with an equivalent series resistance (ESR) that is too high
leads to a poor load step response.
Ceramic capacitance
Too much of ceramic capacitance or improper ratio of bulk capacitors and ceramic
capacitors may lead to an oscillating UHC4/UHC4T channel.
Connection of sense lines
Improper connection of sense lines results in incorrect measurement of the DUT
voltage.
Impedance of the force path
High impedance of the force path on the DUT board leads to a high voltage drop.
Note that a UHC4/UHC4 channel is disconnected if the force voltage drop exceeds a
certain limit (default 250mV, max. programmable to 500mV).
Voltage ramps
If no voltage ramps are used, high current peaks can occur when the DUT board
capacitors are discharged to disconnect. This can lead to the system being switched
off.
Note that in SmarTest 7 some parameters of the DPSPINS resources or of the PSSR
firmware command are programmed as inverse slew rate in milliseconds per volt
(ms/V). Setting the inverse slew rate for falling edges to very small values or 0 ms/V
is supported by SmarTest, but results in very high slew rates (V/s), which can cause
the behavior described above.
act_min disconnect state not used (SmarTest 7 only)
Not using the act_min disconnect state (SmarTest 7 only) to ensure safe
disconnection can lead to undesired behavior. For more information, refer to
keyword offcurr in DPSPINS resources.

Pogo cable assemblies
There are two variants of pogo cables available, which enables the two pogo blocks per
card to be either placed in adjacent locations or split between different locations on the
DUT board.
E8013UHP pogo cable assembly: Single pogo block unit with two pogo blocks.
The lower pogo pin (S1) is always block A; for example A=230, B=430:
Block A must be in an S1 position.
Block B must be in the adjacent S2 position.
The second pair of channels (Block B = Channel P1/P2) always gets assigned a pogo
block number that is by 200 higher than the first pair. If the model file sets the
physical pogo block number to 230, then the software automatically uses the pogo
block locations 230 and 430.
E8024UHPS pogo cable assembly: Connects the UHC4 / UHC4T channels via two
separate pogo blocks A and B to the DUT. The two pogo blocks can be installed in
any position on the DUT interface, within the limitation presented by the cable
length.
The E8024UHPS cable is fully compatible with the E8013UHP cable when the A and B
pogo blocks are installed in adjacent positions on the DUT interface. In such a case, no
change to the model file is required when the E8024UHPS cable is used instead of the
E8013UHP cable.

Operating modes
DC Scale VI32 cards have two operating modes:
DPS operating mode (DPS+)
In DPS operating mode you can use the DC Scale VI32 cards like a standard DPS, to
supply devices with power during the execution of a test flow.
To find a summary of all supported resource parameters in the level file, refer to
DPSPINS resources.
PMU operating mode (SIG)
In PMU operating mode you can use the DC Scale VI32 cards like a standard PMU
to temporarily supply power for a single testsuite or for a group of testsuites.
A VI32 channel can be configured either for the DPS operating mode or for the PMU
operating mode but not for both.
In both operating modes each of the 32 channels of every power supply card can
source and sink current at a programmed voltage,
measure the voltages and currents supplied,
supply power to external circuits on a load board,
be programmed in a testsuite for a certain test,
be shared between different sites (channel sharing),
be ganged to increase the supply current,
do connectivity checks,
check the status of the device power supply.
The DPS operating mode is a superset of the PMU operating mode and has some
additional capabilities. Only in DPS operating mode the DC Scale VI32 power supply
cards can
take part in connect and disconnect sequences, and
take part in the set activation.
Note  In PMU mode a DC Scale VI32 card does not take part in standard
connect and disconnect sequences, and cannot take part in the set activation,
although you can add DC Scale VI32 cards to user-defined connect and
disconnect sequences.

Measurement modes
DC Scale VI32 cards support voltage and current measurements in both the DPS and
PMU operating modes.
For measurements in DPS operating mode see Measuring current or voltage in DPS
operating mode.
For measurements in PMU operating mode see Measuring current or voltage in PMU
operating mode.
Ganging DC Scale VI32 channels
To achieve a higher output current, you can operate multiple channels of DC Scale VI32
cards in parallel, known as ganging. Ganging is the combining of multiple DPS channels
to provide a higher current than a single DPS channel could provide.
The actual ganging, that is the physical parallel connection, is done on the DUT board.
For details see Connecting DPS channels in parallel.
To gang DC Scale channels you use either the Pin Configuration tool or firmware
commands.
You can gang any number of successive channels (max. 32) within a DC Scale VI32
card. Ganged channels must be located on the same card. You cannot gang across
VI32 cards.
You can configure these successive channels in up to 16 gang groups.
For details on the setup procedure see Digital Pins editor.
For the firmware commands see DFPS, DFPS? - (DeFine Power Supply) for ganging in
DPS operating mode and DFPN, DFPN? - (DeFine Pin Name) for ganging in PMU
operating mode.
Each gang group consists of a master channel and one or more slave channels. The
master channel distributes two analog signals to the slave channels. One signal is the
target voltage on the output, and the second is a voltage that represents the current of
the master. The slave channels will adjust their own voltage to match the current of the
master channel.
Ganging supplies higher currents to a device. To avoid a negative effect on measure-
current accuracy, for example for IDD-measurements, you can temporarily ungang
channels during measurement. The unganging differs for the DPS and PMU operating
modes. For details see Measuring current or voltage in DPS operating mode, and
Measuring current or voltage in PMU operating mode.

Channel sharing
You can share the same DC Scale channel between several sites.
This allows to save DPS channels and to supply external circuits on the DUT board.
See also Test Method Programs and Sharing Channels Between Several Sites.
Licenses overview
For an overview of all licensed V93000 products by Product ID, as they are referenced on
the Entitlement Certificates, see Licensed V93000 products.

Focus calibration for DC Scale VI32 cards
The DC Scale VI32 card has two high accuracy voltage measurement modes:
2 voltage ranges [0V-3V], [3V-6V]
200uV accuracy
These high accuracy measurement modes require a focus calibration of the pins
involved. The focus calibration for DC Scale VI32 cards is a fully automated process and
requires no operator interaction. The advantages of this process are:
It does not require an undocking of the DUT board.
It does not require a reload of settings after focus calibration.
It triggers a focus calibration on request for specific channels.
It triggers an internal digital multimeter (DMM) calibration when needed.
It can be integrated in test methods and user programs.
For the focus calibration you require an Keysight 3458A Digital Multimeter (DMM) with

Integrating focus calibration in a test flow
To be automatically executed, the focus calibration must be part of a test flow. The focus
calibration is executed in parallel on all specified channels and takes around 5 minutes.
The number of channels is insignificant.
About this task
To integrate the focus calibration in a test flow, you use the Flow Sequence Editor.
When inserting the focus calibration test method in a test flow, make sure it is the first
element of the test flow. This ensures that the focus calibration is always up-to-date.
Note  No errors or warnings are issued if the focus calibration data is outdated or
not available.
Note  Be aware that the Keysight 3458A Digital Multimeter (DMM) also executes
the Auto Calibration every 5 days. For warm-up the DMM must be running at least 4
hours to ensure correct calibration. You cannot enforce the Auto Cal manually. It is
started automatically during the focus calibration if required. Auto calibration of the
DMM takes 15 to 20 minutes. Any failure during this process leads to a complete re-
run.

Voltage
Description
The PEHMV Focus Cal step does a high-precision calibration of the "measure voltage"
functionality of the VI32 power supply (Pin PMU at other channel types) using an
external DMM.
The HPPMU of the clock board is connected to the channel via the DC-sense line.
Simultaneously the DC-sense line is connected to an external DMM.
The HPPMU provides several voltages that are simultaneously measured by the channel
ADC and the external Keysight 3458A DMM. A third-order transfer function for the
channel ADC is calculated.
