Connecting and disconnecting in DPS
operating mode
When connecting and disconnecting in DPS operating mode, DC Scale cards behave like
a standard device power supply.
When connected, it forces the programmed power supply voltage (vout). The current is
limited to the connect current limit (ilimit).
The DC Scale card must be disconnected before changing any of the following:
a voltage force range (vout_frc_rng)
a clamp current range (iout_clamp_rng)
If the DC Scale card is still connected, you cannot activate a dps set that contains one of
above changes. To avoid damages to your device or the DUT board, the system will
Topic 94156

display an error message in the report window instead.
The rule above applies not to the DC Scale AVI64 card and not to the DC Scale FVI16
card: AVI64 and FVI16 support changing the force voltage range and the force current
range in connected state both for the DPS operating mode and for the PMU operating
mode.

To achieve a higher output current, you can gang multiple DC Scale channels (see

effect on current-measurement accuracy.
To achieve a higher accuracy, for example for IDDQ-measurements, you can temporarily

To temporarily ungang channels in DPS mode, use the

PMU operating mode of DC Scale cards
In PMU operating mode you can use DC Scale channels like a standard PMU to
temporarily supply power in a single testsuite or for a group of testsuites. Each channel
can source and sink current at a programmed voltage, and each channel can measure
the voltages and currents supplied.
A DC Scale channel is configured for the PMU operating mode if the channel is defined
as a DC Scale pin using the Digital Pins editor. The Type parameter must be set to dc
and the Mode parameter must be set to SIG.
Topic 94454

Connect/Disconnect
Note  In PMU operating mode a DC Scale pin does not take part in standard
connect and disconnect sequences, and cannot take part in the set activation.
A DC Scale pin must be manually connected and disconnected using test method APIs
in a test suite, the User-defined disconnect sequence, the Special test suite
bin_disconnect, or the Multibin SmartDisconnect test suite.
Note  On startup SmarTest always performs a standard disconnect.

Measuring current or voltage in PMU
operating mode
VFIM - Voltage Force / Current Measure
In PMU operating mode you can use DC Scale cards like a standard PMU.
In voltage force mode, to perform current measurements you must specify a clamp
current. Specify both the minimum and maximum pass current values and units (mA or
µA).
For the voltage and current range specifications of the DC Scale cards see DC Scale
DPS32 specifications and DC Scale VI32 specifications.
For test method programming details see SPMU_PIN_TASK.
Topic 105773

VFIM_UNGANGED - Voltage Force / Current Measure
Unganged
To achieve a higher output current, you can gang multiple DC Scale channels (see
Ganging DC Scale channels). But the higher current of ganged channels has a negative
effect on accuracy.
To achieve a higher accuracy, for example for IDDQ-measurements, you can temporarily
ungang channels before measurement.
To temporarily ungang channels in PMU operating mode use the VFIM_UNGANGED
parameter of the SPMU_PIN_TASK test method API.
If the current range of a ganging group of DC Scale pins is larger than the measured
current, you can use only part of the pins within this group to perform the
measurement. Selecting the "VFIM_UNGANGED" mode automatically ungangs not
needed channels, based on the min() max() limits.
For details see SPMU_PIN_TASK.
IFVM - Current Force / Voltage Measure
In PMU operating mode you can use DC Scale cards like a standard PMU.
In current force mode, to perform voltage measurements you must specify a clamp
voltage. Specify both the minimum and maximum pass voltage values and units (mV or
V).
For the voltage and current range specifications of the DC Scale cards see DC Scale
DPS32 specifications and DC Scale VI32 specifications.
For test method programming details see SPMU_PIN_TASK.
VM_HIZ - High Impedance Voltage Measure
In PMU operating mode DC Scale cards support high impedance voltage measurements
(neither voltage nor current is forced).
In high impedance measurement mode (himp) DC Scale power supply cards act like a
voltmeter.
The high impedance measurement mode opens the AC_Force and H_Imp relays, and
closes the AC_Sense relay.
Note  You cannot use this feature for a DPS-slot DPS.
For details on equations see Level Equations.
For a non-equation based setup you must use the PSLR firmware command.

VM_HIZ_HAC - High Impedance High Accuracy Voltage
Measure
In PMU operating mode the DC Scale VI32 card also supports high-impedance, high-
accuracy voltage measurements (neither voltage nor current is forced).
You select the voltage range via min()/max() limits. The possible ranges are 0V - 3V and
3V - 6V.
High accuracy voltage measurements are supported for the high impedance
measurement (himp) mode. See "VM_HIZ - High Impedance Voltage Measure" above.
Note  You cannot use this feature for a DPS-slot DPS or the DPS32 card.
For test method programming details see SPMU_PIN_TASK. For details on equations see
Level Equations.
For a non-equation based setup you must use the PSLR firmware command.

Filling rules for DC Scale cards
DC Scale cards can reside in any channel card slot of a card cage but the following filling
rules must be respected for V93000 Smart Scale and Pin Scale systems.
A pair of adjacent odd and even slots must be filled with the same card type. For
details see Card compatibility.
A UHC4 / UHC4T cannot reside next to an HC-DPS card, because of physical
limitations.
On the large DUT interface, no UHC4 / UHC4T pogo block is allowed in the four
outer half-groups. For details see UHC4 / UHC4T standard configuration.
The UHC4 and UHC4T are not supported in a V93000 test head at the same time.
Install one or the other.
These filling rules apply only to V93000 Smart Scale and Pin Scale systems.

Except for the UHC4T, DC Scale cards can coexist with any other device power supply in
a test head. The UHC4T can be used only in Smart Scale systems. It is not supported
with PS400, PS800, or PS3600 digital cards.

Ganging on the fly and connection sets
In order to achieve a higher output current, parallel connection of multiple DC channels
is supported. This is called "ganging". "Ganging on the fly" means that channels may be
ganged, unganged, and reused in other configurations according to the needs of the
testflow. Reusing of DC channels requires different connection set definitions.

Connection set
The Connection Set adds the ability to define several pins containing the same DC
Scale channel in PMU mode.
These connection sets are defined in the column Connection Set of the Digital Pins
editor. A multiple defined DC Scale channel can be sequentially reused as a single pin or
part of a ganged pin.
Therefore, "Ganging on the fly" requires setting up the DC channels in the PMU
operating mode and defining Connection Set for the reused channels. For more
information on how to set up reused channels, refer to DC Scale pin (PMU mode) setup.
The following screenshot shows how the channels of pins AVI_01, AVI_02, AVI_03 and
AVI_04 (blue-framed) are reused and combined in the AVI_12_gang and AVI_34_gang
(red-framed). Reusing the related channels in the same testflow ("Ganging on the fly")
requires the definition of a "Connection Set" as shown below as AVI_g2.
An empty connection set column (blue-framed) defines the Default Connection-Set.
Note  If reuse of DC Scale channels is not required, explicit definition of connection
sets is not needed. Those pins will be part of the "Default Connection-Set".

setups.

Common timing (limited flexibility)
As the setup of a multiport timing can be comprehensive for cases with multiple
connection sets, a common timing might be used as an alternative.
Note  A common timing uses the same pattern cycle time for all pins and does not
define any ports. Thus, the timing is applied to the single-channel pins, not to the
ports of the connection sets. Therefore, all channels of the ganged pins in the
connection sets must be configured as single-channel pins additionally. Even
though the effort to create a proper multiport timing can be significantly higher than
using a simple common timing, we recommend to create a multiport timing to apply
the correct pattern period to each connection set in a flexible way.
This example uses the same pin configuration as the multiport timing example
(including the same ports). All channels of the pins in connection sets are also
configured as single-channel pins in the default connection set.

General Improvements:
SmartVec upload speed improvement
Before SmartRDI 2.4.5, the DIGCAP read mode uploads data at a speed of 1 bit per word;
SmartRDI 2.4.5 improves this speed to 32 bit per word.
In SmartRDI 2.4.5, the Emap read mode's upload speed is accelerated by changing the
default error map location. This improvement takes effect only if the Emap location is set to
RAM (default).
TMU upload speed improvement
In SmartRDI 2.4.5, the result upload of TMU pins with the same setup is combined. Because data
upload for multiple TMU pins with the same parameters in one RDI_BEGIN()/RDI_END() block is
combined, the upload speed is improved.

TMU Timeout behavior improvement
Before SmartRDI 2.4.5, the TMU time out is set to 50 ms, which means that if the digital TMU does
not get all results, it will wait for 50 ms after the pattern is finished. In SmartRDI 2.4.5, the timeout
of the digital TMU is set to 0 ms, which means that the TMU stops working after the pattern is
finished. To keep the same timeout behavior as SmarTest 2.4.4, a flag is implemented in the
RDI_Configure file.
See the new keyword TMU_TIMEOUT_50ms in SmartRDI: RDI_Configure file.

SmartRDI: Alarm handling for DCVI
SmartRDI features alarm handling for DCVI channels by inserting compare events
between measurements and judging pass or fail based on alarm limit values set in the
alarm setup file.
The following sections are available in this topic:
Overview
Applicable pins
Alarm compare event insertion
Alarm handling on ports
Alarm handling and connection sets
Alarm checks disabled by current threshold
Understanding alarm fails and warnings
Application
Topic 345141

Overview
SmartRDI handles alarms in vForce, iForce, and vPulse or iPulse modes.
In the vForce mode, the voltage is checked and compared whether it is settled around
the expected force value. The following image demonstrates the concept.
In the iForce mode, the voltage is checked and compared whether it is within the
clamp low and high values and the setup limits. The following image demonstrates the
concept.
After the compare, if the actual value is not in the range of the limit values specified in
the alarm setup file, SmartRDI reports an alarm in the report window.
For vPulse and iPulse, the alarm check is added to the level of the pulse after
measurement.
Note  For iForce() and iPulse() scenarios, verify the actual vClamp values first. If the
values are not correct, change them as required. For example, specifying a correct
vClamp value.
rdi.dc(id).pin(pinA).iPulse(300 mA, 0 mA, 300 us).vClamp(-1 V, 3 V).v

Applicable pins
SmartRDI supports pins from the following cards:
AVI64
FVI16
PVI8
DPS128-HC
If a pin is in one of the following status, the alarm checking cannot be applied on it:
Disconnected
High-impedance mode (HiZ)
AVI64 in the digital I/O operating mode

Alarm compare event insertion
SmartRDI automatically inserts alarm checking events into bursts without changing the
coding.
For AVI64 and FVI16 cards, each alarm checking is a vMeas().limit(lo,hi) event.
Automatic setup of vMeasRange() for DPS128 and PVI8 cards:
In SmartRDI 7.5.0, the alarm checking for DPS128 and PVI8 cards is a
vMeasRange().measWait().vMeas().limit(lo,hi) event. This is because these
cards need vMeasRange() to activate them entering the voltage measurement
mode (vMeas mode).
In 7.5.1, SmartRDI will not add
vMeasRange().measWait().vMeas().limit(lo,hi) in the following events:
The first alarm event after RDI_BEGIN.
The first alarm event after a vForce change.
The first alarm event after an iMeasRange() user-defined or added
automatically by SmartRDI alarm handling.
Automatic setup of iMeasRange() for DPS128 and PVI8 cards:
In SmartRDI 7.5.0, if a user-defined iMeas() is executed on an alarm pin, SmartRDI
will generate a warning that tells you to call an iMeasRange() command first
before the iMeas() command within the same execute() action.
In 7.5.1, SmartRDI automatically adds the iMeasRange() command for you in the
code when both of the following conditions are met:
iMeas() is in the voltage measurement mode (vMeas mode).
The vMeas mode (vMeasRange) has already been set by alarm handling.

After a runtime vForce or vClamp value has been performed on a pin, the alarm
compare event will not be added for the pin until the next fixed vForce or vClamp
value appears. The reason is that the target value has been changed.
The basic rule is that all of SmartRDI commands with an ID can trigger an alarm
checking insertion. These commands include but are not limited to:
rdi.func("id"): Inserts a compare pattern after the current pattern.
rdi.smartVec("id"): Inserts a compare pattern after the current pattern.
rdi.tmu("id").pin("digital"): Inserts a compare pattern after the current
ARM pattern.
rdi.tmu("id").pin("DCS"): Insert a compare event inside the current pattern
after ARM event.
rdi.dc("id").pin("DCS"): Insert a compare event inside the current pattern
after MEAS event.

Alarm handling on ports
SmartRDI 7.5.0 does not generate alarms for pins that are not in the same port of
measurement.
SmartRDI 7.5.1 can generate alarms not only for the pins that are in the same port of
measurement also for pins that are not in the same port. This means a measurement
also can trigger the alarm checking on another port besides its own. After the
measurement, the alarm checking event will be added to the port right after a
portSync() event.
The alarm will be added after the first action done in the "alarm" port.

synchronization after alarm compare.

Alarm handling and connection sets
Connection sets are supported for some cards such as AVI64 or FVI16. These connection
sets allow you reusing pins with another name or configuring pins that are otherwise
used as gang group. Reusing channels in gang configurations is called "Ganging on the
fly".
Connection sets are defined in the Connection Set column of the Digital Pins editor. An
empty string parameter defines the default connection set.
For pins that use connection sets, pattern containing DC events must be set up as a
multiport burst. A port can only contain pins with the same connection set or only pins
with the default connection set. The use of a multiport timing is required if connection
sets are defined for the related pins.
If you use alarm handling in combination with connection sets, you must follow these
rules:
If you use connection sets in combination with a single-port pattern, you must
ensure that all pins defined by the currently active alarm set are in the default
connection set.
If alarm handling is required for pins that are defined for another connection set,
you must use multiport programming and assign the pins of the other connection
set to a separate port.
Note  If the channel is disconnected on purpose, SmartRDI will skip alarm handling.
If the disconnect is caused by an erroneous situation, such as missing kelvin
connection, SmartRDI will get this flag and set alarm handling checking.

Alarm checks disabled by current threshold
Starting from SmartRDI 7.5.3, you can define a current threshold to disable alarm checks
globally or per pin.
In the alarm setup file, you can use GlobalDisableAlarmIth to define a global current
threshold value for globally disabling alarm checking actions; or use DisableAlarmIth to
define a current threshold value per pin for disabling alarm checking on a specific pin.
In SmartRDI code, you can use rdi.alarm().globalDisableAlarmIth() or
rdi.alarm().pin(pinA).disableAlarmIth() to define a current threshold value. See the
following example.
Understanding alarm fails and warnings
If an alarm checking fails in a burst, the general burst Pass/Fail result fails too. The
reason is that the alarm pin's fail contributes to the general burst Fail result.
In the Alarm setup file, alarm warnings can be enabled/disabled for printout to the UI
report window by the flag ALARM_FAIL_WARNING = TRUE/FALSE. The warning indicates
an alarm fail.
Normally, a limit violation triggers an alarm fail and a warning. The violation is then
reported in the UI report window if DEBUG_VALUE = TRUE in the alarm setup file.
Furthermore, since the alarm limit violations trigger a pattern fail result on the related
alarm pin, the fail location can be seen in the expanded view of the executed burst by
red dots.
It may, however, happen that an alarm fail and a warning is reported, but there is no
alarm limit violation. Possible reasons are:
A failing match loop, as it sets all pins, including DC and DPS, of the same port to
FAIL.
A Power Supply Accumulated Status failure, please refer to PSAS? - (Power Supply
Accumulated Status). The status can be checked by pressing the "Get Status Flag"
button in the hardware view of the reported pin right after the execution of the
RDI-block that triggered the fail and the warning.

RDI_Configure file:

more information.

Alarm setup file
An alarm setup file contains groups of limit setups for all the pins on which alarm checks
are applied.
The alarm setup file must be stored in the root path or a sub-folder of the loaded
device. We recommend using folder testmethod of the loaded device.
The path to the alarm setup must be defined by keyword
ALARM_HANDLING_DCVI_SETUP_FILE of the SmartRDI: RDI_Configure file.
Topic 345140

Alarm setup file format
In an alarm setup file, a group of setups is called a SET. Each SET has a name and
contains pins to be checked, global limit parameters, and local limit parameters.
An example of the file format:
SET: Specify a set name. The SET name can be any string but DEFAULT is reserved
for default setups.
GlobalLimit...: Represent a global limit parameter.
PINS: Specify a DCVI pin group or pins on which alarm checks are applied.
Limit...: Represent a local limit parameter.
Pay attention to the following points:
Alarm checks are done only for the pins listed in the active SET.
If LimitLo and LimitHi are defined in the file, their values are applied for
vClamp/vForce in alarm checking. The values of other specified parameters will be
ignored, such as GlobalLimitRelForce, LimitRelForce, GlobalLimitRelClamp,
and LimitMinRelClamp.
If there is no GlobalLimitRelForce or LimitRelForce specified in the file, the
value of GlobalLimitMinDisForce or LimitMinDisForce is applied for vForce
checks.
If there is no GlobalLimitMinDisForce or LimitMinDisForce, an error is thrown
in the first run.
If there is no GlobalLimitRelClamp or LimitMinRelClamp, the vClamp values are
used as limits for vClamp checks.

Parameters in the alarm setup file
The parameters used in the alarm setup file can be divided into two categories: global
parameters and local parameters.
Topic 345144

Global parameters
A global parameter defines a global limit value for all the pins in the SET.
GlobalLimitRelForce: Define a global relative limit value for vForce actions. Its
unit can be % (percentage), V or mV.
GlobalLimitMinDisForce: Define a global minimum limit distance when the
GlobalLimitRelForce (%) is applied. Its unit is V or mV.
GlobalLimitRelClamp: Define a global relative limit value for clamp actions. Its
unit can be %, V or mV.
GlobalDisableAlarmIth: Define a global current threshold value for disabling
alarm checking actions. Its unit is μA.
Local parameters
A local parameter defines a limit value for specific pins. This value will overwrite the
global value.
LimitRelForce: Define a relative limit value for vForce actions. Its unit can be %, V
or mV.
LimitMinDisForce: Define a minimum limit distance when LimitRelForce (%) is
applied. Its unit is V or mV.
LimitRelClamp: Define a relative limit value for clamp actions. Its unit can be %, V
or mV.
LimitLo: Define a fixed low limit value. Its unit is V or mV.
LimitHi: Define a fixed high limit value. Its unit is V or mV.
DisableAlarmIth: Define a current threshold value per pin for disabling alarm
checking on the specific pin. Its unit is μA.
Functional changes
Introduced in SmartRDI 7.5.0
SmartRDI 7.5.3: GlobalDisableAlarmIth and DisableAlarmIth to define a current
threshold value for disabling alarm checks globally or per pin.
Limit setup of alarm checking
Low and high limit values are determined by vForce or vClamp related values. For
vForce, the decisive values are vForce, LimitRelForce, and LimitMinDisForce. For vClamp,
the decisive values are vClampLo, vClampHi, and LimitRelClamp.
Topic 345145

Limits for vForce
In the vForce mode, you can use LimitRelForce and LimitMinDisForce to decide
low and high limits.
First, calculate the value of vForce*LimitRelForce (%).
If the value is greater than LimitMinDisForce, calculate LimitLo and LimitHi as follows:
LimitLo = vForce - vForce*LimitRelForce (%)
LimitHi = vForce + vForce*LimitRelForce (%)
If the value is less than LimitMinDisForce, calculate LimitLo and LimitHi as follows:
LimitLo = vForce - LimitMinDisForce
LimitHi = vForce + LimitMinDisForce
If LimitRelForce in V or mV is used, calculate LimitLo and LimitHi as follows:
LimitLo = vForce - LimitRelForce (mV or V)
LimitHi = vForce + LimitRelForce (mV or V)
The following images show the relationship of vForce, low and high limit values when
the limit values are compared to vForce.
LimitRelForce = 5%:
If LimitRelForce = 10%, the valid range gets wider than LimitRelForce = 5%:

Limits for two-sides vClamp on AVI64 or FVI16
When a two-sides vClamp is used on a pin of AVI64 or FVI16, you can use
LimitRelClamp to decide two values of low and high limits.
If you use a percentage value of LimitRelClamp (%), calculate the low and high limit
values as follows:
LimitLo = vClampLo + (vClampHi - vClampLo) * LimitRelClamp (%)
LimitHi = vClampHi - (vClampHi - vClampLo) * LimitRelClamp (%)
If you use a value of LimitRelClamp in V or mV, calculate the low and high values as
follows:
LimitLo = vClampLo + LimitRelClamp (mV or V)
LimitHi = vClampHi - LimitRelClamp (mV or V)
If you do not set a value for LimitRelClamp, the limit values would be the same as the
clamp values.
LimitLo = vClampLo
LimitHi = vClampHi
The following images show the relationship of low and high vClamp values and low and
high limit values when the limit values are compared to vClamp values.
LimitRelClamp = 5%:
If LimitRelClamp = 10%, the valid range gets narrower:

Limits for one-side vClamp on DPS128 or PVI8
When a one-side clamp is performed on a pin of DPS128 or PVI8, only a limit value need
to be determined. The value is either LimitHi or LimitLo. The limit lie in the iForce value.
If iForce is greater than zero, calculate the limit value as follows:
LimitHi = vClamp - vClamp * LimitRelClamp (%)
LimitHi = vClamp - LimitRelClamp (mV or V)
If iForce is less than zero, calculate the limit value as follows:
LimitLo = vClamp + vClamp * LimitRelClamp (%)
LimitLo = vClamp + LimitRelClamp (mV or V)
If iForce is equal to zero, No compare is applied.
Fixed limits
For most of cases as described above, limit values depend on the vForce or vClamp
value in the test program. For special cases, you can directly set the limit values with
LimitHi and LimitLo.

Return value
The pass or fail result is returned:
1 is returned for pass.
0 is returned for fail.
-1 is for "not enabled."
To retrieve the alarm pass or fail result on a pin in the current RDI_BEGIN-RDI_END
block, use rdi.id(string id).getAlarmPassFail(string pin);. The result ID can
be any result ID in this RDI_BEGIN-RDI_END block.
Note  If any of alarm checking events on a pin fails in the burst, the result is fail on
this pin only.
To retrieve the general alarm pass or fail result in the current RDI_BEGIN-RDI_END block,
use rdi.id(string id).getAlarmPassFail();. The result ID can be any result ID in
this RDI_BEGIN-RDI_END block.
Note  The general alarm result is a combination of the results from all valid alarm
pins. As long as any one of the alarm pins fails, the general alarm result fails.
Note  If an alarm checking fails in a burst, the general burst Pass/Fail result will fail
too. The reason is that the alarm pin's fail contributes to the general burst fail result.
Note  If the burst comprises a match loop and the match loop fails on any site, the
alarm results of that site will be reported as fail, even if none of the alarm checks
itself fails.
Note  If an alarm pin has a user-defined measurement, all value results including
alarm measurement values will get uploaded. getValue() and getMultiValue() will not
be impacted. But getBurstValue() will include voltage measurement values and
results of alarm events.
Also see the example in Commands.

SmartRDI: Analog test setup
SmartRDI provides the interface to do the mixed signal test with AV8, AV8+, MBAV8 and
MBAV8+. It provides the class awg() and dgt() to set up the AWG and the digitizer in
the analog cards.
In the pattern‑based mode, all analog events in one RDI_BEGIN()/RDI_END() block
will be generated in one analog set. The generated analog set is named as <
testsuite name> + <block number in this test suite>. The trigger pins are
defined in the Trigger Configuration of the pin configuration file. SmartRDI will find the
corresponding trigger pin for each analog pin, generate the pattern for the trigger pin,
and create the burst pattern for all the trigger pins in the RDI_BEGIN()/RDI_END()
block. You need to define the waveform index 0 for low level and the waveform index 1
for high level for the trigger pin in the timing file. The burst pattern for the trigger pins
will be executed when RDI_END() is executed.
Before an execution, SmartRDI automatically connects relevant pins and also enables
relevant trigger pins. After the execution, SmartRDI runs the disconnect command but
does not proceed with FLUSH at once. The purpose of no immediate FLUSH after an
execution is that SmartRDI does not have to repeatedly run the disconnect and connect
commands if the subsequent RDI_BEGIN/RDI_END block has the same pins that need
connecting and disconnecting.
In the SINGLE mode, each analog event will generate its own analog set and the
software trigger is used in each execute(). The analog waveform output will be kept
on for debugging purpose.

it alive.

execution, and disconnect without flush in analog or RF test.
For analog or RF pins, SmartRDI follows the same rule that it does not disconnect these
pins immediately after an RDI_END() execution.

The code above shows the following main elements of the SmartRDI code structure:
#include "rdi.hpp"
You must include the file rdi.hpp for each test suite that uses SmartRDI.
RDI_INIT()
In each test method class, all code programmed with SmartRDI needs to be put after
RDI_INIT().
RDI block
The RDI block starts with API RDI_BEGIN() and is closed with RDI_END(). The RDI
block holds the RDI commands that are converted as far as possible into individual
pattern and are executed as pattern burst if the execution mode of the block has
been set to the default value TA::BURST.
Note  DO NOT put any code that you would like to run in EACH execution into
the RDI block.
The code inside the RDI block is executed only in the first run after build. This is
required for generating pattern content.
The two macros RDI_BEGIN() and RDI_END() already contain the curly brackets
{ … } that enclose the code within the block. Nevertheless, we recommend using
extra brackets as shown in the example above. This improves the readability of the
code and simplifies correct indentation using the related Eclipse tool.
RDI command
Normal RDI commands begin with the RDI main class rdi, optionally define an RDI
class to be used, followed by one or more member function calls of the defined class
and are closed by rdi.execute() that is a member function of all RDI classes.
An RDI command can be divided into multiple lines using function rdi.cont().

SmartRDI
Setting up DC resources as AWG is like setting up a real AWG. Define a waveform and
then set up a type and a sampling frequency for the waveform.
About this task
The DC resources used as AWG can be DC Scale pins and PPMU.
Before you begin

Procedure
1. Define a waveform with the class anaWaveform.
2. Set up a pin or pins to work as AWG.
a. Specify a port. It is a must setup for PPMU and optional for DC Scale pins.
b. Create a test with the class dc().
c. Specify a pin or pins to work as AWG with pin(). For PPMU, the specified pin
must be the same as defined in the specified port.
d. Specify the type of waveform with vForce() or vClamp() for voltage
waveform or iForce() or iClamp() for current waveform. Voltage waveform
is default.
For iClamp waveform:
If the waveform values are less than 0.0, iClamp waveform sets the clamp low
test points. The clamp high value follows the setting from the previous
programming. The clamp high value for AVI64 cards is an exception, and RDI
gets the biggest value of the waveform for the clamp high value for AVI64
cards.
If the waveform values are greater than 0.0, iClamp waveform sets the clamp
high test points. The clamp low value follows the setting from the previous
programming. The clamp low value for AVI64 cards is an exception, and RDI
will get the biggest value of the waveform for the clamp low value for AVI64
cards.
For vClamp waveform:
If the waveform values are less than 0.0, vClamp waveform sets the clamp low
test points. The clamp high value is set to the biggest value of the waveform
for all card types.
If the waveform values are greater than 0.0, vClamp waveform sets the clamp
high test points. The clamp low value is set to the biggest value of the
waveform for all card types.
e. Specify a waveform to force with the function waveform().
f. Specify a sampling frequency with FS(), samplePeriod() or
sampleCycle().
g. Execute the setup with execute().

Results

rdi.dc().addWaveform()
Adds one or more waveforms in an execute() operation.
This function supports digital cards and DC Scale cards (PMU and DPS operating
modes).
It can work together with vForce(), iForce(), iClamp(), and vClamp() actions. In
addition, iMeas(), vMeas() or viMeas() can be used to the force or clamp actions.
measWait() can be used to the measurement as well: force waveform() +
addWaveform() + iMeas()/vMeas()/viMeas() + measWait().
The waveform() plus repeat() can be taken as the first waveform group.
Note  Do not support force addWaveform() parallel in one execute().
anaWaveform vClampWave ("vClampWave");
vClampWave.definition(TM::RAMP).direction(TM::NEG)
          .samples(100).periods(1).min(-25 V).max(-1 V);
rdi.dc().pin("AVI_01").iForce(1 mA)
                      .iForceRange(10 mA)
                      .vClamp(-10, 10)
                      .vForceRange(30 V)
                      .execute();
RDI_BEGIN();
  rdi.dc().pin("AVI_01").vClamp()
                        .waveform(vClampWave)
                        .FS(1 kHz)
                        .execute();
  rdi.wait(1 ms);
RDI_END();
rdi.dc().pin("AVI_01").disconnect().execute();

Procedure
1. Specify the port to set up with port().
It is optional for DC Scale pins and it is a must setup for PPMU and board ADC with
the trigger mode.
2. Create a test with the class dc().
3. Specify pins to do the capture with pin().
4. (optional) Specify a force action with iForce() or vForce().
5. Use vMeas() to capture the voltage waveform and use iMeas() to capture the
current wavefrom. By default, vMeas() is used.
6. Specify the number of samples to capture with samples().
7. Specify a sampling frequency with FS(), sampleCycle() or samplePeriod().
8. (For PPMU and board ADC) Specify a capture mode with capMode(). It can be
either trigger mode or vector mode.
9. (For PPMU) Specify an instrument to get the value with valueMode(). When it is
used together with samples(), the default mode is TA::BADC.
10. Execute the setup with the function execute().

Results
The DC resource is set up as a digitizer.
Note  When PPMU is used as AWG, its default relay action is the same as a normal
PPMU measurement:
Parameter Description

TA::ppmuRly_onPPMU_offACDC.
rly_after The relay actions after a PPMU measurement. The default value is TA::ppmuRly_NO. If not
specified, the relay will not be changed after the measurement.
You can use relay() to change the relay actions. See rdi.dc().relay().

Application notes
Replacing average() with measFilter() on AVI64 and FVI16 pins
The average() function for AVI64 and FVI16 pins utilizes hardware based averaging
for calculating the average of multiple consecutive samples on board. Using the
average() function limits the effective maximum sample frequency to
1 MHz / Number of averaged samples.
The average() function may be replaced by the measFilter() function to avoid
this limitation. The digital low-pass measure filter behaves like a simple RC filter.
Therefore, not only the signal settling time but also the measure filter settling time
must be considered when programming the delay time of the measurement by
function rdi.dc().measWait().

Topic 151327

This function is only for the DC Scale AVI64 card and the DC Scale FVI16 card.
The function can be used only in the pattern‑based mode.
Two measurement events (one is for the voltage measurement, and the other is for the
current measurement) are inserted into the related SmartRDI pattern. The maximum
sample rate is therefore defined by the required time for 64 vectors. The sample values
are taken from the continuous stream of voltage measurement samples and current
measurement samples that are simultaneously provided by the digital closed loop
control of AVI64 and FVI16 channels.
The function must always be programmed in combination with function
rdi.dc().samples() and the related functions for setting the sample rate: rdi.dc().FS(),
rdi.dc().sampleCycle(), or rdi.dc().samplePeriod().
Using the viMeas() function in combination with rdi.dc().average() is supported but the
following issues must be observed:
Without averaging, the time difference between the two measurement is defined by
the time for transferring the 32 vectors and for capturing the value for the second
measurement event from the continuous stream of data. The delay will be about 1
μs for a pattern sequencer frequency higher than 32 MHz.
With averaging enabled, the two measurements are pulled apart by the time
required for averaging if this exceeds the time for transferring the 32 vectors of the
second measurement event.
The maximum sample rate is not only defined by the required time for 2 * 32
vectors but also by the time required for averaging as far as it exceeds the time for
the 32 vectors per measurement event.
The measured values can be retrieved by three functions returning the results as an
array of type ARRAY_D:
Function rdi.id().getWaveform() returns both the voltage measurement values and
the current measurement values in one array. The size of the array is twice the
number of samples that has been set by function rdi.dc().samples(): Even elements
[0, 2, 4, ...] are the voltage measurement values; odd elements [1, 3, 5, ...] are the
current measurement values.

The two functions rdi.id().getCurrentWaveform() and rdi.id().getVoltageWaveform()
return the current measurement values or the voltage measurement values in a
single array. The size of the array corresponds to the number of samples that has
been set by function rdi.dc().samples().

SmartRDI: DC test setup
SmartRDI supports DC tests with PPMU, BADC, SPMU, MS-DPS/GPDPS, and DC Scale
pins on V93000.
To do static DC tests, use the code‑based mode. To do dynamic DC tests, use the
pattern‑based mode.
Pattern-based commands only trigger actions that you have specified. Although it is
rare, there are some pattern‑based commands that do not follow this rule, for
example, commands for TMU connections.
Code-based commands can contain default settings if the related parameters have
not been specified. The default settings are applied in each separate command
(.execute()). For examples,
Topic 141501

Recommendations:
If you are not to use default values for parameters used for connecting pins,
specify all the relevant parameters in code‑based commands.
Use code‑based commands only for connection or disconnection of pins and
put all other commands inside an RDI_BEGIN/RDI_END block.
If you need to execute setups or measurements in code‑based commands,
specify all relevant parameters in each .execute().
Set RDI_INFO_LEVEL = 1 or 3 and then verify the execution events of
code‑based commands in the UI_Report log; or check the HW-Monitor.
Note  In a command as rdi.dc().pin(A)...pin(B)...execute():
If pin A and pin B are the same type, for example, both are DC Scale pin or
digital channel, pin A and pin B will act in parallel.
If pin A and pin B are not the same type, for example, pin A is a DC Scale pin
and pin B is a digital channel pin, pin A and pin B will act in serial order.

Setting up Board ADC with SmartRDI
SmartRDI provides the class dc() and related functions to measure the voltage of a
digital pin directly with board ADC.
The code‑based mode is supported on all Pin Scale and Smart Scale cards.
The pattern‑based mode is only supported on Smart Scale cards.
If measurements are done on more than one pin sharing the same board ADC, the
measurements will be done serially in the pattern.
Note  When serial measurements are being done on multiple pins that share the
same board ADC, SmartRDI adds a default setting time between consecutive
measurements that is long enough waiting for a single measurement done. For more
information, see MSET timing of digital pins.
CAUTION In the high impedance mode, the board ADC may generate a spike
when the DC relay of a digital bin is being closed. To avoid the spike occurrence,
discharge the board ADC or force a voltage before the next measurement.
Note  If the BADC is shared over sites, make sure to set Site Match = OFF in the
related test suite.

Application notes
Replacing average() with measFilter() on AVI64 and FVI16 pins
The average() function for AVI64 and FVI16 pins utilizes hardware based averaging
for calculating the average of multiple consecutive samples on board. Using the
average() function limits the effective maximum sample frequency to
1 MHz / Number of averaged samples.
The average() function may be replaced by the measFilter() function to avoid
this limitation. The digital low-pass measure filter behaves like a simple RC filter.
Therefore, not only the signal settling time but also the measure filter settling time
must be considered when programming the delay time of the measurement by
function rdi.dc().measWait().
For more information, refer to application note Measure filter settling time.

LAST measurements
Each channel of a DC Scale FVI16 card features five ADCs for voltage measurements,
current measurements, voltage drop measurements on the force line and on the return
line and battery level measurements at the on-board energy storage. The ADCs are
always triggered simultaneously but only the measured value that is defined by the
individual measurement command is transferred from the front-end to the test
processor and can be uploaded later.
For pattern‑based measurements, additional APIs or parameters that are named "…
LAST ..." provide the functionality to transfer and upload the measured values of all five
ADCs without initiating a new trigger. The values of the last synchronous measurement
of the five ADC are therefore available until the next measurement is triggered.
Averaging of LAST measurements:
If average is used for the primary measurement, then the "… LAST ..." measurements
will also return an averaged value.
Voltage and current measurements are performed every 1 us.
Battery level and force/return drop measurements are performed every 5 us. These
measurements will return a value every 1 us; however, the value is refreshed only
once every 5 us.

Measurements and relay settings
The measurement functions rdi.dc().iMeas() and rdi.dc().vMeas() are supported for both
the code‑based mode and the pattern‑based mode. Controlling the relays differs for the
two modes:
Code-based mode: Functions rdi.dc().iForce() or rdi.dc().vForce() are to be used to
connect a DC Scale pin in the PMU operating mode. Three more issues are to be
considered in this mode:
The pin remains connected until the function rdi.dc().disconnect() is executed
for the pin.
The first code‑based measurement must be separated from the initial
rdi.dc().iForce() or rdi.dc().vForce() that connects the pin or the pin will be
disconnected immediately after the measurement: The initial force function and
the code‑based measurement must be placed in separate RDI command lines,
each terminated with function rdi.execute().
Code-based measurements and the force functions can be combined in one
RDI command line if the pin is already connected.

Application notes
Replacing average() with measFilter() on AVI64 and FVI16 pins
The average() function for AVI64 and FVI16 pins utilizes hardware based averaging
for calculating the average of multiple consecutive samples on board. Using the
average() function limits the effective maximum sample frequency to
1 MHz / Number of averaged samples.
The average() function may be replaced by the measFilter() function to avoid
this limitation. The digital low-pass measure filter behaves like a simple RC filter.
Therefore, not only the signal settling time but also the measure filter settling time
must be considered when programming the delay time of the measurement by
function rdi.dc().measWait().
For more information, refer to application note Measure filter settling time.

Supported only by AVI64.

Supported by AVI64 and FVI16.
This is the default comparator for AVI64.

TA::COMP_HS_TERM Terminated high-speed voltage comparator. The input signal is terminated to

The channel must be set to a high impedance mode before this mode is used. For
more information see the note below.
Supported only by AVI64.
TA::COMP_HS_DIFFERENTIAL High-speed differential voltage comparator: 100 Ω termination to the adjacent
channel in combination with differential compare.
Supported only by AVI64.
Both channels must be set to a high impedance mode before this mode is used. For
more information see the note below.
The high-speed differential voltage comparator supports hardwired combinations of
channels. For more information refer to AVI64 channel group and differential
compare assignment.
Note  The affected channels must be set to a high impedance mode if the
terminated high-speed voltage comparator (TA::COMP_HS_TERM) or the high-speed
differential voltage comparator (TA::COMP_HS_DIFFERENTIAL) are used.
Ensure that the affected channels are set to the TA::HIZ measurement mode or to the
TA::HIZ_COHERENT connection state using function rdi.dc().connectState() before the
comparator is set to TA::COMP_HS_TERM or TA::COMP_HS_DIFFERENTIAL. Ensure that a
non-terminated comparator has been selected before a voltage or current forcing
connection state is selected.
Violating these rules will result in an unregulated state of the channel.

Available options of parameter: FVI16_connectionState
Option Description
TA::FORCE_SENSE_LINK Closes the internal force to sense (FS) link.
The internal FS link can be used to provide temporarily a stable force to sense
connection for the short time while the setup of external relays is changed.
For more information, refer to FVI16 internal force to sense (FS) link.
The internal FS link can be set in code based mode and in pattern‑based
mode. The function rdi.dc().forceSenseLink() is to be used in pattern based
mode.
The internal force to sense (FS) link is automatically opened and the sense
connection to the DUT is restored at the end of the RDI block or whenever a
pattern on an FVI16 channel ends. This is to prevent from erroneous
measurements with closed internal FS link.
When closing the internal force to sense (FS) link, the high-sense and low-
sense output relays are opened automatically . These relays will remain open
until the internal FS link opened.

(FS) link.
TA::FORCE_SENSE_LINK_KEEP Closes the internal force to sense (FS) link and deactivates the automatic
opening of the FS link after pattern execution: The FS link remains closed at

Closes or opens the internal force to sense (FS) link of a DC Scale FVI16 pin. The internal
FS link connects the HF# line to the HS# line and the LF# line to the LS# line.
This member function is supported only for the DC Scale FVI16 card in PMU operating
mode.
The function can be used only in the pattern‑based mode.
In code‑based mode, the function rdi.dc().connectState() with the parameter set to
TA::FORCE_SENSE_LINK is to be used.
The internal FS link can be used to provide temporarily a stable force to sense
connection for the short time while the setup of external relays is changed. For more
information, refer to FVI16 internal force to sense (FS) link.
CAUTION Use the internal force to sense (FS) link with caution. Improper use of
internal FS link may lead to incorrect measurements or other unwanted behavior:
The force and return drop measurements and monitoring of the maximum force
and return drop will not work while the internal FS link is closed.
With closed internal FS link, all voltage measurements are referenced to the
internal connection. The voltage drop on the force and return line to the DUT
cannot be compensated or monitored in this case and the measured voltage is
wrong.

Sense output relays open with internal FS link closed
When closing the internal force to sense (FS) link, the high-sense and low-sense
output relays are opened automatically. These relays will remain open until the
internal FS link opened.

The internal force to sense (FS) link is automatically opened and the sense
connection to the DUT is restored at the end of the RDI block or whenever a pattern
on an FVI16 channel ends. This is to prevent from erroneous measurements with
closed internal FS link.

with caution: The single step execution will cause that the internal FS link is

behavior can be disabled only in code‑based mode using function

Overlapped switching, caused by improper switching sequences, may result in

AVI64 and FVI16 pins:
The function can be used in the code‑based mode and in the pattern‑based mode.
The pin must not be disconnected for changing the current force range.
In pattern‑based mode, the function can be used both for pins in PMU operating

Range programming sequence (AVI64 and FVI16 only)
DC Scale AVI64 and DC Scale FVI16 pins can change the force or clamp range in
connected mode. The programmed force or clamp value must always match to the
selected range. Violating this rule may lead to a range overflow warning.
The behavior of SmartRDI differs for the code‑based mode and the pattern‑based
mode:
Code-based mode:
The programmed sequence is always defined and applied as complete setup. The
test processor of AVI64 and FVI16 pins will automatically select the correct
sequence to avoid range overflow warnings. No special sequence must be
considered in code‑based mode.
Pattern-based mode:
The programmed value and the range that are defined within the same RDI
command (rdi()...execute()) are set by separate patterns of the automatically
created pattern burst. Regardless of the programmed sequence within the RDI
command, SmartRDI always executes first the pattern that sets the range, followed
by the pattern that sets the value.
For the pattern‑based mode, we therefore recommend carefully checking the
sequence for changing the force value, the clamp value, or the related range of an
AVI64 or FVI16 pin. For the correct sequence, the settings must be programmed in
separate RDI commands.
The correct sequence depends on the currently set range and the new force or
clamp value to be set:
The force or clamp value of an AVI64 or FVI16 pin is to be increased:
1. The new range that matches to the new force or clamp value must be
programmed first and must be applied using function rdi.execute().
2. The new force or clamp value can be set now using a new RDI command.
The range of an AVI64 or FVI16 pin is to be decreased:
1. The new force or clamp value that matches to the new range must be
programmed first and must be applied using function rdi.execute().
2. The new range can be set now using a new RDI command.
Both steps of the sequence are to be programmed in separate RDI commands (
rdi()...execute()). Using separate RDI commands ensures that the patterns are
started in the programmed order.

AVI64 and FVI16 do not have different force and measurement ranges.
Thus using iForceRange() and iMeasRange() within one SmartRDI command that
is terminated by rdi.execute() will not result in different ranges, but the current

LAST measurements
Each channel of a DC Scale FVI16 card features five ADCs for voltage measurements,
current measurements, voltage drop measurements on the force line and on the return
line and battery level measurements at the on-board energy storage. The ADCs are
always triggered simultaneously but only the measured value that is defined by the
individual measurement command is transferred from the front-end to the test
processor and can be uploaded later.
For pattern‑based measurements, additional APIs or parameters that are named "…
LAST ..." provide the functionality to transfer and upload the measured values of all five
ADCs without initiating a new trigger. The values of the last synchronous measurement
of the five ADC are therefore available until the next measurement is triggered.
Averaging of LAST measurements:
If average is used for the primary measurement, then the "… LAST ..." measurements
will also return an averaged value.
Voltage and current measurements are performed every 1 us.
Battery level and force/return drop measurements are performed every 5 us. These
measurements will return a value every 1 us; however, the value is refreshed only
once every 5 us.

rdi.dc().loadCap()
Sets the load capacitance in Farad (F).
Topic 149349

Supported only by the DC Scale AVI64 card, the DC Scale DPS128/DPS64 cards, and the
DC Scale FVI16 card.
The function can be used only for the PMU operating mode.
The load capacitance of the DUT or on the DUT board has an effect on the dynamic
behavior of a DPS channel. The function is used to adapt the dynamic behavior of the
channel to the load capacitance.
Some rules must be respected when changing the load capacitance. The rules are
different for the supported DC Scale cards:
AVI64:
The programmed analog load capacitance value is used to adapt the dynamic
behavior of a pin to the load capacitance.
The default value for the load capacitance is 0.0 µF.
The load capacitance can be set with connected or disconnected channel.
The function can be used in code‑based mode and in pattern‑based mode.
Function loadCap() can be used in combination with all other functions.
DPS128 / DPS64:
DPS128 allows for cap-less operation that is defined as working with some
bypass capacitor network = 10 nF.
The cap-less mode is enabled if the load capacitance is set to 0.0 µF by this API.
The cap-less mode is disabled and up to 470 µF per channel are supported if
the load capacitance is set to any value > 0.0 µF.
The reset value for the load capacitance is 1.0 µF: The cap-less mode is
disabled and a load capacitance of up to 470 µF per channel is supported.
Default value if this API is omitted: The last programmed value is kept until it is
(in disconnected state) explicitly programmed or the system is reset. This
applies also if another setup is applied or the channel is disconnected and
reconnected again.
The pin must be disconnected to set the load capacitance.
The function can be used only in the code‑based mode.
Function loadCap() can be used in combination with other functions that
connect the channel.
The set load capacitance must be maintained in all following code‑based
commands until the pin is disconnected. With cap-less mode already enabled

Application notes
Replacing average() with measFilter() on AVI64 and FVI16 pins
The average() function for AVI64 and FVI16 pins utilizes hardware based averaging
for calculating the average of multiple consecutive samples on board. Using the
average() function limits the effective maximum sample frequency to
1 MHz / Number of averaged samples.
The average() function may be replaced by the measFilter() function to avoid
this limitation. The digital low-pass measure filter behaves like a simple RC filter.
Therefore, not only the signal settling time but also the measure filter settling time
must be considered when programming the delay time of the measurement by
function rdi.dc().measWait().
For more information, refer to application note Measure filter settling time.
Measure filter settling time
The programmable digital low-pass measure filters for all ADCs behave like simple
RC filters. A short settling time is to be applied or some samples are to be ignored to
settle to an acceptable difference to the input signal.
The required settling time of the filter or the number of samples to be ignored
depends on the accepted maximum relative error and the filter settings. The
supported DC Scale cards show a slightly different behavior:
AVI64: Refer to the related application notes in topics Measure voltages or
Measure currents of the AVI64 programming overview.
FVI16: Refer to the related application notes in topics Measure voltages or in
Measure currents of the FVI16 programming overview.

Function not

The PMU on an AVI64 pin is selected as active unit.
This is the default state.

TA::HiSpeed Selects the high-speed voltage AWG mode of the PMU.
The digital closed loop control is disabled for this mode. Changes of the force value are
coherent to the vectors of the digital pattern. The DUT is to be connected via the force pin P#
or via the sense pin PS#.
The Kelvin connection scheme and the Sense only connection scheme are supported for this
mode and can be set by the rdi.dc().connectState() API. We recommend using the sense only
connection scheme for minimized capacitive load of the signal path.
Note: Programming a clamp current for the high-speed voltage AWG is not supported. The
high-speed voltage AWG features no programmable clamp current but the DC Scale voltage
and current limits can be used to limit the current in several discrete steps.
TA::HiCurrent Selects the floating high-current unit as active unit.
The unit is shared by groups of eight channels. The differential voltmeter is the mandatory
instrument for measuring voltages. The floating high-current unit is always to be connected in
the Kelvin connection scheme. The definition of a reference pin is required by function
rdi.dc().refPin() if the unit should to be connected in floating mode.
TA::HiRes Selects the high-resolution voltage AWG as active unit.
The unit is shared by groups of eight channels. The PMU ADC is the default voltage measure
instrument in this mode. The differential voltmeter can be selected as optional voltage measure
instrument.
The high-resolution voltage AWG is always to be connected in the Kelvin connection scheme.
Note: Programming a clamp current for the high-resolution voltage AWG is not supported. The
output current of the high-resolution voltage AWG is limited to a fixed value of about 20 mA.
TA::PMU Starting from SmartRDI 7.5.2, you can use this option to directly set the operating mode to

AVI64 pins:
The function can be used in the code‑based mode and in the pattern‑based mode.
The pin must not be disconnected for changing the current force range.
In pattern‑based mode, the function can be used both for pins in PMU operating
mode and in DPS operating mode.
FVI16 pins:
High-power mode and code‑based mode: The function can be used both for
pins in PMU operating mode and in DPS operating mode. The pin must not be
disconnected for changing the force voltage range.
High-power mode and pattern‑based mode: The function can be used only for
pins in PMU operating mode. The pin must not be disconnected for changing
the force voltage range.
High-voltage mode: The function can be used only in the code‑based mode for
pins in PMU operating mode. FVI16 pins must be disconnected before they are
changed from the high-power mode to the high-voltage mode and vice versa.
For more information, refer to FVI16 force and clamp voltages.
Other DC Scale pins:
The function can be used only in the code‑based mode. It needs to be used with
the function rdi.dc().vForce() or rdi.dc().iForce(). Disconnect the pin before changing
the range.

Range programming sequence (AVI64 and FVI16 only)
DC Scale AVI64 and DC Scale FVI16 pins can change the force or clamp range in
connected mode. The programmed force or clamp value must always match to the
selected range. Violating this rule may lead to a range overflow warning.
The behavior of SmartRDI differs for the code‑based mode and the pattern‑based
mode:
Code-based mode:
The programmed sequence is always defined and applied as complete setup. The
test processor of AVI64 and FVI16 pins will automatically select the correct
sequence to avoid range overflow warnings. No special sequence must be
considered in code‑based mode.
Pattern-based mode:
The programmed value and the range that are defined within the same RDI
command (rdi()...execute()) are set by separate patterns of the automatically
created pattern burst. Regardless of the programmed sequence within the RDI
command, SmartRDI always executes first the pattern that sets the range, followed
by the pattern that sets the value.
For the pattern‑based mode, we therefore recommend carefully checking the
sequence for changing the force value, the clamp value, or the related range of an
AVI64 or FVI16 pin. For the correct sequence, the settings must be programmed in
separate RDI commands.
The correct sequence depends on the currently set range and the new force or
clamp value to be set:
The force or clamp value of an AVI64 or FVI16 pin is to be increased:
1. The new range that matches to the new force or clamp value must be
programmed first and must be applied using function rdi.execute().
2. The new force or clamp value can be set now using a new RDI command.
The range of an AVI64 or FVI16 pin is to be decreased:
1. The new force or clamp value that matches to the new range must be
programmed first and must be applied using function rdi.execute().
2. The new range can be set now using a new RDI command.
Both steps of the sequence are to be programmed in separate RDI commands (
rdi()...execute()). Using separate RDI commands ensures that the patterns are
started in the programmed order.

LAST measurements
Each channel of a DC Scale FVI16 card features five ADCs for voltage measurements,
current measurements, voltage drop measurements on the force line and on the return
line and battery level measurements at the on-board energy storage. The ADCs are
always triggered simultaneously but only the measured value that is defined by the
individual measurement command is transferred from the front-end to the test
processor and can be uploaded later.
For pattern‑based measurements, additional APIs or parameters that are named "…
LAST ..." provide the functionality to transfer and upload the measured values of all five
ADCs without initiating a new trigger. The values of the last synchronous measurement
of the five ADC are therefore available until the next measurement is triggered.
Averaging of LAST measurements:
If average is used for the primary measurement, then the "… LAST ..." measurements
will also return an averaged value.
Voltage and current measurements are performed every 1 us.
Battery level and force/return drop measurements are performed every 5 us. These
measurements will return a value every 1 us; however, the value is refreshed only
once every 5 us.

SmartRDI: Digital capture test setup
SmartRDI provides the class digCap() and the following functions to set up digital
capture tests.
pin(), initDiscard(), samples(), capMode(), label(), copyLabel,
addVecRange(), interSkip(), bitPerWord(), rdi.execute(), getVecVar(),
getVector(), getVectorBit(), enPassFail(), burstUpload(), vecVarOnly(),
and format().
Currently only the selective mode capturing is supported by SmartRDI.
SmartRDI can create the digital capture label and the vector variable according to the x-
mode and the capture waveform index in the wavetable.
Topic 141504

SmartRDI supports both serial transfer mode and parallel transfer mode.
For the serial transfer mode, a vector variable is created for each capture pin with 32 bits
per word by default. You can only get the vectors of one pin at a time. In the parallel
mode, a vector variable is created for all pins in the capture with one sample per word.
You need to get the vectors of all the pins at a time.
The bits in the captured samples are assembled in the order of MSB (Most Significant
Bit) to LSB (Least Significant Bit) from the first pin to the last.
For the usage of hidden upload, refer to using hidden upload with SmartRDI.
See X-mode handling in digCap with SmartRDI for an example of digCap x-mode
handling and some attention points.

Introduced in SmartRDI 2.1.0
Using Immediate Upload in SmartRDI
SmartRDI supports the SmarTest 7.4.2 new feature - "Immediate upload" mode for
captured data upload.
Immediate upload
It is introduced to fill the gap in using the hidden upload technology of the SmartCalc
framework.
Topic 343521

Immediate upload versus hidden upload
To achieve best throughput and multisite efficiency with V93000, the SmartCalc
framework is used.
SmartCalc enables performing data upload and calculation while another test is being
executed. This technology is called hidden upload. Hidden upload has two drawbacks:
Binning is delayed (late binning)
Another test with suitable execution time must be in place
Besides, hidden upload also has a known limitation that it becomes inapplicable when:
No other tests are available to hide uploads
Late binning is not an option
The immediate upload technology fills this gap for digital capture tests by immediate
upload and calculation which allows to upload result chunks of a started and running
capture test and do calculations on this result chunk while test is running.
Immediate Upload is introduced with SmarTest 7.4.2 for digital capture tests. Supported
Smart-Scale cards include PS1600, PS9G, Pin Scale SL, and AVI64 (in Digital I/O
operating mode).
The following diagram shows the general structure of immediate upload.
Immediate upload only supports the digCap() class with two API functions:
rdi.digCapImmediateUpload() and rdi.id().getImmediateVector().

In short, with a capability of uploading data and hiding calculation during the capture
running, immediate upload improves tests performance especially when a huge amount
of data are generated at a low capture speed.
Examples
Using immediate upload for data upload only
In the example below, digCapImmediateUpload() is used alone to upload digital
capture data immediately while the test is running. The upload of the captured data
referenced by "resultId" is started while the burst is executed.
Using immediate upload for data upload and result calculation
In the example below, digCapImmediateUpload() is used together with
getImmediateVector() to upload digital capture data as well as hide result calculation
while the test is running.
rdi.digCapImmediateUpload("resultId"); 
RDI_BEGIN();
   rdi.digCap("resultId").samples(...)...execute();
   ...
RDI_END(); // Raw Result upload within pattern run
rdi.id("resultId").getVector();

__data__.text:
SmartRDI: DUT board connections control by
Routing Tools
The Routing Tools feature native multisite handling, user friendly table based
configuration editors and a unified programming interface for controlling utility lines
and MUX card switches.
The Routing Tools are a combination of the Routing Tools editors and the rdi.route()
class of SmartRDI. The rdi.route() class, which is described in this section, applies the
data, that are defined using the Routing Tools editors, to the controlled hardware.
The Routing Tools provide additionally the following features:
Static and pattern‑based control of utility lines
Support of the setup memory of PMUX cards
Definition of switch behavior and wait time handling
Automatic generation and download of control pattern supported by SmartRDI
The Routing Tools consist of the combination of the Routing Tools editors as shown
above and corresponding APIs of SmartRDI. that are described in this section.

Global Setup editor
The Global Setup editor of the Routing Tools enables you defining, loading and
saving the XML file that contains all configuration data or a master file that
references the required XML files. In addition, the number of sites and other
configuration parameters for utility lines and the IC bus of the MUX cards are to be
defined in this editor.
Utility Lines Control editor
The Utility Lines Control editor of the Routing Tools enables you selecting static or
sequencer‑controlled utility Lines and defining the digital control pins for the
sequencer‑controlled utility lines.
Utility Lines Config editor
The assignment from utility tester channels to utility pins is defined in the Utility
Lines Config editor.
PMUX Control editor
The control group and the digital pins for controlling the IC bus of MUX cards are
defined in the PMUX Control editor of the Routing Tools.
PMUX Config editor
The channels of the PMUX cards are assigned to PMUX pin names in the PMUX
Config editor.
State Setup editor
The routing states to be applied can be defined in the State Setup editor. The user
defined routing states hold the switch states for all utility pins and PMUX pins and
represent one of the Routing Tools main functionality.
Debugger
The Debugger allows you interactively loading and applying stored routing states or
modifying the active routing state of the hardware.

__data__.text:
"File Path" and "Browse" button
Field File Path defines the setup file to be loaded or saved. The file can be an XML file
or a master file that references the required XML files. You can type in the complete file
path manually or you can click the Browse... button and select a folder and the file in
the Select Routing Tools Setup File dialog:
In the Select Routing Tools Setup File dialog
select the file and
close the dialog by clicking the OK button.
The Routing Tools support text files or compressed files. The file name extension defines
whether the file is saved as text file or as compressed file. The extension must be added
manually:
An uncompressed text file must end with ".xml".
A compressed XML file must end with ".zip" or ".rtz".
A master file file must end with ".mfh".
Note that compressed ".zip" or ".rtz" setup files cannot be used in combination with a
".mfh" master file.
We recommend, using folder testmethod in the root directory of the test program for
storing the setup file.

__data__.text:
"Load" button
The XML configuration file, which is defined in field File Path, can be loaded by clicking
the Load button and saved by clicking he Save button of the V93000 Toolbar.
Some hints for loading and saving the XML configuration file:
Loading a configuration file will overwrite all unsaved changes in all Routing tools
editors. Overwriting unsaved changes must be confirmed in a new dialog box that
will pop up if unsaved changes are detected.
Saving a configuration file will overwrite an already existing file however, a series of
up to 10 recent file revisions will be kept on hard disk.
The extension of the file ".zip" or "rtz" defines that the XML file is saved as
compressed file.
Saving the contents of all Routing Tools editor tabs can also be done by pressing
the CTRL + S key combination simultaneously.
For creating a new XML configuration file, enter a valid file path and click the Save
button. The new file will contain all settings that already have been entered in all
Routing Tools editors. For an example refer to section "Example" below.
"Reset" button
Clicking the reset button clears all settings and initializes the Routing Tools editors. The
cleared data includes the selected XML file including the file path, all configuration data
and all routing states.
"Site Count"
The number of configured sites is to be defined in field Site Number. The number of
configured sites must be the same as defined by the Define Site Number dialog of
SmarTest. For more information refer to Defining additional test sites.

__data__.text:
"Utility Lines"
The type of utility pogo blocks is to be defined in field Pogo block size.... The selection
field supports 16 lines per block for the 2-row block or 32 lines per block for the 4-row
pogo block. The selected value must be the same as defined as parameter
utility_lines_per_pogoblock in the Technology file for a device.
Note  The 4-row utility pogo block is mandatory if MUX cards are used.
Field SPI Max. Clock Rate defines the maximum clock for sequencer‑controlled utility
lines. This value will be used by SmartRDI to generate the correct padding in order to
slow down SPI clock speed with fast periods.
A floating-point value like "1.0 MHz" may be entered. The maximum clock frequency
must not exceed "10 MHz". All frequencies are rounded to nearest 1 kHz. For more
information refer to Sequencer-controlled utility lines.
"Failing-site Handling" table
The behavior of MUX card switches for failing sites can be defined in table row Failing-
Site Handling:
Default: The routing state for failing sites is to be selected from a drop-down list.
Content Assist will show the valid options in a drop-down list if you press Control +
Space. The valid options are defined as follows:
keep: The state of the switches for failing sites is not changed.
defined: An already defined routing state is applied for failing sites.
State (defined): This value defines the routing state that is to be applied for failing
sites if Default has been set to defined. Any routing state that already has been
defined in the State Setup editor can be selected.
The settings defined in this section are applied by rdi.route().handleDisabledSites() in the
special test suite bin_disconnect. For compatibility, the legacy option continue can be
emulated by omitting the call of this function. Note: The legacy state continue will not
work for static utility lines, as these are disabled automatically by SmarTest after their
corresponding site failed.
"PMUX"
Field I2C Max. Clock Rate defines the clock frequency for the I2C bus of the MUX cards.

__data__.text:
Control Table
The Control Table shows all installed utility pogo blocks and defines the control mode
of the utility lines per utility block.
Mode defines the control mode for the utility pogo blocks. Content Assist will show the
valid options in a drop-down list if you press Control + Space. The valid options are
defined as follows:
static: The utility lines are controlled only by software.
Note  SmartRDI will control a utility block in code‑based mode if the static
control mode has been selected. This will increase the test time and add more
variance to the overall timing of a test suite.
dynamic: The utility lines are controlled by the pattern sequencer. The Control
Group must be selected and the required digital pins must be defined in the Pin
Config Table. The serial interface for sequencer‑controlled utility lines must be
wired on the DUT board for each utility block that is set to this control mode. For
more information refer to Sequencer-controlled utility lines - Serial interface.
unused: The utility block is not used. SmartRDI will not consider unused utility
blocks when creating the pattern for utility lines. Pins belonging to unused utility
blocks cannot be entered in the Routing Tools - Utility Lines Config editor.
Note  We recommend controlling only dynamic utility lines by the Routing Tools:
Static utility lines cannot be controlled by the pattern of a RDI_BEGIN() ... RDI_END()
block. SmartRDI's power, however, lies in pattern‑based control of tester resources.
Control Group selects a group of control pins for each utility block that is set to the
dynamic control mode. A control group in this context means a group of digital pins
controlling the serial interface of a utility pogo block. Some rules must be respected
when assigning the utility blocks to control blocks:
The utility blocks of one control group must be contiguous.
The utility block with the lowest number becomes the master.
The serial interface pins on the master must be connected to the digital pins that
you will be using to supply the control signals.
The corresponding pins on the slave utility blocks must be left floating on the DUT
board.
For more information refer to Sequencer-controlled utility lines - Serial interface and
Sequencer-controlled utility lines - Ganging (cascading) pogo blocks.

__data__.text:
The MUX cards are controlled via a two-wire serial IC interface. Two digital pins are
required for generating the control signal SDA and SCL of the IC interface.
Each of the used MUX cards must be assigned to one control group that consists of a
digital pin for the SDA signal and another digital pin for the SCL signal of the IC
interface. A control group may generate the IC signals for a single MUX card, a group
of MUX cards or all available MUX cards. For more information refer to PMUX01
programming interface.
The PMUX Control editor provides the Control Table and the Pin Config Table.

__data__.text:
Control Table
The predefined contents of the Card and POGO Locations columns reflect the standard
configuration of the MUX cards:
Card: The value defines the maximum 16 MUX cards that can be installed between
the pogo block groups in the central area of the DUT interface.
POGO Locations: The two columns show the pogo block numbers of the related
MUX card. For more information refer to MUX cards pogo block numbering. The
combination of the pogo block number and the pogo pin as shown in PMUX01
pogo pin assignment defines a tester channel that is used in columns Site # of the
PMUX Config editor.
The Module ID and Control Group columns reflect the configuration and wiring on the
DUT board:
Module ID: This column defines the card specific address. The address must be
hardwired on the DUT board. For more information refer to PMUX01 addressing
scheme and to PMUX01 control pins.
Note  The routing tools require that unique addresses are assigned for all
installed PMUX cards even if the MUX cards are assigned to different control
groups.
The values in this column are filled in automatically, but can be changed and can
also be deleted by simply clicking a cell and pressing the Delete key.
Control Group: A control group consists of two digital pins that generate the SDA
signal and the SCL signal of the IC interface. A control group may generate the IC
signals for a single MUX card, a group of MUX cards or all available MUX cards.

__data__.text:
Pin Config Table
The Pin Config Table defines the digital pins to be used for generating the IC signals
of the control groups. Two digital pins are to be assigned for each control group. The
assigned digital pins must already be defined in the Digital Pins editor. The selected
digital pins must be unique for all control groups.
Control Group: The control group to which the digital pins should be assigned. A
new control group is created automatically if it is assigned in column Control
Group of the Control Table.
SDA: This pin controls the serial data line of the IC bus. The signal is pulled up to
the high level by a pull-up resistor on the DUT board. The signal is pulled down to
the low level for generating the serial data stream by the sending device and is
pulled down to the low level by the receiving device for generating an
acknowledgment signal after all data have been received successfully.
SCL: This signal is the serial clock of the IC bus. The line is pulled up to the high
level by a pull-up resistor on the DUT board. Only the assigned digital pin, which
represents a part of the IC bus master, pulls this pin to the low level for generating
a clock signal.
For more information regarding the SDA and SCL signals refer to PMUX01
programming interface and to PMUX01 control pins.
Note  We strongly recommend using shared digital pins for all sites: In the Digital
Pins editor, each of the digital control pins is to be assigned to the same channel for
all sites. Sharing the control pins for all sites will minimize the required effort for
handling disabled sites.If you do not use shared digital pins, you will lose the control
of some PMUX cards when some sites have been disabled.
Control pins that are not available in the loaded pin configuration are highlighted light-
yellow. Control pins that are in conflict with other control pins and can therefore not be
used are highlighted red.
