Topic 146692

Definition of keywords in the RDI_Configure file
The following tables list all of the applicable keywords and their definitions.
Alarm handling for DCVI
Keyword Description
ALARM_FAIL_WARNING Disable alarm warnings when alarm fails.
If you set ALARM_FAIL_WARNING = TRUE, SmartRDI
throws an warning message when the alarm fails, for
example, Test Suite:: SuiteName, Burst Label::
BurstName, Alarm Pin ("PinName") failed!.
If you set ALARM_FAIL_WARNING = FALSE, SmartRDI
throws NOTHING. You can use rdi.id().getAlarmPassFail()
to retrieve the alarm result.
The default value is TRUE.
ALARM_HANDLING_DCVI_ENABLE Enable the alarm handling for DCVI. The option is TRUE or
FALSE.
The default value is FALSE.
ALARM_HANDLING_DCVI_SETUP_FILE Specify a path that directs to an alarm setup file which
contains the limit setups for handling alarms for DCVI.
A file path relative to the root path of the loaded device is
to be specified.
You can use different alarm handling setups for different
testflows since you can use RDI_CONFIGURE_FILE to
specify a RDI_Configure file for each testflow. See Testflow
variable RDI_CONFIGURE_FILE above.
For more information on Alarm handling, see SmartRDI: Alarm handling for DCVI.
Default pin status
Keyword Description
DEFAULT_STATUS_INDEX Specify the default physical index for the pins, separated by
commas.
DEFAULT_STATUS_PIN Specify the pins to set the default status, separated by
commas.
For more information about default pin status, see Changing the default pin status
with SmartRDI.
For debugging

Keyword Description
ENABLE_RDI_INFO_LOG_FILE Specify TRUE or FALSE to enable or disable saving the
RDI_INFO_LEVEL report (shown in the UI report window) to
a log file. When enabled, the RDI_INFO_LEVEL_x.log file
is generated in the device/testmethod folder.
The default value is FALSE.
REPORT_RESULT_IN_SINGLE_MODE Specify TRUE or FALSE to enable or disable the
measurement result in the SINGLE mode to be shown in
the UI report window. When it is enabled, if the command
is with a result ID, the results for DC and functional tests
will show in the window once the commands are being
executed one by one.
If not specified, FALSE is used by default.
For production
Keyword Description
SETUP_UPTODATE Specify this option to TRUE to have NO * (asterisk) in the
setup tool; or to FALSE to have * in the setup tool.
The default value is FALSE.
SETUP_UPTODATE = TRUE # Have NO * in the setup
tool.
SETUP_UPTODATE = FALSE # Have * in the setup tool
as before.
Only setups programmed in SmartRDI code are handled.
MS-DPS HW trigger setup
Keyword Description
DPS_TRIGGER_PIN Specify the external trigger pin for the current measurement
with MS-DPS or GPDPS.
DPS_VBUMP_PIN Specify the trigger pin for forcing voltage with the vbump
function of GPDPS or MS-DPS.
For more information about MS-DPS HW trigger setup, see Setting up MS-
DPS/GPDPS with SmartRDI.
Offline Result Emulation (ORE) setup

Keyword Description
ENABLE_ORE Specify TRUE or FALSE to enable or disable Offline Result
Emulation.
The default value is FALSE.
In online mode, to automatically disable ORE, you can set
this keyword as ENABLE_ORE = TRUE_OFFLINE. With this
setting, ORE works only for offline.
If the ORE feature is enabled for online, SmartRDI delivers
an error message for reminder.
Settings of ENABLE_ORE
RDI_Configure option Offline mode Online mode
ENABLE_ORE = TRUE Enable ORE Enable ORE
ENABLE_ORE = FALSE Disable ORE Disable ORE
ENABLE_ORE = TRUE_OFFLINE Enable ORE Disable ORE
ORE_FILE Specify a path to which the ORE file is saved. The ORE file
path can be specified as an absolute path or a relative
path. A relative path is based on the current test device's
root directory. For example, ./myORE.xml is
current_device_folder/myORE.xml.
ORE_FOLDER Specify a path for the
rdi_ore_template_by_user_code.xml and ARRAY
data files.
If it is not set, the
rdi_ore_template_by_user_code.xml and ARRAY
result data files will be created in the device path.
The path can be an absolute path or a relative path. A
relative path is based on the current test device directory.
It can be ./ORE which directs to the
current_device_folder/ORE/ folder.
You can also use it inside any XML file as the keyword to
represent the result file path that has been specified in
the RDI_Configure file.
ORE_TEMPLATE_BY_USER_CODE Enable the generation of a specific ORE template file
based on user code.
The default value is FALSE.
If it is set to TRUE, a template file named
rdi_ore_template_by_user_code.xml will be
generated during the first run of the test program and
the file is stored in the current device path.
ORE_TEMPLATE_DATA_FILE_SIZE_THRESHOLD Set a threshold for the result size of your ORE template.
If the generated result size is less than the threshold
value, the result will be inserted to the .xml file.

If the generated result size is greater than or equal to the
threshold value, the result will be inserted to a .txt file
which is located in the same folder as the
rdi_ore_template_by_user_code.xml file is; the

Keyword Description

For more information about ORE setup, see Offline Result Emulation in SmartRDI.
Pass or fail per label
Keyword Description
PER_LABEL_FUNC_RESULT_MODE Define how to return the pass/fail results per label in
functional tests: ERMP or FLBL.
If not specified, ERMP is used by default.
PER_LABEL_FUNC_RESULT_NO_BREAK_VEC Specify TRUE or FALSE to enable or disable the
SmartScale cards (PS1600, PS9GPSSL) feature of
retrieving per label Pass/Fail results without inserting
break vectors (BFLM mode).
If not specified, FALSE is used by default.
When this option is set to TRUE, no break vectors are
inserted between labels of a burst.
Note  This mode requires a pattern length not
less than eight cycles for patterns inside an
RDI_BEGIN()/RDI_END() block, because in BFLM
mode, each pattern in the burst must generate
eight or more cycles (see Compression factor for
overview Error Map). So when this mode is enabled,
a specified pattern length less than eight cycles is
ignored and all patterns generated by SmartRDI
have at least eight cycles. There are exceptions, for
example vecLength() of the smartVec() class,
where SmartRDI reports an error for a user setting
with insufficient pattern length, rather than
ignoring the setting. User labels less than eight
cycles cause an error as well.
For more information about pass/fail per label, see Pass/Fail per label without break
vectors.
PMUX setup

Keyword Description
PMUX_CTRL_MAX_SPEED Specify a maximum speed of SmartRDI doing padding in the
control pattern.
The value range is from 0.1e6 to 1e6.
PMUX_X_CTRL Define two digital pins for controlling an MUX card.
The first value defines the SDA pin and the second value
defines the SCL pin.
For example,
PMUX_1_CTRL = pinA,pinB
PMUX_2_CTRL = pinC,pinD
See Digital pins controlling MUX cards with SmartRDI for
more information.
For more information about PMUX setup, see SmartRDI: Power MUX setup.
Note  The settings mentioned in this section are used for the legacy way of
controlling MUX cards by digital pins.
For SmarTest version 7.4.4 and higher, we recommend using the more
comfortable and powerful Routing Tools and the rdi.route() class.

Keyword Description
PPMU_DEFAULT_RELAY Specify PPMU_ON or NO to set the default relay action.
If not specified, PPMU_ON is used by default.
PPMU_DEFAULT_VALUE_MODE Specify SA or BADC to set the default voltage or current
measurement mode.
If not specified, BADC is used by default.
FAST_PPMU_LEVEL_TRANSFER Specify TRUE or FALSE to enable DC fast download. This
reduces the time required for Changing the parameter
value at runtime with SmartRDI in high-site-count
applications.
If not specified, FALSE is used by default.
For more information, refer to PPMU fast transfer mode of
SmartRDI.
For more information about PPMU setup, see DC test with digital channels.
Result upload

Keyword Description
ANA_RESULT_RDI_SEMI_PARALLEL_IMPROVE Specify TRUE (default) or FALSE to enable/disable the
enhancement of result upload time in a semi-parallel
setup, by restricting the pin configuration. See
SEMI_PARALLEL_CONFIG () for more information about
SEMI_PARALLEL_CONFIG setups.
DC_BURST_SITE_UPLOAD Specify TRUE or FALSE to allow or disallow uploading DC
results over sites in one burst (a SmarTest 7.4.3 new
feature).
In the Technology File, a setting is required to use this
capability:
If not specified, FALSE is used by default.
Note  Burst site upload does not support hidden
upload.
DIGCAP_ADAPTIVE_RESULT_SIZE Specify the result size to be retrieved when the number of
samples actually captured is less than the expected
number.
The default value is FALSE.
When this flag is set to TRUE, the result array contains the
values of actually-captured samples. For example, if the
expected sample number is 32 and the sample number
actually captured is 20, the result is an array with 20
values.
When this flag is set to FALSE, the result array contains
the values of actually-captured samples plus some "-999"
to match the length of the expected number. For
example, if the expected sample number is 32 and the
actually-captured sample number is 20, the result is an
array with 20 values plus 12 of "-999".
DIGCAP_BURST_SITE_UPLOAD Specify TRUE or FALSE to allow or disallow uploading
digital capture results over sites in one burst (a SmarTest
7.4.2.1 new feature).
This configuration is set to FALSE by default.
With this feature enabled, the SmartRDI classes
digCap() and smartVec() with
readMode(TA::DIGCAP) upload the digital capture
results over sites in one firmware query.
For DIGCAP_BURST_SITE_UPLOAD = TRUE, the maximum
sample number is 8192.
This global setting can be overwritten by a local setting
specified with rdi.digCapBurstSiteUpload().
Note  Burst site upload does not support hidden
upload.
For more information about upload setup, see Controlling burst site upload.

Keyword Description

route state is applied successfully to PMUX01 Power MUX
cards. The Acknowledge bit of the I C bus is checked when a
new state is applied by rdi.route().applyState() or when a

If not specified, FALSE is used by default.

Setup naming
Keyword Description
ANALOG_SET_NAME_MD5 Specify this option to be TRUE to append an MD5 checksum
at the end of all analog set names. The MD5 checksum
briefly shows the content in the burst. If the same analog set
has already existed, the analog set will not be generated
again.
If not specified, FALSE is used by default.
See Setting and retrieving the setup name with SmartRDI.
BURST_NAME_MD5 Specify this option to be TRUE to append an MD5 checksum
at the end of all the burst names. The MD5 checksum briefly
shows the content in the burst. If the same burst name has
already existed, the burst will not be generated again.
Before SmartRDI 2.4.5, when BURST_NAME_MD5 is set to
FALSE, the burst pattern does not contain MD5 information
and SmartRDI always deletes and regenerates the burst
pattern during the first run.

In SmartRDI 2.4.5, when BURST_NAME_MD5 is set to FALSE,
SmartRDI saves the MD5 checksum into the burst pattern (by
leveraging the new LBUD firmware command in SmarTest
7.4.2) and judges whether the burst pattern needs to be
regenerated during the first run.
If not specified, FALSE is used by default.
See Postfix in burst pattern names.
2
smartVec setup

Keyword Description
DEFAULT_EMAP_LOCATION Provide a global option to set an error map location:
TP indicates an error map location in the test
processor memory of the channel.
RAM indicates that the error map is located in the
vector memory of the channel.
If not specified, the default error map location is RAM, which
is the vector memory, because this location provides a
higher upload speed.
In case the vector memory is insufficient for the test, the
location switches to TP, which is the test processor memory.
Note that the RAM location is related to the "result area"
configuration in the technology file of SmarTest.
For information about the error map size, refer to Pin Scale
1600 error map size.
See also rdi.emapLocation().
Note  TP is the default value before SmartRDI 2.4.5.
RAM is the default value since SmartRDI 2.4.5.
DEFAULT_SMV_READ_MODE Specify a central selection of SmartVec read mode for the
whole test program: EMAP or DIGCAP.
If not specified, the default read mode is DIGCAP.
SMV_DIGCAP_AUTO_BURSTUPLOAD Specify TRUE or FALSE to enable or disable automatic burst
of upload.
The default value is TRUE.
Using burstUpload for data read by SmartVec in the digital
capture mode can significantly decrease test time. By
default, all SmartVec's digital capture data on a certain pin
in one RDI_BEGIN()/RDI_END() block are uploaded as
one burst, and the burstUpload() function set in the code
is ignored.
The only exception is a combination of digCap() and
smartVec() readings in the same
RDI_BEGIN()/RDI_END() block on the same pin. As the
digCap class supports different capture modes (par, ser,
bitPerWord), the smartVec burstUpload will be split into
segments between the digCap commands.
SMV_VEC_MEM_TYPE Specify the memory location to put generated smartVec
patterns: SHMEM or SM.
If not specified, SM is used by default.
USER_NAMED_LABEL_CONTENT_CHECK Specify TRUE or FALSE to enable or disable whether to
check label content when you set a label name.
The default value is TRUE.

The default value is TRUE.
Based on the new LBUD firmware command in SmarTest
7.4.2, this option provides a capability of performing a

Keyword Description
content check on labels set by one of the following
commands or command combinations:
A labelName() function in the smartVec() class
A burstLabel(TA::MD5_OFF) function in the
smartVec() class
A label().copyLabel(false) function
combination in the dc(), digCap(), tmu(), or
smartVec() class
With this feature enabled, the SmartRDI verifies
whether the label content corresponds to the code in
the RDI_BEGIN()/RDI_END() block and reports an
error when a difference is detected.
VEC_EDIT_MODE Specify this option to select one of vector edit modes: VECD
or VEC_TRANSFER_TASK (VTT) for smartVec() class actions.
If not specified, VECD is used by default.
See rdi.smartVec().vecEditMode() for more information.
SMV_IGNORE_COMMENT Globally enable or disable the suppression of smartVec
comments generated in pattern.
By default, SMV_IGNORE_COMMENT = FALSE. If you set
SMV_IGNORE_COMMENT = TRUE, all smartVec comments
inserted by rdi.smartVec().comment() will be ignored in
pattern generation.
For more information about vector setup, see SmartRDI: Vector and protocol
programming.
SMC execution
Keyword Description
DISABLE_SMC_EXEC_GLOBAL Specify TRUE or FALSE to globally allow or disallow SMC
execution.
This configuration is set to FALSE by default.
DISABLE_SMC_EXEC_SHORT_BURST Specify TRUE or FALSE to enable or disable the SMC
execution mode for short bursts (<1 ms) automatically.
This configuration is set to FALSE by default.
For more information about SMC execution, see SmartRDI functions controlling
SmartCalc (SMC).
Utility line setup

Keyword Description
UTIL_BLOCK Specify the utility block to be controlled by the pattern.
Use commas to separate groups; do not use commas to
define ganged (cascaded) groups. Use the "-" character to
link the ganged pogo block numbers.
For example,
UTIL_BLOCK = 123, 4, 5, 6 // blocks 1, 2, and
3 are ganged
UTIL_BLOCK = 1-2-3, 4, 5, 6 // blocks 1, 2,
and 3 are ganged
UTIL_CTRL_MAX_SPEED Specify the target utility control maximum speed in case a
lower speed is required such as 2e6 or 3e6. The valid value
range is from 1e6 to 10e6.
If not specified, 10e6 is used by default.
UTIL_DYN_MASK_INACTIVE_SITE Specify TRUE or FALSE to keep or not keep the states
(mask) of the utility bits of inactive sites. FALSE indicates
that utility pins at inactive sites will STILL be changed by
pattern; TRUE indicates that utility pins at inactive sites will
NOT be changed by pattern.
The default value is FALSE.
This configuration option is implemented based on the
utility mask capability in SmarTest 7.4.2 for the
sequencer‑controlled utility lines.
UTIL_DYN_MASK_UNSPECIFIED_PIN Specify TRUE or FALSE to keep or not keep the states
(mask) of unspecified utility bins in a command. FALSE
indicates that unspecified utility pins in the same control
pattern will be set to OFF; TRUE indicates that unspecified
utility pins in the same control pattern will KEEP their
states.
If not specified, the default value is TRUE.
This configuration option is implemented based on the
utility mask capability in SmarTest 7.4.2 for the
sequencer‑controlled utility lines. To keep the
compatibility with old test programs, use FALSE for this
keyword.
UTIL_FRAM Specify the serial frame enable pins for the
sequencer‑controlled utility lines.
UTIL_PADDING_RPTV_FLAT Define a threshold which decides to use a flat pattern or
RPTV pattern for padding.
The default value is 16.

The default value is 16.
If the padding value is less than and equal to the
threshold, a flat pattern is used and repeated to append to
the burst. If the padding value is greater than this
threshold, RPTV is used to insert vectors.
UTIL_SCLK Specify the serial clock pins for the sequencer‑controlled
utility lines.

Keyword Description
UTIL_SINP Specify the serial data in pins for the sequencer‑controlled
utility lines.
UTIL_SOUT Specify the serial data out pins for the
sequencer‑controlled utility lines.
For more information about utility line setup, see SmartRDI: Utility lines control.
Others

Keyword Description
ALLOW_SAME_RESULT_ID_ACROSS_RDI_BLOCK Specify TRUE or FALSE to allow or disallow using the same
result ID in different RDI_BEGIN()/RDI_END() blocks
inside the same test suite. It only supports a serial
execution of a shmoo test suite when the value is set to
TRUE.
The default value is FALSE.
FLUSH_COMPATIBLE Specify TRUE to keep FLUSH() original functionality. If set
to FALSE, a new FLUSH() command can be used to have
better throughput, such as FLUSH(TM::FLUSH_ANALOG),
FLUSH(TM::FLUSH_UTIL) or
FLUSH(TM::FLUSH_PRIMARY) API in different cases
instead of the FLUSH() API.
The default value is TRUE.
INACTIVE_SITE_AUTO_MASK If this option is set to TRUE, all inactive sites will execute a
dummy label and remain in a hold state; other sites will
still execute their normal labels.
The default state is FALSE.
PURE_GENERATION_MODE Specify TRUE or FALSE to enable or disable pure
generation mode.
When this option is set to TRUE, SmartRDI generates
setups (pattern, burst, dc event, analog set and so on)
only and skips pattern execution and results upload.
Note  All rdi...getXXX() calls such as
getVector(), getReadBit(), getWaveform()
return dummy results. The size of result arrays = 0.
Enabling this option reduces the execution time of a
"clean" 1st run by omitting the Viasco bind. It also allows
to generate setups (pattern or analog set) and save them
for later use or reuse in another program.
If not specified, FALSE is used by default.
SMT_PROTECT_MODE Specify TRUE to allow RDI using VEC_TRANSFER_TASK
(VTT) instead of VECD to modify generated patterns in
SmarTest protected mode operating environment.
If not specified, the default value is FALSE.
TMU_SHARE_PIN_RESULT_OVER_SITES The default value is FALSE.
By default, a shared pin's TMU measurement result is
available only on the last site.
If the flag is set to TRUE, the shared pin's TMU
measurement result can be available on all the sites.

Note  TMU_SHARE_PIN_RESULT_OVER_SITES =
TRUE does not work when SMC (hidden upload) is
enabled.
VEC_MODE_SAMPLING_WAIT Specify MSET or PATTERN to set up a wait time for PPMU
or BADC digital sampling in the VEC mode. The default

Keyword Description
choice is PATTERN which uses the wait time being defined
in the measurement set as the sampling period. Use the
PATTERN mode for inserting some waiting time in the
pattern to set up a deterministic sampling rate.
Note  The RDI_Configure file and the settings that can be set in the file are all
optional. You can omit any settings in the file or even omit the complete file if no
settings are required.

SmartRDI: RF test setup
SmartRDI provides the class rfs() and rfm() to set up the RF test.
In the pattern‑based mode, all analog events in one RDI_BEGIN()/RDI_END() block
will be generated in one analog set. The labels for hardware triggers will be generated
and bursted.
For RF CW stimulus, FE and Source triggers will be generated only.
For RF Mod stimulus, AWG trigger will be generated after FE and Source triggers.
For RF measurement, DGT trigger will be generated after FE and Source triggers.
Topic 141816

The hardware trigger pin needs to be specified in the RDI_configure file as shown
below. If some trigger pins are not needed, leave them blank. If a trigger pin is shared
by several RF cards, put the same trigger pin name.
In the first run of a test method, SmartRDI checks whether the trigger pins specified in
the RDI_configure file are defined in the pin configuration file. If the trigger is not
available, a warning message will be shown.
RF stimulus and RF measurement can be put in one RDI_BEGIN()/RDI_END() block
and a "Measure with Sim" will be generated in the RF definition.
RF setup and analog setup can be put in one RDI_BEGIN()/RDI_END() block and an
analog set with both the RF definition and the analog setup will be generated.
In the single execution mode, each analog event will generate its own analog set. The
software trigger is used in the execution. The RF stimulus will be kept on for the
debugging purpose.
Before an execution, SmartRDI automatically connects relevant pins and also enables
relevant trigger pins. After the execution, SmartRDI runs the disconnect command but
does not proceed with FLUSH at once. The purpose of no immediate FLUSH after a
disconnect is not to repeatedly disconnect and connect HW channel if the subsequent
RDI_BEGIN/RDI_END block has the same pins that need to be connected and
disconnected.

SmartRDI: Testflow level burst and
concurrency tests
SmartRDI naturally supports burst and concurrency in test suite level when different test
blocks are in an RDI_BEGIN and RDI_END block.
In 2.4.0, SmartRDI provides two classes CCTestMethod_SYNC and CCTestMethod_ISR to
support burst and concurrency in testflow level with multiple tests that are located in
different test suites.
From 2.5.1, SmartRDI provides postBurst() to fully support concurrent test framework.
Related information
Concurrent test framework
Functional changes
Introduced in SmartRDI 2.4.0
SmartRDI 2.5.1: Enhanced with a new function postBurst().
CCTestMethod_SYNC
SmartRDI has a CCTestMethod_SYNC class to achieve multiport burst-based concurrent
tests in the testflow level. The class is an extension to the existing concurrent test
framework (CCF) in SmarTest 7.

Hidden upload in CCTestMethod_SYNC
If you use the hidden upload feature in your CCTestMethod_SYNC code, follow these
rules:
Put rdi.hiddenUpload() as the first command in burstRun().
Configure the hidden upload per test suite.
All result IDs in burstRun() must be unique in testflow.
To make result IDs unique in testflow, you can use the test suite as a key.

Migration from TestMethod to CCTestMethod_ISR
In the CCTestMethod_ISR code, you do not need to use RDI_INIT(). The
RDI_CCT_BEGIN() and RDI_CCT_END() block is equal to an RDI_BEGIN() and RDI_END
block.
Test suite parameters

SmartRDI: TMU test setup Topic 149090

The SmartRDI TMU class provides APIs for TMU measurements based on Smart Scale
digital cards and selected DC Scale cards.
Supported DC Scale cards are DC Scale AVI64 card, the DC Scale FVI16 card, and the DC
Scale PVI8 card. Besides these cards, the TMU class also supports digital cards. See
Supported hardware for all the digital cards that SmartRDI supports.
With this class, you can:
Create an independent TMU measurement.
Insert a TMU measurement into an existing pattern.
Note that the default sequencer timeout is 900 s (see SQTO, SQTO? - (SeQuencer
TimeOut)).
When using PS1600 TMU to perform ABSOLUTE timing measurements, pay attention to
the following points:
Phenomena: Arming may not work properly and a shift in measurement values or
other undefined behaviors may occur.
Solution: When the arming of the TMU starts to be executed on pattern, the input
signal through the TMU channel must always have the same level. This means that
if the input signal is 0, the next one must be zero too; the same to the input signal
1.
Workaround: Add a vector to the end of the pattern to ensure that the input signal
returns to its initial state. In this way, the input remains the same state when the
next arming starts.
Relative timing measurements are not affected by this phenomena.
After the TMU execution, you must set a wait time long enough for the TMU to capture
all samples.

This function is for the DC Scale AVI64 card and the DC Scale FVI16 card. The function
can be used only in the pattern‑based mode.
Note  The function can be programmed only in pattern‑based mode although it
controls the static setup of the comparator hysteresis. The set-up of the hysteresis is
applied before the pattern burst of the RDI_BEGIN() ... RDI_END() block is started.
SmartRDI applies only the first definition of the hysteresis if the function is called
more than once for the same pin within one RDI block. The following hysteresis
definitions in the same RDI block and for the same pin are ignored.
Syntax
Parameters
Parameter Description
compHyst_highRes Defines the hysteresis in percent of the range for a high-resolution comparator. High-
resolution comparators are selected by function rdi.tmu().compMode() and defined by
keywords TA::COMP_LS or TA::COMP_LS_DIFFVM.
For information on how to set the comparator threshold of AVI64 pins refer to paragraph
Hysteresis and sample frequency of the high resolution comparators in AVI64 time
measurement unit (TMU).
For information on how to set the comparator threshold of FVI16 pins refer to paragraph
Hysteresis and sample frequency of the high resolution comparators in FVI16 time
measurement unit (TMU).
compHyst_highSpeed Enables or disables the fixed hysteresis for a high-speed comparator. High-speed
comparators are selected by function rdi.tmu().compMode() and defined by keywords
TA::COMP_HS, TA::COMP_HS_TERM, or TA::COMP_HS_DIFFERENTIAL.
The hysteresis is to be programmed as follows:
0.0 V: The fixed hysteresis is switched off
> 0.0 V: The fixed hysteresis is switched on
The high-speed voltage comparator of AVI64 pins and FVI16 pins feature a fixed hysteresis of
about 20 mV.
Return Value
A reference to the tmuBase object.

comparatorMode Defines the comparator mode to be set.
Available options of parameter: comparatorMode
Option Description
TA::COMP_LS High-resolution voltage or current comparator.
The compare mode voltage or current is defined by the measurement mode that is
set by rdi.tmu().vth() or rdi.tmu().ith().
This is the default comparator for an AVI64 or FVI16 pin in the PMU operating mode.
TA::COMP_HS High-speed voltage comparator.
TA::COMP_LS_DIFFVM High-resolution voltage comparator of the differential voltmeter.
This value is only for AVI64.
TA::COMP_HS_TERM Terminated high-speed voltage comparator. The input signal is terminated to
ground via 50 Ω.
The channel must be set to a high impedance mode before this mode is used. For
more information see the note below.
This value is only for AVI64.
TA::COMP_HS_DIFFERENTIAL High-speed differential voltage comparator: 100 Ω termination to the adjacent
channel in combination with differential compare.
Both channels must be set to a high impedance mode before this mode is used. For
more information see the note below.
The high-speed differential voltage comparator supports hardwired combinations of
channels. For more information refer to AVI64 channel group and differential
compare assignment.
This value is only for AVI64.

This function is for the DC Scale AVI64 card and the DC Scale FVI16 card. The function
can be used only in the pattern‑based mode.
The current compare mode is provided by the high-resolution current measure circuitry
and comparators of the AVI64 or FVI16 pins. Using this mode requires that the pin is
forcing voltage or current with an active digital closed loop control.
Supported combination with the connection state and the active unit:
AVI64:
The current compare mode is not supported if the connection state has been set to
TA::HIZ or TA::HIZ_COHERENT or if the active unit has been set to TA::HiSpeed
or TA::HiRes.
FVI16:
The current compare mode is not supported if the connection state has been set to
TA::HIZ.
SmartRDI selects automatically the high-resolution (LS) comparator for the current
compare mode. Other comparators are not supported in this mode.
Note  The function combines the static code‑based selection of the compare mode,
the initial set-up of the thresholds, and the dynamic pattern‑based modification of
the thresholds. The selection of the compare mode and the initial thresholds are
applied before the pattern burst of the RDI_BEGIN() ... RDI_END() block is started.
SmartRDI applies only the first selection of the compare mode if the function is
called more than once for the same pin within one RDI block. The following compare
mode selections in the same RDI block and for the same pin are ignored but the
thresholds are always applied by dynamic DC events.

rdi.tmu().postDisconnect()
Controls the disconnect status of the TMU after a functional test.
This function is only for the DC Scale AVI64 card, the DC Scale FVI16 card, and the DC
Scale PVI8 card.
The function can be used only in the code‑based mode.
The supported DC Scale cards show a different behavior:
AVI64
The TMUs of AVI64 pins feature no separate TMU relays and are therefore always
connected if the PS# pin is connected to the DUT. The function is to be used only to
control the comparator that has been selected by rdi.tmu().compMode(): The
comparator will be reset to the default state TA::COMP_LS with disconnect status set
to true.
We recommend resetting the comparator always to the default state if the
terminated comparators TA::COMP_HS_TERM or TA::COMP_HS_DIFFERENTIAL have
been selected for the TMU measurement.
FVI16
The function controls the relay connections that have been defined by function
rdi.tmu().compMode(). postDisconnect() must open the FVI16 TMU input relay if
the high-speed voltage comparator has been selected. If one of the high-resolution
comparators for both voltage and current has been selected, postDisconnect()
must do nothing.
PVI8
The function controls the relay connections that have been defined by function
rdi.tmu().connectMode(). By default, PVI8 TMU relays will be opened after a
functional test.
We strongly recommended disconnecting the PVI8 TMU after the measurement. This
will minimize the bias current of the related DUT pins, prevent the TMU from being
damaged by voltages that exceed the maximum operating range and avoids
potential issues with the PVI8 surge tracker.

selected, postDisconnect(true) must do nothing.
DC Scale PVI8 cards: The TMU relays will be opened after.

Digital pins and DC Scale pins in the Digital I/O operating
mode
If used with digital applications and pins, the vth() function sets the threshold voltage
for the TMU of the digital pins.
Note  If the vth() command is skipped for a digital pin TMU the VOH setting in the
level set will be used as TMU threshold.
DC Scale pins in the PMU operating mode
This function is only for the DC Scale AVI64 card, the DC Scale FVI16 card, and the DC
Scale PVI8 card.
The TMUs of DC Scale pins in the PMU operating mode combine both the high
comparator and the low comparator output to the TMU input of the test processor to
support single shot rise time and fall time measurements. Two different thresholds must
be defined for these pins.
Note  The function combines the static code‑based selection of the compare mode,
the initial set-up of the thresholds, and the dynamic pattern‑based modification of
the thresholds. The selection of the compare mode and the initial thresholds are
applied before the pattern burst of the RDI_BEGIN() ... RDI_END() block is started.
SmartRDI applies only the first selection of the compare mode if the function is
called more than once for the same pin within one RDI block. The following compare
mode selections in the same RDI block and for the same pin are ignored but the
thresholds are always applied by dynamic DC events.

SmartRDI: Utility lines control
SmartRDI provides the class util() to control the utility lines in code‑based mode and
in pattern‑based mode.
The following member functions are provided:
rdi.util().pin(),
rdi.util().setOn(),
rdi.util().setOff() and
rdi.execute().
In the code‑based mode, the setup will be executed directly.
In pattern‑based mode, sequencer‑controlled utility lines are controlled via a serial
interface available on each utility pogo block. The required signals are provided by
patterns of digital pins connected to the serial interface. The patterns for the digital pins
will be generated by SmartRDI. The control pins need to be specified in the Utility line
setup section of the RDI_Configure file as shown below. The following configuration
means utility block 1 and 2 are cascaded (ganged). A comma is used to align the utility
block and the digital pins to control the utility block.
After the code is executed, you can check the relay status in the hardware view.
Topic 141837
11  UTIL_BLOCK UTIL_BLOCK ==    1212,,33,,44    // or 1-2,3,4// or 1-2,3,4
22  UTIL_FRAM  UTIL_FRAM  ==  FR1  FR1,,FR3FR3,,FR4FR4
33  UTIL_SCLK  UTIL_SCLK  ==  SK1  SK1,,SK3SK3,,SK4SK4
44  UTIL_SINP  UTIL_SINP  ==  SN1  SN1,,SN3SN3,,SN4SN4
55  UTIL_SOUT  UTIL_SOUT  ==  SO1  SO1,,SO3SO3,,SO4SO4

Note  The utility lines a controlled by digital pins connected to the serial interface.
For these digital pins, you need to set up levels, equations, and wavetables as for
normal digital pins.
For more information, refer to the related sections in the example of Sequencer-
controlled utility lines - Setting up.
Note  In SmartRDI, utility lines may be controlled by the rdi.util() class or by
the rdi.route() class of the Routing Tools. In addition, the utility lines may be
controlled by test method APIs, firmware commands or the "Routing Setup Tool".
This may lead to conflicts if the same utility line is controlled by more than one API
or tool.
For SmartRDI we therefore strongly recommend, controlling utility lines either by the
rdi.route() class or by the rdi.util() class. The mixed use of the two APIs or
other test method APIs and tools is not recommended. This recommendation
applies to code‑based programming and to pattern‑based programming.
Code‑based programming for the rdi.route() means that the utility lines are set
to "static" in the "Control table" of the Utility Lines Control editor. Pattern‑based
programming for the rdi.route() means that the utility lines are set to "dynamic"
in the "Utility Lines Control editor".

Two new flags in the RDI_Configure file work together to control the behavior:
UTIL_DYN_MASK_UNSPECIFIED_PIN =TRUE /FALSE
FALSE: Unspecified utility pins in the same control pattern will be set to OFF
(default)
TRUE: Unspecified utility pins in the same control pattern will KEEP their states
UTIL_DYN_MASK_INACTIVE_SITE =TRUE /FALSE
FALSE: Utility pins on inactive sites will STILL be changed by pattern (default)
TRUE: Utility pins on inactive sites will NOT be changed by pattern
Note  UTIL_DYN_MASK_INACTIVE_SITE can be set to TRUE only when
UTIL_DYN_MASK_UNSPECIFIED_PIN is set to TRUE.
Note  The mask feature for the sequencer‑controlled utility lines requires the FPGA
version 0xA2 of the wiring board. The FPGA bundles 4.015 provides the mentioned
version.
In SmartRDI 7.6.0, a wait time can be added to pins in Pin Configuration for
sequencer‑controlled utility pattern. A wait pattern will be generated after relay
switching. If there are multiple pins in one SmartRDI command, SmartRDI chooses the
longest wait time to use.
Note  For existing test programs, this enhancement in SmartRDI 7.6.0 may cause
those test programs with sequencer‑controlled utility failed. To keep compatibility
with these test programs, you can set UTILITY_SETTLING_TIME = FALSE in the
SmartRDI: RDI_Configure file.

The SmartRDI Vector class supports the generation of vector and patterns with simple
commands. It provides an easy way to read digital outputs of a device.

The typical vector and pattern operations you can perform using the smart vector class
are listed below:
3 different data input options for the pattern creation (data block, bit stream, vector
stream).
Automatic handling of the x mode and 1/x mode.
Creation of patterns with structured burst data.
Creation of patterns with a parallel data burst for multiple ports.
Creation of big patterns for a series of pattern creation commands.
Data retrieval is handled in different ways for test time optimization (digital capture
and error map).
The number of upload actions is minimized in case of multiple data retrievals.
The vector generation class provides APIs and commands for different "layers": Vector

Relationship between bits and device cycles
In the pattern generation through the smartVec() class, SmartRDI allows the bit values 0,
1, and 2 specified by some APIs to match with 0, 1, Z or L, H, X device cycles (DVC)
defined in your wavetable.
Topic 351019

Write APIs
For the "write" type of commands, such as rdi.smartVec().writeBit(), bits 0, 1, and 2 in the
specified value are converted to 0, 1, and Z for corresponding with DVCs. That means
SmartRDI always deals with 0, 1, and 2 for "0", "1", and "Z".
The relationship between bits and DVCs for X1 and Xn modes are different:
X1 mode: bit 0 to DVC "0", 1 to "1", and 2 to "Z".
Xn mode: bits 0101 to DVC "0101" and bits 0112 to "011Z".
In the corresponding wavetable, waveform definitions must consecutive, ranging from
"00...0" to "11...1". For example, a wavetable for x8-mode:
If a waveform contains "Z" or "X", like "10Z1", it can have any physical index in the
wavetable.

rdi.smartVec().burstLabel()
Combines multiple smart vector commands into one burst label. The commands are
surrounded by burstLabel().begin()/burstLabel().end().
The usage of burstlabel() converts several single labels to one common label. Thus
the granularity of pass/fail results is limited to the common burstlabel.
Accordingly the commands expectBit(), expectData(), and enPassFail() cannot
be used with an id (smartVec(id)) inside burstlabel().
To insert compare vectors, use writeVec(), fillVec(), and writePat().
This command can also work together with enPassFail() to specify that the burst
label requires pass/fail results. See Example 3.
burstLabel creates a label only with its specified name. Do not use labelName() inside
the burstLabel().begin()/burstLabel().end() block. Using a labelName()
command inside the block can have some side effects, for example, pass/fail retrieval
does not work.
Note  Do not put
rdi.smartVec().burstUpload().begin()/rdi.smartVec().burstUpload().end(
inside an rdi.burstLabel().begin()/rdi.burstLabel().end() block because

rdi.smartVec().insertJmpe()
This function allows inserting vectors as a subroutine called by the JMPE instruction into
a main label or another subroutine.
It works with passNode() and failNode() which define the content for the pass and
the fail branches.
Its behavior in connection with rdi.smartVec().label() is similar to
rdi.smartVec().insertSub().
JSUB and JMPE can get inserted into each other by using level. See Example 2 and
Example 3 at the bottom of this topic.
insertJmpe() can be used with rdi.smartVec().readData() and rdi.smartVec().readBit().
Below are the rules of using readData() and readBit() together with insertJmpe()
in the same execute().
readData() and readBit() cannot be put within a sublabel generated by
insertJmpe() because the JMPE branching is not predictable.
insertJmpe() cannot be inserted into a readData() or readBit() area in the
main pattern.
After the vector invokes a sublabel inserted by insertJmpe(), readData() or
readBit() in the main label cannot be used in the EMAP mode because the cycle
count after JMPE is not fixed. It can only be used in the DIGCAP mode.
Syntax
List of parameters
Parameter Description
vecLine Number of the vector line where you want to insert the subroutine.
level Subroutine level. This refers to the target level at which you want to insert a new subroutine.
The default value is 1, which means the first level subroutine and actually refers to the main pattern. To
insert a subroutine into another subroutine, you should specify a level larger than 1.
Return value
There is no return value.

If you need to use xMode() for specific pins, you must define consecutive waveforms in
the corresponding wavetable. For the write mode, the definition range is from "00...0" to
"11...1". If the waveform contains "Z" or "X", like "10Z1", you can assign any physical
index. For the read mode, the definition range is from "LL...L" to "HH...H". If the
waveform contains "Z" or "X", like "LHXL", you can assign any physical index. For the
SmartRDI-suggested default dvc "." for doing nothing, you must set it to "..." that the
dot length is equal to the Xmode value for the correct Xmode recognition of error map
result.
If you do not specify a parameter in xMode(), the default value is set to 1.
Syntax
List of parameters
Parameter Description
Xmode The number of device cycles in each tester cycle.
Note
The fail count and fail position are about "compare edge" (not tester cycle). So
they supports xMode directly.
The xMode parameter for a pin must be correct, otherwise the result for the pin
will not be correct.
The parameter specified in the function, such as startCyc and cycRange, is
about user cycles (edge), not tester cycles. This setting is critical when xMode is
set to be greater than 1.
For one pin, the xMode must remain the same in different labels in burst;
otherwise the results might be wrong.
Note  For correctly retrieving the results of error map data:
For a specified pin, in one RDI_BEGIN/RDI_END block, its xMode number must
remain the same value, no matter it is for a SmartRDI command or in the user
pattern.
In the wavetable, the length of the device cycle name must align with the
xMode() value. For example, if you set xMode to xMode(2), the dvc must
correspondingly have two letters, such as "LL", "00", "11", "LL". Even the dvc of
the physical index f, which normal value is "."

Even the dvc of
the physical index f, which normal value is "." with SmartRDI, must be ".." for
xMode(2). Otherwise SmarTest cannot recognize the correct xMode value from
pattern.
